title: Quality Control — SQC 1 & SA 220 (CA Final – Audit)
description: CA Final – Auditing and Professional Ethics: application-oriented MCQ bank on the Quality Control chapter, covering SQC 1 (system of quality control at firm level, applicability and definitions, the six elements, leadership responsibilities for quality within the firm, ethical requirements and independence including familiarity threat and seven-year engagement partner rotation for listed entities, acceptance and continuance with client-integrity and capability considerations, withdrawal from an engagement, human resources and engagement partner assignment, engagement performance through review of engagement work and consultation, engagement quality control review, engagement documentation including sixty-day assembly and seven-year retention, monitoring, complaints and allegations, and the Peer Review Board, Quality Review Board and NFRA review mechanisms) and SA 220 (engagement partner responsibilities at the particular audit engagement level, modelled on SQC 1, including leadership, ethical requirements and engagement quality control review duties). Each question is independently usable; case studies are repeated in full in every question of a family.

questions.category: SQC 1 - Objective of the System of Quality Control
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the objective of a system of quality control under SQC 1:
Statement 1: The system is designed to provide reasonable assurance that the firm and its personnel comply with professional standards and with regulatory and legal requirements.
Statement 2: The assurance contemplated by the system is confined to compliance by engagement partners, since staff compliance is tested only engagement-wise under SA 220.
Statement 3: Compliance with regulatory and legal requirements is part of the objective along with compliance with professional standards.
Statement 4: The system is designed to provide absolute assurance that no engagement of the firm will ever be found wanting.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
1, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: SQC 1 requires the firm to establish a system of quality control designed to provide it with reasonable assurance that the firm AND its personnel comply with professional standards and regulatory and legal requirements. Statement 2 is incorrect because the objective expressly extends to the firm and its personnel generally, not merely to engagement partners; the firm-level system cannot be narrowed to partners alone. Statement 4 is incorrect because the standard promises only reasonable assurance, not absolute assurance, so it never guarantees that no deficiency will ever occur. Statement 3 is correct because regulatory and legal requirements stand alongside professional standards in the objective clause; omitting either limb would understate the system's purpose. Statements 1 and 3 together reproduce the complete objective, hence the first option.

questions.category: SQC 1 - Objective of the System of Quality Control
questions.question: A CA firm has established and diligently applies all the elements of a system of quality control under SQC 1. Despite this, on one audit the firm's personnel fail to comply with an applicable legal requirement, and the failure goes unnoticed until after the report is issued. On the wording of the objective of SQC 1, which conclusion is MOST APPROPRIATE?
options: The lapse proves that the firm's system must have excluded the engagement partner and staff, since both are covered by SA 220 alone.

A system designed to provide 'reasonable', not absolute, assurance can still tolerate an isolated human failure; SQC 1 fixes the design objective of the system, not a guarantee of perfection on every engagement.
SQC 1 ceases to apply to a firm once its documented policies are being followed, because compliance then depends on the personnel alone.
The lapse shows that regulatory and legal requirements are outside the system, which covers professional standards only.
questions.explanation: The pivotal wording is 'reasonable assurance': the system must be DESIGNED to provide reasonable assurance that the firm and its personnel comply with professional standards and regulatory and legal requirements, which is a design-and-operation standard, not an absolute guarantee that no breach can ever occur. The second option correctly identifies that an isolated failure does not by itself show the system was outside SQC 1's objective. The first option wrongly relocates personnel to SA 220 only, whereas the firm-level objective expressly covers the firm and its personnel. The third option confuses diligent application with exemption; nothing in SQC 1's applicability suspends the requirement once policies are followed. The fourth option contradicts the objective clause, which names regulatory and legal requirements alongside professional standards.

questions.question:
Match the following:
Column I:
(A) Firm
(B) Engagement Partner
(C) Engagement Team
(D) System of Quality Control
Column II:
(1) All personnel (the engagement partner and staff) performing the engagement
(2) Sole proprietor, partnership, or any entity of chartered accountants
(3) Policies and procedures established by the firm to provide reasonable assurance that the firm and its personnel comply with professional standards and with regulatory and legal requirements
(4) A full-time practicing chartered accountant in the firm who is responsible for the engagement
Select the correct matching:
questions.explanation: SQC 1 defines a firm expansively as a sole proprietor, partnership, or any entity of chartered accountants (A-2); the Engagement Partner specifically as a FULL-TIME practicing CA in the firm who is responsible for the engagement (B-4); the Engagement Team as all personnel, covering the EP and staff, performing the engagement (C-1); and the system of quality control as the structure of policies and procedures designed to give reasonable assurance of compliance by the firm and its personnel with professional standards and regulatory and legal requirements (D-3). The distractor pairings split these definitions across the wrong terms, for instance attaching the full-time condition to the engagement team or the compliance-assurance objective to the term 'firm'. The decisive markers are 'full-time' for the EP and 'all personnel' for the engagement team, while the reasonable-assurance objective clause belongs to the system, not to any person.

questions.category: SQC 1 - Elements of a System of Quality Control
questions.question:
The following situations are drawn from the working records of different CA firms. Match each situation to the element of a system of quality control under SQC 1 that it most directly relates to:
Column I (Situations):
(A) The firm frames criteria for deciding whether to accept a new prospective client.
(B) The partners fix ultimate responsibility for the firm's system of quality control on a named senior partner.
(C) The firm requires that every level of review carried out on an audit file be evidenced by appropriate documentation.
(D) The firm periodically inspects whether its own quality control policies and procedures are being applied.
Column II (Elements):
(1) Leadership responsibilities for quality within the firm
(2) Acceptance and continuance of client relationships and specific engagements
(3) Human resources
(4) Engagement performance (review and documentation)
(5) Monitoring
questions.explanation: Situation (A) is a client-acceptance decision, squarely within element (2), acceptance and continuance of client relationships and specific engagements. Situation (B) concerns where responsibility for quality in the firm is placed, i.e. element (1), leadership responsibilities for quality within the firm, not human resources; human resources deals with the personnel lifecycle rather than the allocation of responsibility for the system itself. Situation (C) pairs review with documentation of engagement work, the parenthetical content of element (5) as listed, engagement performance (review and documentation). Situation (D), the firm's periodic inspection of its own policies and procedures, is the essence of element (6), monitoring. The common trap is swapping engagement performance with monitoring, but internal inspection of the whole system is monitoring, whereas review evidence on a file is engagement performance.

questions.category: SQC 1 - Elements of a System of Quality Control
questions.question: SQC 1 requires the firm's system of quality control to include policies and procedures addressing six named elements. Which one of the following is NOT among those six elements?
options: Ethical requirements
Acceptance and continuance of client relationships and specific engagements
Complaints and allegations
Monitoring
questions.explanation: The six elements listed by SQC 1 are: leadership responsibilities for quality within the firm; ethical requirements; acceptance and continuance of client relationships and specific engagements; human resources; engagement performance (review and documentation); and monitoring. 'Complaints and allegations' is not one of the six named elements in that enumeration, even though complaints and allegations are dealt with elsewhere in the standard's guidance; the candidate must answer from the element list itself, not from what sounds like a plausible quality-control topic. The other three options appear verbatim in the six-element list. The distinction matters because exam questions on the composition of the system test the enumerated elements strictly.

questions.category: SQC 1 - Elements of a System of Quality Control
questions.question:
Consider the following reproductions of the element headings of a system of quality control stated by four firms in their internal manuals:
Statement 1: 'Leadership responsibilities for quality on audits'
Statement 2: 'Acceptance and continuance of client relationships and specific engagements'
Statement 3: 'Engagement performance (review and documentation)'
Statement 4: 'Human resources and peer review of firms'
Which of the above statements are NOT faithful to the element headings listed in SQC 1?
options: 1 and 4 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3 only
3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is unfaithful because SQC 1 words the element as leadership responsibilities for quality WITHIN THE FIRM, a firm-wide concept covering all engagements to which the standard applies, not merely audits; narrowing the heading to audits is a classic misquote. Statement 4 is unfaithful because the element is simply 'Human resources'; peer review of firms is a separate mechanism outside the six-element enumeration, and grafting it onto the heading changes the list. Statements 2 and 3 reproduce the source headings exactly, including the words 'and specific engagements' and the parenthetical '(review and documentation)'. The decisive skill is spotting subtly altered scope words ('within the firm' versus 'on audits') and smuggled-in additions ('and peer review').

questions.category: SQC 1 - Elements of a System of Quality Control
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The first element of a system of quality control in SQC 1 is worded 'Leadership responsibilities for quality within the firm' and not 'leadership responsibilities for quality on audits'.
Reason (R): SQC 1 is applicable to all types of engagements, including related services engagements, and applies to all CA firms, so the leadership element addresses quality across everything the firm does rather than only its audit portfolio.
Which of the following is correct?
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is incorrect.
A is incorrect but R is correct.
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) quotes the element heading accurately: SQC 1 speaks of leadership responsibilities for quality within the firm. Reason (R) states the applicability rule correctly: the standard applies to all types of engagements, including related services engagements, and to all CA firms. R also explains A properly, because the firm-wide wording of the leadership element follows directly from the standard's firm-wide, all-engagements scope; if the element were confined to audits it would leave the firm's review, other assurance and related services work without leadership ownership of quality. The alternative of 'both correct but R does not explain A' fails here precisely because the applicability clause is the reason the leadership wording is firm-level.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the applicability of SQC 1:
Statement 1: SQC 1 is applicable to all types of engagements, including related services engagements.
Statement 2: SQC 1 is applicable only to firms that perform audits of companies; firms performing only reviews and related services are outside it.
Statement 3: A firm for SQC 1 purposes includes a sole proprietor, a partnership, or any entity of chartered accountants, so the applicability does not depend on the form of practice.
Statement 4: A sole proprietorship may omit the mandatory elements of the system of quality control on the ground that its staff strength is negligible.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 4 only
1, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: SQC 1 is expressly applicable to all types of engagements, including related services engagements, which makes Statement 1 correct. Statement 2 is wrong because the standard applies to all CA firms, not just firms auditing companies; restricting it to company audits reads in a limitation the standard does not contain. Statement 3 is correct because the definition of 'firm' covers a sole proprietor, a partnership or any entity of chartered accountants, so the form of practice is irrelevant to applicability. Statement 4 is wrong because the firm's system shall include policies and procedures addressing all six elements; neither the definition of firm nor the applicability clause offers a small-staff exemption from elements of the system.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes the division of labour between SQC 1 and SA 220 as contemplated by SQC 1's applicability section?
options: SQC 1 governs all the firm's engagements while SA 220 has no application to audit work at all.
The firm may elect either SQC 1 or SA 220 for its quality framework depending on the size of its practice.
SQC 1 prescribes firm-level quality control across all types of engagements, while SA 220 prescribes quality management at the level of a particular audit engagement.
SQC 1 governs quality at firm level while SA 220 governs quality at particular audit engagement level, so once a firm applies SQC 1, the firm's individual audit engagements are exempt from SA 220.
questions.explanation: SQC 1's applicability section draws a level-based distinction: SQC 1 deals with quality at the firm level, while SA 220 deals with quality at the level of a particular audit engagement. The third option states this division accurately and without excess. The first and second options distort the relationship by denying SA 220 any role or by treating the two standards as alternatives a firm can choose between; a firm-level system and an engagement-level responsibility are different layers, not substitutes. The fourth option starts with the correct contrast but then fabricates an exemption, which the level-based division does not support: applying the firm-level standard does not disapply the engagement-level one.

questions.question:
Bannerjee and Co. is a newly formed partnership of four chartered accountants in Kolkata. In its first year, the firm received the statutory audit of a listed company, two tax audit engagements, several related services engagements such as assistance in the preparation of financial information and book-keeping support, and a limited review engagement. Discussing SQC 1 compliance at a partners' meeting, the managing partner Mr. Ashok Das said: 'SQC 1 concerns only our audit and review work; our routine accounting and tax assignments lie outside it. Further, we are a new firm; unless the volume of assurance work crosses some threshold, we need not have any system of quality control. Quality is a subject for the individual engagement partner, so our firm as a whole must comply with SA 220 and not SQC 1.'

Which of the following is the MOST APPROPRIATE response to Mr. Das's first statement regarding the coverage of the firm's work?
options: He is right; SQC 1 applies to audits and limited reviews only, and all other engagements are outside the firm's system.
He is wrong solely because SQC 1 applies to all CA firms irrespective of the mix of engagements each firm performs.
He is wrong; SQC 1 is applicable to all types of engagements, including related services engagements, so those assignments also fall within the firm's system of quality control.
He is right regarding related services engagements but wrong regarding tax audit engagements.
questions.explanation: The applicability section states that SQC 1 is applicable to all types of engagements, including related services engagements. The decisive response must therefore match the reason to the complaint: Das's error is about the scope of ENGAGEMENTS, and the third option supplies exactly that answer. The second option cites a correct rule (applicability to all CA firms) on the wrong facts, which does not rebut an argument about engagement types. The first option wrongly restricts the system to assurance work, and the fourth creates a false split within non-audit assignments; the standard's 'all types of engagements' wording gives no basis for excluding any category of the firm's work, tax audits or related services alike.

questions.question:
Bannerjee and Co. is a newly formed partnership of four chartered accountants in Kolkata. In its first year, the firm received the statutory audit of a listed company, two tax audit engagements, several related services engagements such as assistance in the preparation of financial information and book-keeping support, and a limited review engagement. Discussing SQC 1 compliance at a partners' meeting, the managing partner Mr. Ashok Das said: 'SQC 1 concerns only our audit and review work; our routine accounting and tax assignments lie outside it. Further, we are a new firm; unless the volume of assurance work crosses some threshold, we need not have any system of quality control. Quality is a subject for the individual engagement partner, so our firm as a whole must comply with SA 220 and not SQC 1.'

Consider the following statements on Mr. Das's three assertions:
Statement 1: His threshold argument fails because SQC 1 applies to all CA firms and the requirement to establish a system is not conditioned on any volume of assurance work stated in the standard.
Statement 2: His scope argument fails because SQC 1 is applicable to all types of engagements, including related services engagements.
Statement 3: His SA 220 argument confuses levels of responsibility: SQC 1 deals with quality at firm level while SA 220 deals with quality at a particular audit engagement level.
Statement 4: The system he is reluctant to establish must, by its objective, provide reasonable assurance that the firm and its personnel comply with professional standards and with regulatory and legal requirements.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1 and 3 only
2 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
questions.explanation: All four statements are correct applications of SQC 1's opening provisions to Das's assertions. Statement 1 answers the threshold claim: the standard applies to all CA firms with no volume trigger in its applicability section. Statement 2 answers the engagement-mix claim, since all types of engagements including related services engagements are covered. Statement 3 answers the SA 220 claim by locating each standard at its own level, firm versus particular audit engagement. Statement 4 correctly describes what the system Das resists is supposed to achieve, reasonable assurance of compliance by the firm and its personnel with professional standards and regulatory and legal requirements; the objectives clause names both limbs, so no statement understating them could be accepted.

questions.question:
Bannerjee and Co. is a newly formed partnership of four chartered accountants in Kolkata. In its first year, the firm received the statutory audit of a listed company, two tax audit engagements, several related services engagements such as assistance in the preparation of financial information and book-keeping support, and a limited review engagement. Discussing SQC 1 compliance at a partners' meeting, the managing partner Mr. Ashok Das said: 'SQC 1 concerns only our audit and review work; our routine accounting and tax assignments lie outside it. Further, we are a new firm; unless the volume of assurance work crosses some threshold, we need not have any system of quality control. Quality is a subject for the individual engagement partner, so our firm as a whole must comply with SA 220 and not SQC 1.'

WHAT CHANGES IF, instead of a four-partner firm, Bannerjee and Co. were a sole proprietorship with one full-time employee but the same engagement mix? Which conclusion correctly reflects the changed position?
options: SQC 1 would continue to apply in full, since a 'firm' expressly includes a sole proprietor and the standard applies to all CA firms and to all types of engagements.
SQC 1 would cease to apply, because a system of quality control can be established only over a partnership of chartered accountants.
SQC 1 would apply only to the audit and limited review work, since related services by a sole proprietor are supervised personally.
SQC 1 would apply only to the elements of ethical requirements and monitoring, the remaining elements presupposing multiple partners.
questions.explanation: The defined term 'firm' in SQC 1 covers a sole proprietor, a partnership, or any entity of chartered accountants, and the applicability clause states SQC 1 applies to all CA firms. Changing the constitution of the practice therefore changes nothing: the sole proprietorship remains a firm, all engagement types including related services stay within scope, and the system of quality control must still address all six elements. The distractors each assume that some element or some engagement category presupposes partners or supervisory layers, which the definitions and applicability provisions do not support. The decisive point is that neither the definition of firm nor the list of elements contains a form-of-practice or headcount condition.

questions.question:
Meena Iyer is a chartered accountant practicing as a sole proprietor under the name Meena and Associates. Her practice includes one other full-time employee who is a chartered accountant, two articled clerks engaged in client work, and Mr. Sunil Rathod, a chartered accountant working with the firm on a part-time basis while continuing as a full-time employee of another audit firm. Meena appointed Mr. Rathod as the Engagement Partner for the statutory audit of Ananya Textiles Pvt. Ltd., reasoning that he has more years of experience than her full-time employee. The firm also accepted several related services engagements. When a fellow member advised her that SQC 1 obliges her to establish a system of quality control, Meena responded that a sole proprietorship with a handful of staff is not a 'firm' and that SQC 1 is meant for large partnership firms.

On the meaning of 'firm' under SQC 1 and the applicability of SQC 1 to Meena's practice, which of the following is the MOST APPROPRIATE conclusion?
options: Meena is correct; 'firm' in SQC 1 means an association of at least two practicing chartered accountants, so a sole proprietorship is outside SQC 1.

Meena is incorrect; 'firm' includes a sole proprietor, and since SQC 1 applies to all CA firms and to all types of engagements, her practice must establish the system, covering her related services engagements as well.
Meena is incorrect only in part; SQC 1 covers a sole proprietorship but its system applies only to assurance work, leaving related services engagements outside it.
Meena is substantially correct; a small practice may rely on the personal vigilance of the proprietor in place of any system of quality control.
questions.explanation: SQC 1 defines a firm as a sole proprietor, partnership, or any entity of chartered accountants, so Meena's practice is unambiguously a firm; equally, SQC 1 applies to all CA firms, with no size or structure carve-out. The applicability clause extends the standard to all types of engagements including related services engagements, so her non-audit work is inside the system, not outside it. The first option invents a two-partner minimum that the definition contradicts; the third wrongly narrows coverage to assurance work; the fourth substitutes personal diligence for the mandated system. The decisive facts are the sole-proprietor wording in the definition combined with the all-firms and all-engagements applicability wording.

questions.question:
Meena Iyer is a chartered accountant practicing as a sole proprietor under the name Meena and Associates. Her practice includes one other full-time employee who is a chartered accountant, two articled clerks engaged in client work, and Mr. Sunil Rathod, a chartered accountant working with the firm on a part-time basis while continuing as a full-time employee of another audit firm. Meena appointed Mr. Rathod as the Engagement Partner for the statutory audit of Ananya Textiles Pvt. Ltd., reasoning that he has more years of experience than her full-time employee. The firm also accepted several related services engagements. When a fellow member advised her that SQC 1 obliges her to establish a system of quality control, Meena responded that a sole proprietorship with a handful of staff is not a 'firm' and that SQC 1 is meant for large partnership firms.

Can Mr. Rathod validly hold the position of Engagement Partner for the audit of Ananya Textiles Pvt. Ltd. as per the definitions in SQC 1?
options: Yes, because the definition of Engagement Partner turns on competence, and experience is the decisive qualification.
Yes, because a firm may designate any chartered accountant as Engagement Partner if the proprietor personally reviews the audit work.
No, because the Engagement Partner must be a full-time practicing chartered accountant in the firm, which Mr. Rathod is not.
No, because in a sole proprietorship the Engagement Partner can only be the proprietor herself and no other person.
questions.explanation: SQC 1 defines the Engagement Partner as a FULL-TIME practicing chartered accountant in the firm who is responsible for the engagement. Mr. Rathod works with Meena's firm only part-time and remains a full-time employee of another audit firm, so the full-time condition in the definition fails regardless of his experience; the decisive fact is his engagement status, not his seniority. The first and second options treat experience or supervisory review as substitutes for the defined eligibility condition, which the definition does not permit. The fourth option over-corrects in the other direction: nothing in SQC 1 confines the role to a proprietor in a sole practice; the role simply demands a full-time practicing CA in the firm who is responsible for the engagement.

questions.question:
Meena Iyer is a chartered accountant practicing as a sole proprietor under the name Meena and Associates. Her practice includes one other full-time employee who is a chartered accountant, two articled clerks engaged in client work, and Mr. Sunil Rathod, a chartered accountant working with the firm on a part-time basis while continuing as a full-time employee of another audit firm. Meena appointed Mr. Rathod as the Engagement Partner for the statutory audit of Ananya Textiles Pvt. Ltd., reasoning that he has more years of experience than her full-time employee. The firm also accepted several related services engagements. When a fellow member advised her that SQC 1 obliges her to establish a system of quality control, Meena responded that a sole proprietorship with a handful of staff is not a 'firm' and that SQC 1 is meant for large partnership firms.

Consider the following statements on the 'engagement team' for the audit of Ananya Textiles Pvt. Ltd.:
Statement 1: The engagement team comprises all personnel performing the engagement, covering the engagement partner and the staff.
Statement 2: The articled clerks deployed on the audit work form part of the engagement team.
Statement 3: No person can belong to the engagement team unless he is a full-time practicing chartered accountant in the firm.
Statement 4: Meena cannot be part of the engagement team because she owns the practice rather than serving as staff on engagements.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2 and 4 only
questions.explanation: SQC 1 defines the engagement team as ALL personnel (engagement partner and staff) performing the engagement, which makes Statement 1 correct and, by the same wording, brings the articled clerks actually deployed on the audit inside the team, making Statement 2 correct. Statement 3 imports the EP's full-time condition into the wrong definition; the full-time practicing requirement attaches to the Engagement Partner role alone, while the team test is simply whether the person performs the engagement, so even Mr. Rathod working on the file falls within 'all personnel performing engagement'. Statement 4 wrongly excludes the proprietor: ownership is irrelevant, and any personnel performing the engagement, including Meena if she performs work on it, belong to the team. The decisive distinction is between the qualification for heading an engagement and the membership test for the team.

questions.category: SQC 1 - Elements of a System of Quality Control
questions.question:
Kothari and Partners is a newly formed partnership of three chartered accountants in Pune. Within two months of its formation, the firm accepted the statutory audit of a listed company, a limited review engagement for a half-year, a tax audit and several related services engagements. The firm drafted a quality control manual addressing: (1) the ultimate responsibility of the senior most partner for quality within the firm; (2) compliance with ethical requirements; (3) criteria for deciding whether to accept a prospective client and whether to continue a specific engagement of an existing client; (4) recruitment, compensation and development of personnel; (5) performance of engagements including review and documentation; and (6) periodic inspection by the firm of its own quality control policies and procedures. At the partners' meeting, one partner proposed that the entire area of monitoring be dropped from the manual for the first two years because the firm has no dedicated staff for the purpose. Another partner observed that all three partners hold full-time practicing certificates and proposed that each of them be appointed as Engagement Partner for the engagements allocated to him.

Consider the following statements regarding Kothari and Partners' obligations under SQC 1:
Statement 1: The firm's system of quality control shall include policies and procedures addressing all six elements, and the six areas of the manual correspond to those elements.
Statement 2: The proposal to drop monitoring for two years is impermissible, because none of the six elements is optional and the obligation is not conditioned on having dedicated staff.
Statement 3: The firm's system need only provide reasonable assurance regarding compliance with its own internal manual, since regulatory requirements are covered by professional standards anyway.
Statement 4: Being two months old, the firm may complete a few engagements first and design its system of quality control only at the close of its first financial year.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
Statements 1, 2 and 3 only
Statements 2 and 4 only
Statements 1, 2, 3 and 4
questions.explanation: Statement 1 correctly identifies the six areas of the manual with the six mandatory elements: SQC 1 requires the firm's system of quality control to include policies and procedures addressing each of the listed elements. Statement 2 is correct because the six-element enumeration admits no optionality; the applicability section extends SQC 1 to all CA firms without conditioning compliance on dedicated staff or firm age. Statement 3 is wrong because the stated objective is compliance with professional standards AND regulatory and legal requirements, which are stated as separate coordinate limbs; assurance defined by reference to the firm's own manual, on the premise that legal duties are absorbed into professional standards, understates the objective. Statement 4 is wrong: a newly formed partnership is fully covered from inception, and no waiting period appears in the applicability provisions.

questions.category: SQC 1 - Elements of a System of Quality Control
questions.question:
Kothari and Partners is a newly formed partnership of three chartered accountants in Pune. Within two months of its formation, the firm accepted the statutory audit of a listed company, a limited review engagement for a half-year, a tax audit and several related services engagements. The firm drafted a quality control manual addressing: (1) the ultimate responsibility of the senior most partner for quality within the firm; (2) compliance with ethical requirements; (3) criteria for deciding whether to accept a prospective client and whether to continue a specific engagement of an existing client; (4) recruitment, compensation and development of personnel; (5) performance of engagements including review and documentation; and (6) periodic inspection by the firm of its own quality control policies and procedures. At the partners' meeting, one partner proposed that the entire area of monitoring be dropped from the manual for the first two years because the firm has no dedicated staff for the purpose. Another partner observed that all three partners hold full-time practicing certificates and proposed that each of them be appointed as Engagement Partner for the engagements allocated to him.

A partner proposes amending the manual's third element to cover acceptance of new clients only, omitting continuance decisions on individual engagements, arguing that one unsuitable engagement in an otherwise good client relationship is immaterial. Which is the MOST APPROPRIATE reaction?
options: The amendment is impermissible; the element as listed by SQC 1 covers acceptance and continuance of client relationships AND of specific engagements, so engagement-level decisions must remain within the element.
The amendment is permissible, because decisions about an individual engagement belong to the element of engagement performance rather than to acceptance and continuance.
The amendment is permissible for a newly formed firm, since element (3) presupposes a mature client base with continuance histories.
The amendment is impermissible, because deleting continuance would first collide with the leadership responsibilities element, which owns all client decisions.
questions.explanation: The element is expressly headed 'Acceptance and continuance of client relationships and specific engagements', so the continuance limb operates at two levels, the relationship and the individual engagement; narrowing it to acceptance of new clients alone rewrites the element as listed. The first option captures this decisive wording. The second option mislocates engagement acceptance-and-continuance judgments in engagement performance, which is directed to review and documentation. The third option invents a maturity precondition that neither the elements nor the applicability clause contains. The fourth option reaches the right result through the wrong element, since leadership responsibilities for quality within the firm does not own specific client decisions.

questions.question:
Kothari and Partners is a newly formed partnership of three chartered accountants in Pune. Within two months of its formation, the firm accepted the statutory audit of a listed company, a limited review engagement for a half-year, a tax audit and several related services engagements. The firm drafted a quality control manual addressing: (1) the ultimate responsibility of the senior most partner for quality within the firm; (2) compliance with ethical requirements; (3) criteria for deciding whether to accept a prospective client and whether to continue a specific engagement of an existing client; (4) recruitment, compensation and development of personnel; (5) performance of engagements including review and documentation; and (6) periodic inspection by the firm of its own quality control policies and procedures. At the partners' meeting, one partner proposed that the entire area of monitoring be dropped from the manual for the first two years because the firm has no dedicated staff for the purpose. Another partner observed that all three partners hold full-time practicing certificates and proposed that each of them be appointed as Engagement Partner for the engagements allocated to him.

Which of the following is the MOST APPROPRIATE inference on the proposal that each of the three partners serve as Engagement Partner for the engagements allocated to him?
options: The proposal is inconsistent with SQC 1, as a firm can have only one Engagement Partner at any time.

The proposal is consistent with SQC 1, because the Engagement Partner is defined as a full-time practicing chartered accountant in the firm who is responsible for the engagement, and each partner can satisfy that description for the engagement he is responsible for.
The proposal is consistent only if the allocated engagements concern non-listed companies, listed audits demanding a single senior partner.
The proposal is inconsistent, because only the partner designated with ultimate responsibility for quality in the firm may serve as Engagement Partner.
The proposal is consistent only if the partners together form the engagement team for each other's engagements.
questions.explanation: The definition ties the Engagement Partner role to a person, not to a count: a full-time practicing chartered accountant in the firm who is responsible for THE engagement. Since responsibility runs engagement-wise and all three partners hold full-time practicing certificates, each can be the Engagement Partner of the engagement he is responsible for; nothing in SQC 1's definitions caps the number of engagement partners a firm may have across its engagements. The first option fabricates a one-EP-per-firm rule, the third a listed-company restriction, and the fourth conflates the leadership element's responsibility for quality within the firm with engagement-level responsibility. The fifth imposes a teamwork condition that the engagement team definition does not contain.

questions.category: SQC 1 - Elements of a System of Quality Control
questions.question:
Parekh and Co. is a partnership of five chartered accountants at Ahmedabad. The firm conducts annual financial statement audits, limited reviews and a large volume of related services engagements for more than 200 clients. While reviewing the firm's quality control documentation, a prospective partner notices that: (i) the manual's objective clause states that the firm's system of quality control is designed to provide reasonable assurance that the firm and its personnel comply with professional standards, without mentioning regulatory and legal requirements; (ii) the element headed 'acceptance and continuance' addresses only the acceptance of new clients, not the continuance of existing client relationships; (iii) there is no element dealing with leadership responsibilities, the partners treating it as a vague idea with no place in a quality control system; and (iv) the manual equates the 'engagement team' for each audit with the staff assistants alone, excluding the engagement partner.

Based on the above case, which of the following statements are correct?
Statement 1: Defect (i) is material because the objective of SQC 1 extends to compliance with regulatory and legal requirements alongside professional standards, and omitting the limb understates what the system must deliver.
Statement 2: Defect (ii) is material because the element as listed covers acceptance and continuance of client relationships and specific engagements.
Statement 3: Defect (iii) is immaterial because leadership responsibilities is guidance only and not one of the elements whose policies and procedures the system must address.
Statement 4: Defect (iv) is immaterial because the engagement team properly means only the personnel other than the engagement partner.
options: 1, 2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the stated objective covers compliance with professional standards AND regulatory and legal requirements, and the element is headed acceptance and continuance of client relationships and specific engagements, so defects (i) and (ii) each cut against the standard's wording. Statement 3 is wrong because leadership responsibilities for quality within the firm is one of the six elements the system shall address through policies and procedures; its absence is a structural defect, not a stylistic one. Statement 4 is wrong because the engagement team comprises ALL personnel, expressly including the engagement partner, performing the engagement, so excluding the EP contradicts the definition. All four defects are therefore material; only statements 1 and 2 acknowledge the two they concern.

questions.question:
Parekh and Co. is a partnership of five chartered accountants at Ahmedabad. The firm conducts annual financial statement audits, limited reviews and a large volume of related services engagements for more than 200 clients. While reviewing the firm's quality control documentation, a prospective partner notices that: (i) the manual's objective clause states that the firm's system of quality control is designed to provide reasonable assurance that the firm and its personnel comply with professional standards, without mentioning regulatory and legal requirements; (ii) the element headed 'acceptance and continuance' addresses only the acceptance of new clients, not the continuance of existing client relationships; (iii) there is no element dealing with leadership responsibilities, the partners treating it as a vague idea with no place in a quality control system; and (iv) the manual equates the 'engagement team' for each audit with the staff assistants alone, excluding the engagement partner.

Parekh and Co. decides to revise its manual to conform to SQC 1. Which combination of changes is required?
options: Restore the regulatory and legal requirements limb in the objective clause; add a new element of complaints and allegations so continuance decisions need not be revisited; insert the leadership responsibilities element; and retain the engagement team definition.

Restore the regulatory and legal requirements limb in the objective clause; extend element (3) to cover continuance of client relationships and specific engagements; insert the element of leadership responsibilities for quality within the firm; and redefine engagement team to comprise all personnel, the engagement partner and staff, performing the engagement.

Extend element (3) to continuance decisions; insert the leadership responsibilities element; and redefine engagement team to comprise all personnel performing the engagement, the objective clause needing no change since professional standards subsume legal requirements.

Restore the regulatory and legal requirements limb; insert the leadership responsibilities element; redefine the engagement team; and, to fund the revision, replace the monitoring element with periodical peer review.
questions.explanation: Conformity requires four coordinated corrections, each traceable to the opening provisions of SQC 1: the objective must cover compliance with professional standards AND regulatory and legal requirements; the third element must read acceptance and continuance of client relationships AND specific engagements; leadership responsibilities for quality within the firm must appear among the six elements the system's policies and procedures address; and the engagement team must include the engagement partner along with staff performing the engagement. The first option wrongly presents 'complaints and allegations' as one of the six elements while leaving defect (ii) uncorrected. The third leaves defect (i) uncorrected on the false premise that professional standards subsume legal requirements. The fourth trades the mandatory monitoring element for peer review, repeating rather than curing a structural omission.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the leadership responsibilities of a firm for quality within the firm under SQC 1:
Statement 1: The firm's leadership and the examples it sets significantly influence the internal culture of the firm to perform work that complies with professional standards and regulatory and legal requirements.
Statement 2: The firm must assign its management responsibilities so that commercial considerations do not override the quality of work performed.
Statement 3: Policies designed to demonstrate the firm's overriding commitment to quality are required only in regard to compensation and promotion; performance evaluation of personnel is outside this requirement.
Statement 4: The firm must devote sufficient resources for the development of its quality control policies and procedures.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1 and 3 only
1, 3 and 4 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 4 only
questions.explanation: SQC 1 states that leadership and the examples it set significantly influence the internal culture of the firm to perform work complying with professional standards and regulatory and legal requirements, and then lists three specific requirements: assignment of management responsibilities so that commercial considerations do not override quality, policies addressing compensation, promotion AND performance evaluation designed to demonstrate the overriding commitment to quality, and the devotion of sufficient resources to the development of quality control policies and procedures. Statement 3 is incorrect because performance evaluation is expressly named as one of the three policy areas, so the requirement cannot be confined to compensation and promotion. The decisive point is the completeness of the policy list in requirement (ii). Statements 1, 2 and 4 reproduce the source correctly.

questions.question:
CASE STUDY: Mehta and Associates is a mid-size chartered accountancy firm with 14 partners and 90 personnel. The senior partner, CA Mehta, has restructured the firm so that every partner is a business head responsible for client acquisition and revenue targets for an assigned group. The firm's annual performance review of partners allots 60 weightage to fee growth and billable hours and only 20 to engagement quality indicators; a partner in the lowest quartile for fee growth is refused elevation to the executive committee for three years irrespective of the quality of his or her engagements. The quality control policies were drafted three years ago by a single part-time partner with no supporting staff and no training budget, and they have not been revised since. On one audit, the engagement partner gave up a substantive procedure on a material revenue balance after the client threatened to shift its tax work to another firm, and the firm's appraisal note described this decision as protecting the relationship.
Consider the following statements:
Statement 1: The weightage pattern in the partners' performance review is inconsistent with the requirement that policies addressing compensation, promotion and performance evaluation be designed to demonstrate the firm's overriding commitment to quality.
Statement 2: Refusal of elevation to the executive committee on the basis of fee growth is an internal promotion matter outside the requirement, because it concerns the firm's governance structure and not the personnel who perform engagements.
Statement 3: The appraisal note praising the abandonment of a substantive procedure indicates that management responsibilities have not been assigned so that commercial considerations do not override the quality of work performed.
Statement 4: Because the quality control policies were prepared by a partner of the firm rather than by an external consultant, the requirement to devote sufficient resources has been satisfied.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1, 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 4 only
All of the above
questions.explanation: Requirement (ii) reaches the firm's policies on compensation, promotion and performance evaluation with regard to its personnel, and elevation to the executive committee is a promotion decision; therefore Statement 2 is wrong - the requirement is not confined to remuneration, and a promotion rule driven solely by fee growth and expressly indifferent to engagement quality defeats the overriding commitment to quality. Statement 4 is wrong because sufficiency of resources is tested by the adequacy of what the firm devotes (staff, budget, upkeep of the policies), not by the identity or external status of the drafter; a single part-time partner with no staff, no training budget and three years without revision shows the opposite. Statements 1 and 3 correctly apply requirement (ii) and requirement (i) respectively to the facts, and the decisive fact for Statement 3 is that the firm rewarded the surrender of a procedure under commercial pressure.

The firm proposes four separate changes. Which change MOST DIRECTLY remedies the leadership requirement regarding the assignment of management responsibilities?
options: Appointing a full-time quality control partner with supporting staff and a training budget for policy development
Circulating the Code of Ethics to all personnel each year with a cover note from the senior partner
Reducing the fee growth weightage in partner reviews from 60 to 40 and adding a client satisfaction survey

Reorganising the firm so that partners carrying commercial targets do not take the final decision on the nature and extent of procedures on their own groups' engagements, with an independent reporting line for such decisions
questions.explanation: Requirement (i) is directed at how management responsibilities are assigned - the object is that commercial considerations do not override quality of work performed. Handing the decision on the extent of procedures to a line not carrying revenue targets removes the structural conflict that produced the waived procedure, so it addresses requirement (i) directly. the first option remedies requirement (iii) on sufficient resources, the third option remedies requirement (ii) on compensation, promotion and performance evaluation but leaves the same partner able to trade a procedure against client retention, and the second option addresses the communication of ethical requirements rather than the assignment of management responsibilities. The decisive fact is which requirement each change is capable of curing on its own.

On one audit, the engagement partner gave up a substantive procedure on a material revenue balance after the client threatened to shift its tax work to another firm, and the firm's appraisal note described this decision as protecting the relationship.
ASSUME A MODIFIED FACT: the 60/20 weightage and the promotion rule now apply only to personnel of the firm's tax and advisory verticals, while every person working on assurance engagements is reviewed exclusively on engagement quality indicators. The fee growth targets, the client threat and the appraisal praise for the waived procedure remain unchanged.
Which conclusion is MOST APPROPRIATE on the modified facts?
options: The leadership requirements are now fully satisfied, because assurance personnel are appraised only on quality
Only requirement (iii) remains unremedied; the change cures the compensation, promotion and performance evaluation requirement

The change does not cure the breach, because requirement (ii) addresses policies with regard to the firm's personnel and requirement (i) is directed to commercial considerations not overriding the quality of work performed
The requirements are breached only if the abandoned procedure leads to an adverse audit report
questions.explanation: Requirement (ii) speaks of policies addressing compensation, promotion and performance evaluation with regard to the firm's personnel, which is not confined to a particular service line; carving the incentive out of assurance staff while leaving it with other personnel does not demonstrate an overriding commitment to quality across the firm. More decisively, requirement (i) is about the substance of how management responsibilities are assigned and about the quality of work performed: the engagement partner still surrendered a substantive procedure under a commercial threat and the firm still praised it, so a commercial consideration demonstrably overrode quality irrespective of how the reviewer is scored. the second option wrongly treats the resources requirement as the only surviving defect, and the fourth option makes compliance depend on reporting outcomes rather than on the firm's structure and policies.

CASE STUDY: Mehta and Associates is a mid-size chartered accountancy firm with 14 partners and 90 personnel. The senior partner, CA Mehta, has restructured the firm so that every partner is a business head responsible for client acquisition and revenue targets for an assigned group. The firm's annual performance review of partners allots 60 weightage to fee growth and billable hours and only 20 to engagement quality indicators; a partner in the lowest quartile for fee growth is refused elevation to the executive committee for three years irrespective of the quality of his or her engagements. On one audit, the engagement partner gave up a substantive procedure on a material revenue balance after the client threatened to shift its tax work to another firm, and the firm's appraisal note described this decision as protecting the relationship.
Which of the following actions should the firm take to comply with SQC 1's leadership requirements?
Action 1: Redesign its compensation, promotion and performance evaluation policies so that they demonstrate the firm's overriding commitment to quality.
Action 2: Devote sufficient resources for the development of quality control policies and procedures.
Action 3: Assign management responsibilities so that commercial considerations do not override the quality of work performed.
Action 4: Obtain an annual written undertaking from each partner that no engagement conclusion was influenced by fee considerations, in place of altering the policies or the assignment of responsibilities.
options: 1, 2 and 3 only
1 and 4 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Actions 1, 2 and 3 correspond exactly to the three requirements SQC 1 states under leadership responsibilities: assignment of management responsibilities so that commercial considerations do not override quality, policies on compensation, promotion and performance evaluation designed to demonstrate the overriding commitment to quality, and sufficient resources devoted to the development of quality control policies and procedures. Action 4 is an individual assurance offered in substitution for the structural changes; the requirement is directed at the design of the firm's policies and at how responsibilities are assigned, not at declarations by personnel that the existing design was not breached. A written undertaking would also be inconsistent with the requirement that leadership itself, through the examples it sets, shape the internal culture that produced the appraisal note praising the waived procedure.

questions.question:
CASE STUDY: Vindhya Limited is a company whose equity shares are listed on a recognised stock exchange. CA Agarwal has been the engagement partner on its statutory audit since the year 2017-18 and the audit for 2025-26 would be his ninth consecutive year. The audit committee wrote to the firm stating that there have been no restatements, the audit has been completed on time each year and the team possesses deep institutional knowledge, so a change of partner would reduce audit quality. The firm's internal note concluded that because the engagement presents a low assessed risk and the client is content, the same partner may continue, and recorded that rotation would be considered only if the client complained. Separately, CA Agarwal has been the engagement partner for eleven years on the audit of the financial statements of Nirmaan Private Limited, an unlisted company, and for six years on a review of the quarterly financial information of Vindhya Limited.
Which of the following is the MOST APPROPRIATE conclusion regarding the statutory audit of Vindhya Limited for 2025-26?
options: The mandatory requirement is engaged: the engagement partner on the audit of the financial statements of a listed entity shall be rotated after a period of not more than seven years, and neither low assessed risk nor the client's preference displaces it
Continuity may be retained, because rotation is only one of several possible safeguards and the firm is free to select another
The requirement is directory rather than mandatory, because it is stated within an illustrative example
Rotation becomes necessary only if the firm's own processes identify a decline in the quality of performance
questions.explanation: SQC 1 states expressly, as a mandatory requirement, that in the case of the audit of financial statements of listed entities the engagement partner shall be rotated after a period of not more than seven years. The decisive facts are that Vindhya Limited's equity shares are listed and that the coming audit would be the ninth consecutive year under the same engagement partner, which exceeds the stated limit. The audit committee's letter and the low assessed risk are not among the two matters the firm is directed to consider when determining an appropriate safeguard, namely the nature of the engagement including the extent to which it involves public interest and the length of service of the engagement partner. The text labels the seven-year rule a mandatory requirement, so the second option is also wrong in treating rotation as merely one optional response in this situation.

questions.question:
CASE STUDY: Vindhya Limited is a company whose equity shares are listed on a recognised stock exchange. CA Agarwal has been the engagement partner on its statutory audit since the year 2017-18 and the audit for 2025-26 would be his ninth consecutive year. The audit committee wrote to the firm stating that there have been no restatements, the audit has been completed on time each year and the team possesses deep institutional knowledge, so a change of partner would reduce audit quality. The firm's internal note concluded that because the engagement presents a low assessed risk and the client is content, the same partner may continue, and recorded that rotation would be considered only if the client complained. Separately, CA Agarwal has been the engagement partner for eleven years on the audit of the financial statements of Nirmaan Private Limited, an unlisted company, and for six years on a review of the quarterly financial information of Vindhya Limited.
Consider the following statements based on the case:
Statement 1: Using the same engagement partner on an assurance engagement over a long period may impair the quality of performance and may create a familiarity threat.
Statement 2: In determining the appropriate safeguard, the firm should consider the nature of the engagement, including the extent to which it involves public interest, and the length of service of the engagement partner on the engagement.
Statement 3: The audit committee's written assurance of continuity, by itself, reduces the familiarity threat to an acceptable level.
Statement 4: Rotating the engagement partner is a safeguard that SQC 1 identifies for eliminating this threat.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
All of the above
questions.explanation: The worked illustration states that long use of the same engagement partner may impair the quality of performance and may create a familiarity threat, and that the matters to be considered in determining the appropriate safeguard are the nature of the engagement including the extent to which it involves public interest and the length of service of the engagement partner, with rotation named as a safeguard. Statement 3 misreads the framework: the acceptable level is reached by applying a safeguard, and a client's letter is not a safeguard identified by SQC 1; indeed the extent of public interest in a listed entity's audit points towards, not away from, action. The decisive fact is that both the length of service and the listed character of the engagement are the two matters the firm must weigh, and the client's satisfaction is neither of them.

CA Agarwal has been the engagement partner on its statutory audit since the year 2017-18 and the audit for 2025-26 would be his ninth consecutive year. The audit committee wrote to the firm stating that there have been no restatements, the audit has been completed on time each year and the team possesses deep institutional knowledge, so a change of partner would reduce audit quality. The firm's internal note concluded that because the engagement presents a low assessed risk and the client is content, the same partner may continue, and recorded that rotation would be considered only if the client complained. Separately, CA Agarwal has been the engagement partner for eleven years on the audit of the financial statements of Nirmaan Private Limited, an unlisted company, and for six years on a review of the quarterly financial information of Vindhya Limited.
Consider the following statements about the two other engagements described in the case:
Statement 1: The mandatory seven-year rotation requirement extends to the review of the quarterly financial information of Vindhya Limited, because a review is an assurance engagement.
Statement 2: The mandatory seven-year rotation requirement does not extend to the audit of the financial statements of Nirmaan Private Limited, because it is not a listed entity.
Statement 3: Because no mandatory period applies to the eleven-year engagement, the firm need not consider any safeguard for it.
Statement 4: The nature of the engagement, including the extent to which it involves public interest, and the length of service of the engagement partner remain relevant in determining an appropriate safeguard for the unlisted audit and for the review engagement.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
2 and 4 only
questions.explanation: The mandatory rule is stated narrowly for the audit of financial statements of listed entities and fixes rotation at a period of not more than seven years; a review of quarterly financial information, and the audit of an unlisted company, are outside its terms even though both fall within the firm's broader independence obligations. Statement 3 is incorrect because the firm must establish policies and procedures to identify circumstances and relationships that create threats to independence and take appropriate action to eliminate those threats or reduce them to an acceptable level by applying safeguards, and long use of the same engagement partner is the very circumstance the illustration addresses. Statement 4 is correct because the two matters to be weighed apply whenever the firm is determining a safeguard, irrespective of listing status.

CA Agarwal has been the engagement partner on its statutory audit since the year 2017-18 and the audit for 2025-26 would be his ninth consecutive year. Consider the following statements:
Statement 1: Rotation may be deferred until the client raises a complaint, because the illustration says the threat may arise rather than does arise.
Statement 2: Low assessed risk is one of the matters which the firm is required to consider in determining the appropriate safeguard.
Statement 3: For the audit of the financial statements of a listed entity, rotation of the engagement partner after a period of not more than seven years is stated to be a mandatory requirement.
Statement 4: The firm should identify circumstances and relationships that create threats to independence and take appropriate action to eliminate those threats or reduce them to an acceptable level by applying safeguards.
Which of the above statements are NOT correct?
options: 3 only
1, 3 and 4 only
2 only
1 and 2 only
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are the incorrect ones. The word may indicates that long use of the same engagement partner is capable of creating a familiarity threat and of impairing the quality of performance, which triggers the firm's obligation to take appropriate action; it is not a condition that a complaint must first be received, and the firm's file note making rotation contingent on client complaint misuses that language. The matters the firm is directed to consider are only the nature of the engagement, including the extent to which it involves public interest, and the length of service of the engagement partner; assessed risk is not listed, so Statement 2 wrongly elevates it. Statements 3 and 4 correctly restate the mandatory seven-year rule for audits of the financial statements of listed entities and the general independence obligation.

questions.question:
CASE STUDY: Seshadri and Co. has 8 partners, 40 personnel in its statutory audit and assurance wing and 25 personnel in its tax, advisory and internal audit verticals. Each January the firm circulates a one-page memorandum on independence to the assurance wing only, and new joiners receive the same memorandum at induction. In March 2025 the firm obtained signed written confirmations of compliance with independence from its partners and assurance personnel; the tax and advisory personnel were excluded on the view that they do not sign audit reports, and four personnel who were on leave were not chased. In June 2025 a partner reported that a close member of his family had acquired an interest in one of the firm's assurance clients and asked whether it mattered; the firm recorded the report in a register but took no further action, and in October it replied to the partner that its annual confirmation cycle had already been completed for 2025 and nothing would be done before January 2026. The firm's quality control manual states that confirmations are necessary only in a year in which a breach has been reported.
Consider the following statements:
Statement 1: Excluding the tax and advisory personnel from the written confirmation exercise is not permissible, because the confirmation is required from all firm personnel.
Statement 2: The four personnel on leave could be excluded for the year, provided their assigned work did not involve listed companies.
Statement 3: The manual's position that confirmations are needed only in a year in which a breach is reported is inconsistent with the requirement to obtain them at least annually.
Statement 4: Confirmations obtained from partners alone satisfy the requirement, since management responsibility for quality rests with the partners.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1, 2 and 4 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
All of the above
questions.explanation: The note to the ethical requirements section requires the firm, at least annually, to obtain written confirmation of compliance with independence from all firm personnel. The population is therefore the firm's personnel as a whole, so the tax and advisory verticals cannot be excluded on the basis that they do not sign audit reports (Statement 1) and partners alone do not discharge the requirement (Statement 4). The frequency is stated as a minimum, so a manual that suspends the exercise in years without a reported breach contradicts it, and a leave absence does not create an exception for any personnel or for any class of client (Statements 2 and 3).

The firm's quality control manual states that confirmations are necessary only in a year in which a breach has been reported.
What is the MOST APPROPRIATE conclusion on the firm's handling of the report made in June 2025?
options: It is adequate, because the firm completed its written confirmation cycle for the year in March 2025
It is inadequate only if the interest is later shown to have affected the report on the client's financial statements

It is inadequate, because the firm is required to identify circumstances and relationships that create threats to independence and take appropriate action to eliminate those threats or reduce them to an acceptable level by applying safeguards
It is adequate, because entering the report in the register itself amounts to identifying the circumstance as required

The June report disclosed a relationship between a partner's close family and an assurance client, which is precisely the kind of circumstance the firm must act upon; deferral to the next January confirms that no appropriate action was taken. The first option wrongly treats the annual written confirmation as a substitute for acting on an identified threat, since the two obligations are distinct, and the fourth option mistakes recording for action. The second option adds a condition - effect on the report - which the requirement does not impose.
