The firm's quality control manual states that confirmations are necessary only in a year in which a breach has been reported.
Which of the following actions would bring the firm's independence arrangements within SQC 1?
Action 1: Communicate the firm's independence requirements to all personnel rather than to the assurance wing alone.
Action 2: Obtain written confirmation of compliance with independence from all firm personnel at least annually, including those who were on leave.
Action 3: Act on reports of circumstances and relationships creating threats to independence when they arise, instead of waiting for the next annual cycle.
Action 4: Replace the annual written confirmation with an oral assurance from each vertical head in years in which no breach has been reported.
options: 1 and 4 only
1, 3 and 4 only
2 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
questions.explanation: Actions 1, 2 and 3 correspond to the three obligations in the source: communication of independence requirements to the firm's personnel, the note requiring written confirmation of compliance with independence from all firm personnel at least annually, and the duty to identify circumstances and relationships creating threats and take appropriate action to eliminate them or reduce them to an acceptable level by applying safeguards. Action 4 fails on both counts, because the confirmation must be in writing and must come from all personnel, and because it is not conditioned on the absence of a reported breach in the year. The decisive distinction is between the periodic confirmation requirement and the continuous duty to act on identified threats.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding ethical requirements and the Code of Ethics as referred to in SQC 1:
Statement 1: The Code of Ethics establishes five fundamental principles of professional ethics, one of which is professional competence and due care.
Statement 2: Independence is one of the five fundamental principles of professional ethics established by the Code.
Statement 3: Integrity, objectivity, professional competence and due care, confidentiality and professional behaviour are the fundamental principles established by the Code.
Statement 4: A firm may substitute its own internal ethics code for the Code of Ethics for engagements that involve unlisted clients.
Which of the above statements are NOT correct?
options: 1 and 3 only
2 and 4 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2 only
questions.explanation: The five fundamental principles listed are integrity, objectivity, professional competence and due care, confidentiality and professional behaviour, so Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Independence is not among those five: the source refers to the Code as including the independence requirement for assurance engagements, which is a requirement of the Code and not one of the enumerated fundamental principles, making Statement 2 incorrect. Statement 4 is incorrect because ethical requirements relating to audits and reviews of financial information and other assurance and related services engagements are contained in the Code of Ethics, without any carve-out based on the listing status of the client.

questions.question:
Match the following. Column I states a matter governed by SQC 1 under leadership responsibilities or ethical requirements; Column II states the requirement or consequence attached to it.
Column I:
(A) Assignment of the firm's management responsibilities
(B) Firm policies addressing compensation, promotion and performance evaluation of personnel
(C) Use of the same engagement partner on an assurance engagement over a long period
(D) Circumstances and relationships that create threats to independence
Column II:
(1) Should be designed to demonstrate the firm's overriding commitment to quality
(2) May impair the quality of performance and may create a familiarity threat
(3) Should be made such that commercial considerations do not override the quality of work performed
(4) Should be identified, with appropriate action taken to eliminate the threats or reduce them to an acceptable level by applying safeguards
Select the correct pairing.
questions.explanation: Requirement (i) under leadership concerns the assignment of management responsibilities and is worded so that commercial considerations do not override the quality of work performed, which pairs A with 3. Requirement (ii) is the one directed to compensation, promotion and performance evaluation policies and their design to demonstrate the overriding commitment to quality, pairing B with 1; swapping those two, as in any pairing beginning A-1, B-3, attributes each requirement to the wrong subject. The illustration attaches to long use of the same engagement partner the possibility of impaired quality of performance and a familiarity threat, pairing C with 2, while the obligation to identify and act applies to circumstances and relationships creating threats to independence, pairing D with 4. Note that (4) is not a safeguard itself but the general duty, so pairing D with 2 would confuse the general duty with the specific example.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): In the case of the audit of the financial statements of a listed entity, SQC 1 requires the engagement partner to be rotated after a period of not more than seven years. Reason (R): Because ethical requirements relating to audits and reviews of financial information, and other assurance and related services engagements, are contained in the Code of Ethics, the same seven-year rotation requirement applies to a review of the quarterly financial information of a listed entity.
Select the correct option.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is incorrect
A is incorrect but R is correct
questions.explanation: A is correct: the rotation of the engagement partner after a period of not more than seven years is stated as a mandatory requirement specifically for the audit of financial statements of listed entities. The opening clause of R is itself accurate, since ethical requirements for audits and reviews of financial information and other assurance and related services engagements are contained in the Code of Ethics, but the conclusion drawn from it is wrong: the seven-year rule is confined in terms to audits of the financial statements of listed entities and does not extend to a review engagement merely because a review falls within the scope of the Code's ethical requirements. R therefore reaches an incorrect conclusion and cannot explain A. The decisive point is the scope of the mandatory rule, not the breadth of the Code.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The firm should devote sufficient resources for the development of quality control policies and procedures. Reason (R): Since the firm's leadership and the examples it sets significantly influence the internal culture of the firm, the sufficiency of resources devoted to quality control is established by the number of partners who formally approve the quality control manual.
Select the correct option.
options: A is correct but R is incorrect
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is incorrect but R is correct
questions.explanation: A states requirement (iii) under leadership responsibilities correctly: the firm devotes sufficient resources for the development of quality control policies and procedures. R begins with a correct proposition - leadership and the examples it sets significantly influence the internal culture of the firm to perform work complying with professional standards and regulatory and legal requirements - but then supplies a test that the source does not support, because sufficiency of resources is about the resources actually committed to developing the policies, not about the count of partners who sign off the manual. Since the second half of R is incorrect, the option is that A is correct and R is incorrect, rather than both being correct but unconnected. The link between leadership influence and resourcing is a matter of tone and priority, not of a numerical test of approvals.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the firm's obligations in respect of independence as set out in SQC 1:
Statement 1: The Code of Ethics includes the independence requirement for assurance engagements.
Statement 2: The firm should establish policies and procedures to communicate its independence requirements to its personnel.
Statement 3: The firm's policies on independence need extend only to relationships between its personnel and clients, because circumstances internal to the firm cannot create threats to independence.
Statement 4: Where threats are identified, the firm must eliminate them or reduce them to an acceptable level by applying safeguards, since taking appropriate action is required once threats are identified.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 4 only
1 and 4 only
All of the above
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 restate the source: the Code includes the independence requirement for assurance engagements, the firm must communicate its independence requirements to its personnel, and having identified circumstances and relationships that create threats it must take appropriate action to eliminate those threats or reduce them to an acceptable level by applying safeguards. Statement 3 is incorrect because the requirement is expressed as identifying circumstances and relationships that create threats, without confining the exercise to external relationships. Statement 4 also corrects a common misreading: the two responses of elimination and reduction through safeguards are alternatives, so a threat that cannot be eliminated must still be reduced to an acceptable level rather than simply recorded.

questions.question:
CASE STUDY: Kothari and Bansal LLP circulates a quarterly internal newsletter naming the partner who generated the highest net fee revenue as its rainmaker, and states that rainmakers are the first in line for elevation to the equity panel. Its quality control manual provides that the firm's independence requirements are communicated to personnel once, when the manual is issued, and that no further communication is proposed. For the coming three years the firm proposes CA Bhat as the engagement partner on the statutory audits of the financial statements of Tirumala Exchanges Limited, whose equity shares are listed, where CA Bhat has already served as engagement partner for seven consecutive years, and on the audit of the financial statements of Girija Spinning Mills Private Limited, an unlisted client, where CA Bhat has served as engagement partner for nine consecutive years. The proposal paper records that rotation may be replaced by appointing an experienced retired partner as an additional reviewer, because both engagements are assessed as low risk and the clients are content with continuity.
Consider the following statements based on the case:
Statement 1: Linking elevation to the equity panel to fee revenue is a matter falling within the firm's policies addressing compensation, promotion and performance evaluation, which must be designed to demonstrate its overriding commitment to quality.
Statement 2: Communicating the independence requirements once, at the issuance of the manual, discharges the obligation, because that obligation is satisfied by awareness of the requirements rather than by repetition.
Statement 3: Long use of the same engagement partner is a circumstance the firm should identify, and it should take appropriate action to eliminate the resulting threat or reduce it to an acceptable level by applying safeguards.
Statement 4: The requirement that the firm devote sufficient resources for the development of quality control policies and procedures is not engaged by any fact stated in the case.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1 and 3 only
1, 3 and 4 only
1, 2 and 4 only
All of the above
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct because promotion and performance evaluation are expressly named policy areas, and a practice that makes fee revenue the route to elevation is not designed to demonstrate an overriding commitment to quality. Statement 2 is incorrect: the firm must establish policies and procedures to communicate its independence requirements to its personnel, and the same section requires it to identify circumstances and relationships creating threats to independence, which presupposes arrangements operating beyond a single issuance of the manual; nothing in the source limits communication to one occasion. Statement 3 correctly applies the identification and action obligation to the illustrative case of the long-serving engagement partner. Statement 4 is correct and is the fact that appears relevant but is not decisive: the case says nothing about the resources devoted to developing the policies, so that requirement is not engaged.

questions.question:
CASE STUDY: Kothari and Bansal LLP circulates a quarterly internal newsletter naming the partner who generated the highest net fee revenue as its rainmaker, and states that rainmakers are the first in line for elevation to the equity panel. Its quality control manual provides that the firm's independence requirements are communicated to personnel once, when the manual is issued, and that no further communication is proposed. For the coming three years the firm proposes CA Bhat as the engagement partner on the statutory audits of the financial statements of Tirumala Exchanges Limited, whose equity shares are listed, where CA Bhat has already served as engagement partner for seven consecutive years, and on the audit of the financial statements of Girija Spinning Mills Private Limited, an unlisted client, where CA Bhat has served as engagement partner for nine consecutive years. The proposal paper records that rotation may be replaced by appointing an experienced retired partner as an additional reviewer, because both engagements are assessed as low risk and the clients are content with continuity.
What is the MOST APPROPRIATE evaluation of the reasoning recorded in the proposal paper?
options: Sound, because the choice of safeguard is left to the firm's judgment and an additional reviewer may achieve the same objective as rotation

Sound as regards Girija Spinning Mills Private Limited and unsound as regards Tirumala Exchanges Limited, because assessed risk is a recognised ground for deferring rotation only where public interest is limited
Unsound only because a retired partner is not eligible to act as an additional reviewer on an audit engagement

Unsound, because assessed risk and client satisfaction are not among the matters the firm is to consider, and for the audit of the financial statements of a listed entity rotation after a period of not more than seven years is a mandatory requirement
questions.explanation: SQC 1 directs the firm to determine the appropriate safeguard by considering the nature of the engagement, including the extent to which it involves public interest, and the length of service of the engagement partner on the engagement; assessed risk and the clients' contentment are not among those matters, and the extent of public interest in a listed audit points towards action rather than continuity. For Tirumala Exchanges Limited the mandatory requirement as to rotation of the engagement partner after a period of not more than seven years is squarely engaged, and the source names rotating the engagement partner as the safeguard for this threat, so a substitute mechanism cannot rest on a low risk assessment. The first option wrongly treats the choice of safeguard as unconstrained, the second invents a risk based exception, and the third rests on an eligibility point the source does not state.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST APPROPRIATE statement of the source of ethical requirements as referred to in SQC 1?
options: Ethical requirements for audits and reviews of financial information and other assurance and related services engagements are contained in the Code of Ethics, which includes the independence requirement for assurance engagements
Ethical requirements are contained in the quality control policies which each firm is required to frame under SQC 1, with the Code of Ethics relevant only for guidance
Ethical requirements for audits of financial statements alone are contained in the Code of Ethics, which establishes five fundamental principles of professional ethics
Ethical requirements are contained in the Code of Ethics, which establishes the independence requirement as the fifth fundamental principle of professional ethics
questions.explanation: SQC 1 states that ethical requirements relating to audits and reviews of financial information, and other assurance and related services engagements, are contained in the Code of Ethics, and that the Code establishes five fundamental principles and includes the independence requirement for assurance engagements. the second option wrongly transfers the source of ethical requirements to the firm's own policies; the firm's task is to establish policies and procedures relating to independence, not to originate ethical requirements. the third option is wrong on scope because reviews, other assurance and related services engagements are covered, and the fourth option wrongly reclassifies independence as one of the five principles - the fifth principle named is professional behaviour.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement 1: One of the fundamental principles of professional ethics established by the Code is confidentiality.
Statement 2: One of the fundamental principles established by the Code is professional behaviour.
Statement 3: The independence requirement stated by the Code extends, in terms, to assurance engagements.
Statement 4: Professional competence and due care is a fundamental principle established by the Code only in respect of audits of financial statements.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1, 2 and 3 only
1 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
All of the above
questions.explanation: The five fundamental principles listed are integrity, objectivity, professional competence and due care, confidentiality and professional behaviour, so Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is correct because the source describes the Code as including the independence requirement for assurance engagements. Statement 4 is incorrect: professional competence and due care is stated as a fundamental principle without qualification as to the type of engagement, whereas it is the independence requirement that is expressly tied to assurance engagements. The candidate must not import the scope-limiting words of one proposition into another principle.

questions.question: Which of the following pairings of a situation with the treatment required or permitted by SQC 1 is NOT correct?
options: Situation: the firm allots weightage to engagement quality indicators alongside fee growth in performance evaluation. Pairing: relevant to the requirement that compensation, promotion and performance evaluation policies demonstrate an overriding commitment to quality.

Situation: the engagement partner on the audit of the financial statements of a listed entity has served seven consecutive years. Pairing: the engagement partner shall be rotated after a period of not more than seven years.

Situation: a partner appraised largely on fee growth drops a procedure to retain a client and is commended for it. Pairing: no leadership requirement is breached, because the quality control manual states that quality is not to be compromised.
Situation: a review of the financial information of an entity. Pairing: ethical requirements relating to this engagement are contained in the Code of Ethics.
questions.explanation: The third option is the incorrect pairing and therefore the answer. The facts show both requirement (i) and requirement (ii) engaged: management responsibilities are not assigned so that commercial considerations do not override the quality of work performed, and appraisal weightage together with praise for the surrendered procedure shows the policies on performance evaluation are not designed to demonstrate the overriding commitment to quality. A statement in the manual that quality is not to be compromised does not cure a policy design that rewards the opposite. The other three pair each situation with treatment SQC 1 actually attaches to it, including the seven-year mandatory rotation limit for audits of the financial statements of listed entities, which by its terms does not reach review engagements.

questions.question: Four firms describe their practices for the year 2025-26. Which one fully complies with the requirement stated in SQC 1 regarding confirmations of compliance with independence?
options: Firm P obtains written confirmations of compliance with independence from the members of its assurance engagement teams once every two years
Firm Q obtains oral confirmations of compliance with independence from all its personnel every year
Firm S obtains written confirmations of compliance with independence from all its firm personnel, and proposes to obtain them again in a year only if a threat has been reported
Firm R obtains written confirmations of compliance with independence from all firm personnel, and has obtained them in each of the last four years
questions.explanation: The requirement is that at least annually the firm should obtain written confirmation of compliance with independence from all firm personnel, and all three elements are cumulative: frequency at least annually, form written, and population all firm personnel. Firm P fails on frequency, Firm Q fails on form, and Firm S fails because it suspends the exercise in years without a reported threat, treating a minimum frequency as a conditional one. Firm R alone satisfies all three, and the four-year record shows a cycle of not less than annual frequency.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement 1: The internal culture of the firm to perform work that complies with professional standards and regulatory and legal requirements is significantly influenced by the firm's leadership and the examples it sets.
Statement 2: The requirement to assign management responsibilities so that commercial considerations do not override quality of work performed is discharged once the quality control function reports to a partner who carries no client acquisition target.
Statement 3: The requirement that policies on compensation, promotion and performance evaluation demonstrate the overriding commitment to quality applies only to partners and not to other personnel of the firm.
Statement 4: The firm should devote sufficient resources for the development of quality control policies and procedures.
Which of the above statements are NOT correct?
options: 1 and 4 only
2 and 3 only
3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 4 correctly reproduce the source on leadership influence and on the devotion of sufficient resources. Statement 2 is incorrect because the requirement addresses how the firm assigns its management responsibilities so that commercial considerations do not override quality of work performed, and one independent reporting line is not by itself stated to discharge it. Statement 3 is incorrect because the policy requirement is expressed with regard to the firm's personnel, a term that covers staff as well as partners, and there is no stated carve-out for the non-partner population; the inference that only partners are covered reads the requirement too narrowly.

questions.question:
CASE STUDY: Anand and Rao has been the engagement partner on the statutory audit of Suraksha Retail Limited, an entity whose equity shares are listed on a recognised stock exchange, for seven consecutive financial years ending 31 March 2025, and the audit for 2025-26 is due to commence in July 2025. Suraksha Retail has been a client of the firm for nineteen years, during eleven of which a different partner was the engagement partner. The firm's written internal practice is to reappoint an engagement partner for a further two years before any change is considered, and to treat that practice as governing the rotation decision. No restatement, qualification or other quality issue has been reported on the audits completed so far.
Consider the following statements based on the case:
Statement 1: For the audit of the financial statements of Suraksha Retail Limited, the engagement partner shall be rotated after a period of not more than seven years, so the commencement of an eighth audit with the same engagement partner is not permissible.
Statement 2: The firm's nineteen-year association with the client is a matter to be considered along with the length of service of the engagement partner in determining the appropriate safeguard.
Statement 3: The absence of any reported quality issue reduces the familiarity threat to an acceptable level.
Statement 4: The firm's internal practice of a further two years before any change cannot displace the mandatory requirement applicable to this engagement.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1 and 4 only
1 only
1, 2 and 3 only
All of the above
questions.explanation: Suraksha Retail Limited is a listed entity and its statutory audit is squarely within the mandatory requirement that the engagement partner be rotated after a period of not more than seven years; seven consecutive years have been completed, so an eighth audit with the same engagement partner is not permitted and the firm's two-year internal practice cannot displace that requirement. Statement 2 is incorrect because the two matters the firm is directed to consider in determining the appropriate safeguard are the nature of the engagement, including the extent to which it involves public interest, and the length of service of the engagement partner on the engagement, not the duration of the firm's relationship with the client. Statement 3 is incorrect because the acceptable level is reached by applying a safeguard, and the clean audit history is not one; the absence of reported issues is also not among the listed matters.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST APPROPRIATE reflection of the illustrative example in SQC 1 on the use of the same engagement partner over a long period?
options: It states that long use of the same engagement partner may impair the quality of performance and may create a familiarity threat, and that safeguards for this threat include rotating the engagement partner
It states that long use of the same engagement partner creates a threat to independence in every case, and that the only permissible safeguard is rotation
It states that long use of the same engagement partner is permissible unless the client is a listed entity, in which case rotation is required at once
It states that long use of the same engagement partner affects only the appearance of independence and is therefore addressed by communication of independence requirements to personnel
questions.explanation: The illustration is expressed in terms of possibility and is directed to the quality of performance as well as to the familiarity threat, and it says safeguards to eliminate this threat include rotating the engagement partner, so rotation is one safeguard identified rather than the only permissible one. The second option reads the permissive may as a certainty and treats rotation as the only permissible safeguard, whereas the illustration says that safeguards to eliminate this threat include rotating the engagement partner. The third option wrongly equates the absence of a mandatory period for unlisted engagements with permission to continue indefinitely, and the fourth wrongly treats communication of independence requirements as the response to an identified threat, whereas that obligation is the separate general requirement and the response required is to eliminate the threat or reduce it to an acceptable level by applying safeguards.

questions.question:
CASE STUDY: Kothari and Bansal LLP circulates a quarterly internal newsletter naming the partner who generated the highest net fee revenue as its rainmaker, and states that rainmakers are the first in line for elevation to the equity panel. Its quality control manual provides that the firm's independence requirements are communicated to personnel once, when the manual is issued, and that no further communication is proposed. For the coming three years the firm proposes CA Bhat as the engagement partner on the statutory audits of the financial statements of Tirumala Exchanges Limited, whose equity shares are listed, where CA Bhat has already served as engagement partner for seven consecutive years, and on the audit of the financial statements of Girija Spinning Mills Private Limited, an unlisted client, where CA Bhat has served as engagement partner for nine consecutive years. The proposal paper records that rotation may be replaced by appointing an experienced retired partner as an additional reviewer, because both engagements are assessed as low risk and the clients are content with continuity.
Which of the following actions should the firm take to comply with SQC 1?
Action 1: Rotate the engagement partner on the audit of the financial statements of the listed client, since seven years of service on that audit have already been completed.
Action 2: Consider, for both engagements, the nature of the engagement, including the extent to which it involves public interest, and the length of service of the engagement partner, in determining the appropriate safeguard.
Action 3: Redesign the rainmaker recognition and elevation practice so that the firm's policies on compensation, promotion and performance evaluation demonstrate its overriding commitment to quality.
Action 4: Obtain written confirmation of compliance with independence from the partners assigned to these two audits at the conclusion of each audit.
options: 1 and 4 only
1, 2 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Actions 1, 2 and 3 correspond to the mandatory rotation requirement for the audit of the financial statements of a listed entity, to the two matters the firm must weigh in determining the appropriate safeguard, which apply to the unlisted engagement as well, and to the requirement that policies addressing compensation, promotion and performance evaluation demonstrate the overriding commitment to quality. Action 4 fails the confirmation requirement twice, because the written confirmation must be obtained from all firm personnel rather than from the partners on two engagements, and at least annually rather than at the conclusion of an audit. Rotation on the listed audit cannot be replaced by the additional reviewer proposed in the file, since the source names rotating the engagement partner as the safeguard for this threat and fixes a mandatory period beyond which the same partner may not continue.

questions.question:
Case Study. M/s Kalyan Rao & Co., a mid-sized chartered accountants firm with fourteen professionals, has been approached to audit Vindhya Spinning Mills Limited for the year ending 31 March 2026. The firm has not yet accepted the engagement. The following facts emerged in preliminary discussions:
(1) Trade journals describe the principal promoter, Shri R. Gupta, as having publicly abused two earlier auditors, one of whom has a professional complaint pending; two persons proposed for the board are people about whom the firm could obtain no information at all.
(2) Shri Gupta said: "The previous auditor charged Rs. 18 lakh. If your fee is more than Rs. 9 lakh the work will go elsewhere, though we want the same work."
(3) Asked in writing why M/s Deshmukh & Associates, the outgoing auditors, were not reappointed, the company secretary replied: "This is not important, do not waste your time on it."
(4) The head of finance said that two spare-parts warehouses need not be attended by the audit team, that the firm should "not bother testing" internal controls, and that the audit report must be signed by 25 April even though the books close only on 31 March.
(5) The firm has audited hosiery units but no member of the firm has audited a spinning mill; its only textile-experienced partner returns from leave on 30 June 2026 and no outside expert has been approached.
(6) Shri Gupta mentioned that a "related entity at Dubai" sometimes receives payments through unofficial routes for which no records are available.
(7) Shri Gupta added: "We follow our own interpretation of the standards on asset lives and revenue recognition. An auditor who disagrees with us is replaced."

Which of the following statements correctly classifies the above facts under the matters SQC 1 requires the firm to consider?
Statement 1: Fact (2) engages the matter, considered with regard to integrity of the client, concerning whether the client is aggressively concerned with maintaining the firm's fees as low as possible.
Statement 2: Fact (5) engages the capability matter concerning whether firm personnel have knowledge of relevant industries or subject matters.
Statement 3: Fact (3) bears only upon the firm's ability to complete the engagement within the reporting deadline.
Statement 4: The refusal in fact (4) to allow the audit team to attend two warehouses engages the integrity matter concerning indications of inappropriate limitation on scope of work.
options: Statements 1 and 3 only
Statements 2, 3 and 4 only
All four statements
Statements 1, 2 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Fact (2) is squarely within integrity matter (iv), which speaks of a client aggressively concerned with keeping the firm's fees as low as possible, and no cost threshold qualifies it. Fact (5) goes to capability matter (i) - knowledge of the relevant industry or subject matter - because the firm has audited only hosiery, not spinning mills. The refusal to permit attendance at two warehouses is an indication of inappropriate limitation on the scope of the work, i.e. integrity matter (v). Statement 3 is the wrong one: the secretary's refusal to explain the predecessor's non-reappointment is integrity matter (vii), not a timing or capability point, so any option containing statement 3 must be rejected.

With reference to fact (2) alone, which of the following is the MOST APPROPRIATE view under SQC 1?
options: The demand matters only if the offered fee is below the firm's cost of doing the audit.
The demand is one of the matters the firm considers with regard to the integrity of the client, whatever the commercial viability of the fee quoted.
The demand concerns the firm's capabilities and competency, because a lower fee means fewer resources.

Option 1 invents a threshold the source does not state; option 3 transfers the fact into the capabilities and competency list, which instead covers industry knowledge, regulatory experience, sufficiency of personnel, experts and the reporting deadline; option 4 ignores that fee pressure is examined at the acceptance and continuance stage itself.

Case Study. M/s Kalyan Rao & Co., a mid-sized chartered accountants firm with fourteen professionals, has been approached to audit Vindhya Spinning Mills Limited for the year ending 31 March 2026. The firm has not yet accepted the engagement. The following facts emerged in preliminary discussions:

(2) Shri Gupta said: "The previous auditor charged Rs. 18 lakh. If your fee is more than Rs. 9 lakh the work will go elsewhere, though we want the same work."
(3) Asked in writing why M/s Deshmukh & Associates, the outgoing auditors, were not reappointed, the company secretary replied: "This is not important, do not waste your time on it."

(7) Shri Gupta added: "We follow our own interpretation of the standards on asset lives and revenue recognition. An auditor who disagrees with us is replaced."

Which of the following actions are consistent with SQC 1 for the firm while it decides whether to accept?
A1: Obtain the reasons for the proposed appointment of the firm and for the non-reappointment of M/s Deshmukh & Associates, despite the company secretary's reluctance.
A2: Treat the statements in fact (4) as indications of inappropriate limitation on the scope of work and weigh them in evaluating the integrity of the client.
A3: Examine whether personnel with spinning-mill knowledge or outside experts are available and whether the work can be done by the required date, as matters of capabilities and competency.
A4: Accept first and consider facts (1), (2) and (6) during the audit, since consideration of integrity is essentially a continuing exercise.
options: A1, A2 and A4 only
A1, A3 and A4 only
A2, A3 and A4 only
A1, A2 and A3 only
questions.explanation: A1 implements integrity matter (vii), which has two limbs - reasons for the proposed appointment of the firm and for the non-reappointment of the previous firm. A2 implements matter (v) on inappropriate limitation on scope of work, and A3 implements capability matters (i), (iv) and (v) read with condition (b) on capabilities, time and resources. A4 fails, because the firm's policies must give reasonable assurance that it undertakes a relationship or engagement only where it has considered the integrity of the client; that consideration precedes acceptance, and any later-discovered problem belongs to the separate area of information obtained after acceptance.

(7) Shri Gupta added: "We follow our own interpretation of the standards on asset lives and revenue recognition. An auditor who disagrees with us is replaced."

Match the facts in Column I with the matter they primarily engage in Column II.
Column I
(A) Fact (6) - payments routed through unofficial channels to a related entity at Dubai
(B) Fact (7) - "we follow our own interpretation of the standards"
(C) Fact (1) - two proposed directors about whom nothing can be learned
(D) Fact (5) - no access to a person with spinning-mill or valuation expertise
Column II
(1) Identity and business reputation of the client's principal owners, key management and those charged with governance

(4) Availability of experts, if needed, as a matter of capabilities and competency
questions.explanation: Undocumented payments through unofficial routes are the classic indication that the client might be involved in money laundering or other criminal activities, so A pairs with 2. Unknowable proposed directors go to matter (i), which names principal owners, key management and those charged with governance, so C pairs with 1. The absence of any expert is capability matter (iv), so D pairs with 4 - note that this last fact is a capability issue while the first three are integrity issues.

questions.question:
Case Study. M/s Kalyan Rao & Co., a mid-sized chartered accountants firm with fourteen professionals, has been approached to audit Vindhya Spinning Mills Limited for the year ending 31 March 2026. The firm has not yet accepted the engagement. The following facts emerged in preliminary discussions:
(1) Trade journals describe the principal promoter, Shri R. Gupta, as having publicly abused two earlier auditors, one of whom has a professional complaint pending; two persons proposed for the board are people about whom the firm could obtain no information at all.
(2) Shri Gupta said: "The previous auditor charged Rs. 18 lakh. If your fee is more than Rs. 9 lakh the work will go elsewhere, though we want the same work."
(3) Asked in writing why M/s Deshmukh & Associates, the outgoing auditors, were not reappointed, the company secretary replied: "This is not important, do not waste your time on it."
(4) The head of finance said that two spare-parts warehouses need not be attended by the audit team, that the firm should "not bother testing" internal controls, and that the audit report must be signed by 25 April even though the books close only on 31 March.
(5) The firm has audited hosiery units but no member of the firm has audited a spinning mill; its only textile-experienced partner returns from leave on 30 June 2026 and no outside expert has been approached.
(6) Shri Gupta mentioned that a "related entity at Dubai" sometimes receives payments through unofficial routes for which no records are available.
(7) Shri Gupta added: "We follow our own interpretation of the standards on asset lives and revenue recognition. An auditor who disagrees with us is replaced."

Which of the following statements about the firm's decision are correct under the acceptance and continuance requirement?
Statement 1: The firm may undertake this engagement only where it has considered the integrity of the client, is competent and has the capabilities, time and resources to perform it, and can comply with ethical requirements - the three conditions operate together.
Statement 2: Facts (4) and (5) together bear on whether the firm has the capabilities, time and resources, including completion within the reporting deadline.
Statement 3: Fact (7) cannot affect the integrity evaluation, because it concerns accounting-standards interpretation and not honesty.
Statement 4: The absence of information about the two proposed directors in fact (1) falls outside the integrity matters, since only principal owners and key management are named there.
options: Statements 2 and 3 only
All four statements
Statements 1 and 2 only
Statements 1, 2 and 4 only
questions.explanation: The purpose clause states three conditions - (a) considered the integrity of the client, (b) competence plus capabilities, time and resources, (c) ability to comply with ethical requirements - and all must be met, which makes statement 1 correct. Statement 2 is correct because the 25 April date and the missing textile experience engage capability matters (i), (iv) and (v) and the "time and resources" limb of condition (b). Statement 3 is wrong: matter (iii) expressly covers attitude towards the interpretation of accounting standards and towards the internal control environment. Statement 4 is wrong: matter (i) names those charged with governance along with principal owners and key management, so proposed directors are within it.

Which of the following is the MOST APPROPRIATE effect of this change?
options: Condition (b) ceases to be doubtful on these facts, but the firm must still consider the integrity matters raised by facts (1), (2), (3), (4) and (6), and its ability to comply with ethical requirements.

The engagement may then be accepted immediately without anything further being considered, because once capabilities and competency are established by this change the integrity condition in the purpose clause is satisfied by implication.
Only the availability-of-experts matter is cured; the reporting-deadline matter and the time element of condition (b) are untouched by the change.
The change also cures fact (4), because the retained specialist can attend the two warehouses in place of the audit team.

questions.question:
Case Study. M/s Anand & Bhatt is a six-professional firm at Rajkot handling forty audits, thirty-one of which must be reported by 30 May. On 20 January an old client of nine years, Kutch Exports Limited, asked the firm to accept, along with its own audit, the audit of a subsidiary the client had just bought - a gold jewellery trading business - because the subsidiary's earlier auditors "stopped replying to our letters and never told us why they left". The partner already knows, from conversations at a business club, that the promoter of the subsidiary is widely believed locally to deal in unstamped bullion, but decided not to record this because the promoter is "a pleasant person". February to 30 April is the firm's peak period and every staff member is already committed, yet the partner assumed the extra work "would somehow fit in". The firm has nobody who has audited a jewellery business and has no contact with a valuer or with anyone conversant with bullion and precious-metals requirements. The management of the subsidiary said the audit team may not enter the bullion vault and should accept the vault officer's certificate. The firm has never reviewed acceptance decisions in its internal quality review, and the partner said that in any case its acceptance policies apply only to clients not previously audited by it, not to a nine-year-old relationship.

Which of the following statements are correct under SQC 1?
Statement 1: Acceptance and continuance policies are required only for clients the firm has not previously audited, so the partner's view is correct.
Statement 2: The audit of the newly acquired subsidiary is a specific engagement, and the policies must give reasonable assurance that it is undertaken only where the three stated conditions are met.
Statement 3: Continuance of the nine-year relationship with Kutch Exports Limited itself falls within the same policies and procedures.
Statement 4: Because the relationship is nine years old, no consideration of integrity is needed for the subsidiary engagement.
options: Statements 1 and 4 only
Statements 2 and 3 only
Statements 1, 2 and 3 only
All four statements
questions.explanation: The heading and the purpose clause both speak of acceptance and continuance of client relationships and specific engagements, so statement 3 (continuance of the existing relationship) and statement 2 (a discrete new engagement inside that relationship) are both correct, and statement 1 is wrong. Statement 4 is wrong for the same reason: the subsidiary is a different engagement, with different owners, a different business and different persons charged with governance, so integrity must be considered for it even where the parent has been audited for years. Length of association supplies familiarity, not the consideration the standard requires.

The partner's decision to leave unrecorded what he knows about the subsidiary's promoter and that promoter's local standing is best criticised under SQC 1 as:
options: immaterial, because business reputation of a person is relevant only where a formal enquiry report exists.
a failure in respect of the identity and business reputation of the client's principal owners, key management and those charged with governance.
a capabilities and competency deficiency, because the firm has no valuer for a jewellery business.
a defect of internal quality review, which cannot influence an acceptance decision.
questions.explanation: Integrity matter (i) requires the firm to consider the identity and business reputation of the client's principal owners, key management and those charged with governance; it is not confined to documented or formally verified material, so the partner's own knowledge of the promoter's reputation is precisely the information that must be considered rather than set aside as "pleasant". Option 1 adds an evidentiary requirement the source does not impose. Option 3 misclassifies the point into capabilities and competency, which concerns industry knowledge, regulatory experience, sufficient personnel, experts and the reporting deadline. Option 4 is wrong because the acceptance decision itself is governed by conditions (a) to (c), independently of monitoring and review.

Which of the matters considered with regard to capabilities and competency are engaged by the above case?
Statement 1: Whether firm personnel have knowledge of the relevant industry or subject matter, given the jewellery trading business.
Statement 2: Whether the firm has sufficient personnel with the necessary capabilities and competence and whether the work can be completed by the reporting deadlines, given thirty-one audits due by 30 May during the firm's peak period.
Statement 3: Whether experts, such as a valuer or a person conversant with bullion-related requirements, are available if needed.
Statement 4: Whether the firm can comply with ethical requirements despite the nine-year familiarity with the parent, SQC 1 listing such compliance as a matter of capabilities and competency.
options: Statements 1, 2 and 3 only
Statements 1, 3 and 4 only
Statements 2 and 4 only
All four statements
questions.explanation: The five capability matters are industry or subject-matter knowledge, experience with regulatory or reporting requirements, sufficient personnel, availability of experts and completion within the reporting deadline; statements 1, 2 and 3 correspond to matters (i), (iii) with (v), and (iv) respectively, and the peak-season fact is decisive for the third. Statement 4 is the incorrect one: ability to comply with ethical requirements is condition (c) of the purpose clause, not a member of the capabilities and competency list, and familiarity is not treated by this block at all. On these facts, which of the following is the MOST APPROPRIATE overall conclusion under SQC 1?
options: The firm may accept once the previous auditors' departure is explained, because that explanation alone establishes integrity for the purposes of condition (a).

The firm may accept only if all three conditions are met, with the vault refusal and the unexplained departure of the previous auditors weighed as integrity matters and the peak-season load weighed under capabilities, time and resources.
The firm should decline on capability grounds alone, since integrity matters are required to be considered only at the stage when the firm has already decided to withdraw from the engagement.
The firm should accept the parent's audit but treat the subsidiary's audit as covered by the parent's nine-year record on integrity.

Option 1 overstates one matter as conclusive. Option 3 misplaces integrity into the withdrawal discussion. questions.question:
Case Study. Orbitchain Technologies Private Limited, a start-up whose reported revenue comes mainly from sale of participation tokens in a planned logistics blockchain and from fees credited by an offshore trading platform, proposes to appoint M/s Mehta & Shah as statutory auditors. Its register of members shows two foreign shareholders holding 74 per cent through a nominee structure, and the founders decline to identify the beneficial owners, saying that "these are investor privacy matters and the audit does not need them". The company keeps no conventional audit trail for token sales, and part of its advertising income is collected in cash without any receipt. The firm has audited software and IT-enabled service companies for years, but nobody in it has dealt with virtual-asset accounting or with the reporting and compliance requirements applicable to such platforms, and the firm has no access to an expert in this field. The founders said the fee should be "the lowest in the market because we are burning cash", and asked that the audit be completed in six weeks so that a fresh round of investment could then close.

Which of the following statements are correct?
Statement 1: The refusal to identify the beneficial owners behind the nominee holding engages the matter concerning identity and business reputation of the client's principal owners, key management and those charged with governance.
Statement 2: Cash collection of advertising income without receipts and the absence of an audit trail for token sales engage the matter concerning the nature of the client's operations, including its business practices.
Statement 3: The demand that the audit be finished in six weeks engages the integrity matter concerning indications of inappropriate limitation on scope of work.
Statement 4: The demand for the lowest fee in the market is expressly among the matters considered with regard to integrity of the client.
options: Statements 1, 2 and 3 only
Statements 1, 3 and 4 only
Statements 2, 3 and 4 only
Statements 1, 2 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Matter (i) reaches the identity of principal owners, and a 74 per cent holding hidden behind nominees with unidentified beneficial owners is exactly the kind of gap it requires the firm to consider, so statement 1 holds. Statement 2 tracks matter (ii), which expressly includes business practices alongside the nature of operations. Statement 4 tracks matter (iv) on aggressive concern with keeping the firm's fees low. Statement 3 misclassifies: a compressed timetable engages capability matter (v), completion of the engagement within the reporting deadline, together with the "time" limb of condition (b), whereas limitation on scope of work refers to restrictions on the work the firm may do.

Under the matters relating to capabilities and competency, this set of facts engages:

both matter (i) on knowledge of relevant industries or subject matters and matter (ii) on experience with relevant regulatory or reporting requirements, which are separately listed.
matter (ii) only, because the accounting for virtual assets is purely a reporting requirement.
matter (iv) only, since availability of experts is the sole remedy SQC 1 contemplates for such a gap.

The founders said the fee should be "the lowest in the market because we are burning cash", and asked that the audit be completed in six weeks so that a fresh round of investment could then close.

Which of the following actions are consistent with the matters SQC 1 requires the firm to consider before accepting this engagement?
A1: Seek information on the identity and business reputation of the founders and those charged with governance, and press for identification of the beneficial owners behind the nominees.
A2: Treat the indications of possible money laundering as concluded and decline, since such indications compel rejection of the client.
A3: Consider whether the firm has personnel with knowledge of the subject matter and experience of the relevant regulatory and reporting requirements, and whether experts are available.
A4: Consider whether the engagement could be completed within the reporting deadline, as part of capabilities, time and resources.
options: A2, A3 and A4 only
A1, A2 and A4 only
A1, A2 and A3 only
A1, A3 and A4 only
questions.explanation: A1 implements integrity matter (i) and A3 implements capability matters (i), (ii) and (iv), while A4 implements matter (v) read with the time and resources limb of condition (b). A2 is the inconsistent action: matter (vi) makes indications that the client might be involved in money laundering or other criminal activities something the firm considers, not a rule that such indications automatically compel rejection; the decisive point is that the firm must consider them, and a conclusion either way must rest on that consideration. Notice also that the cash receipts without receipts are considered under matter (ii) as business practices rather than under A1.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Under SQC 1, the firm's acceptance and continuance policies are designed to provide reasonable assurance that it will undertake or continue relationships and engagements only where it has considered the integrity of the client.
Reason (R): Because the stated condition is only that the integrity of the client be considered, a firm which has carried out and documented that consideration may accept the engagement even where the consideration discloses an integrity risk the firm is unwilling to carry.

Which of the above is correct?
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is incorrect.
A is incorrect but R is correct.
questions.explanation: A reproduces condition (a) exactly - the firm must have considered the integrity of the client, which is an obligation as to process and diligence and not a word-for-word guarantee that the client is honest. R draws the wrong inference from that wording: the purpose clause requires that the firm undertake or continue only where the conditions are met, and a consideration that discloses an unacceptable integrity risk is a reason not to accept, not a passport to acceptance. R also ignores that conditions (b) and (c) must be satisfied independently. Hence A is correct and R is incorrect.

questions.question:
Which of the following paraphrases of the matters considered with regard to the integrity of a client are INCORRECT?
Statement 1: The identity and business reputation of the client's principal owners and key management, those charged with governance being relevant to a different matter.
Statement 2: The nature of the client's operations, including its business practices.
Statement 3: Whether the client is aggressively concerned with maintaining the firm's fees as low as possible.
Statement 4: Indications of inappropriate limitation on scope of work, which the firm needs to consider only where the client is a new one.
options: Statements 1 and 2 only
Statements 2 and 3 only
Statements 3 and 4 only
Statements 1 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Matter (i) names the identity and business reputation of the client's principal owners, key management and those charged with governance together, so statement 1 wrongly moves TCWG out of that matter and is incorrect. Statements 2 and 3 reproduce matters (ii) and (iv) faithfully and are therefore correct paraphrases. Statement 4 is incorrect because the acceptance and continuance policies cover relationships and engagements continued as well as newly undertaken, so a limitation on scope signalled by a long-standing client is equally to be considered; the source attaches no new-client qualifier to matter (v). Carefully read the instruction, since the question asks for the incorrect ones.

questions.question: In determining whether the firm has capabilities, competence, time and resources to undertake a new engagement, SQC 1 lists certain matters. Which of the following is NOT one of those matters?
options: Whether firm personnel have experience with relevant regulatory or reporting requirements.
Whether the firm has sufficient personnel with the necessary capabilities and competence.
Whether information exists concerning the attitude of the client's key management towards the internal control environment.
Whether experts are available, if needed.
questions.explanation: The five capability matters are knowledge of relevant industries or subject matters, experience with relevant regulatory or reporting requirements, sufficiency of personnel with the necessary capabilities and competence, availability of experts if needed, and the ability to complete the engagement within the reporting deadline. The attitude of principal owners, key management and those charged with governance towards the interpretation of accounting standards and the internal control environment is integrity matter (iii), not a capability matter. The distractor is tempting because both lists are consulted at the same stage of acceptance, but the source keeps them in separate enumerations and the classification matters when documenting which condition was considered.

questions.question:
Match each situation in Column I with the matter on capabilities and competency in Column II that it engages most directly.
Column I
(A) A group audit is offered in a month in which the firm's entire staff is already committed to twenty-five other audits.
(B) A port trust's audit is offered to a firm whose partners have audited only manufacturing companies.
(C) An insurance company's audit needs a actuarial valuation of employee benefit obligations which nobody in the firm can perform.
(D) A bank's audit is offered to staff who know banking well but have never dealt with the regulatory returns required of such entities.
Column II
(1) Knowledge of relevant industries or subject matters
(2) Experience with relevant regulatory or reporting requirements
(3) Sufficient personnel with the necessary capabilities and competence
(4) Availability of experts, if needed
questions.explanation: Situation A is a question of whether the firm has sufficient personnel with the necessary capabilities and competence, i.e. matter (iii), read with the time and resources limb of condition (b). Situation B concerns knowledge of the relevant industry or subject matter, matter (i), since port operations are unfamiliar territory. Situation C is the classic availability-of-experts case, matter (iv), the valuation being outside the firm's own competence. Situation D is matter (ii), because the subject-matter knowledge exists but experience with the relevant regulatory or reporting requirements does not - the distinction that separates matters (i) and (ii) in the source.

questions.question:
Statement 1: The purpose clause requires the firm to have capabilities, time and resources in addition to competence before it undertakes or continues a relationship or engagement.
Statement 2: The ability to complete the engagement within the reporting deadline is expressly one of the matters considered in determining whether the firm has capabilities, competence, time and resources.
Statement 3: A shortage of time before the reporting deadline is an integrity matter, because it reveals management's attitude towards reporting.
Statement 4: The availability of experts, if needed, is treated as a matter of capabilities and competency and not as an integrity matter.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: Statements 1 and 3 only
Statements 2 and 3 only
Statements 1, 2 and 4 only
Statements 1, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Condition (b) is worded as competence plus "capabilities, time and resources", so statement 1 is correct and it is the textual home of the time element. Statement 2 is correct because capability matter (v) asks whether the firm would be able to complete the engagement within the reporting deadline. Statement 4 is correct because availability of experts is capability matter (iv), while the seven integrity matters are silent on expertise. Statement 3 misclassifies: the integrity list covers attitude towards the interpretation of accounting standards and the internal control environment, aggressive fee pressure, scope limitation indications, money-laundering indications, identity and reputation, nature of operations and reasons for the change of auditors - not deadline pressure.

questions.question: Under SQC 1, the firm's policies and procedures on acceptance and continuance are required to cover:
options: client relationships only, specific engagements being dealt with under engagement performance.
both client relationships and specific engagements, so that a decision to continue a relationship does not by itself settle acceptance of each engagement in it.
specific engagements only, integrity being a quality that attaches to the relationship as a whole.
both, but consideration of the integrity of the client is required only when a relationship is first accepted.
questions.explanation: The heading and the purpose clause both refer to acceptance and continuance of client relationships and specific engagements, so the two objects are distinct and the requirement reaches each. Option 2 draws the correct operational consequence: continuing to audit a holding company does not answer whether a newly acquired subsidiary's audit, or an unusual tax or certification engagement for the same group, satisfies conditions (a) to (c). Option 1 and option 3 each delete one of the two objects. Option 4 is wrong because continuance is expressly inside the same policies, so integrity is considered for relationships continued as well as newly accepted.

questions.question: A firm has documented a careful consideration of the integrity of a prospective client and is satisfied that it can comply with ethical requirements. However, its only partner capable of leading the engagement will be on deputation to another city for four of the engagement's five months, and no expert can be secured for the specialised valuation involved. Which conclusion is MOST APPROPRIATE?
options: Acceptance is not supported, since condition (b) is separate from conditions (a) and (c) and the firm cannot say it is competent and has the capabilities, time and resources.
Acceptance is supported, two of the three conditions being met and the third being left to the engagement partner's judgement after appointment.
Acceptance is supported, because inability to obtain an expert becomes an integrity matter only where the client forbids the use of experts.
Acceptance is not supported, because a shortage of resources amounts automatically to inability to comply with ethical requirements.
questions.explanation: The three conditions are cumulative and each stands on its own facts, so satisfying (a) and (c) cannot cure a failure of condition (b). The missing leader and the unavailable expert engage capability matters (iii) and (iv) and the time and resources limb of condition (b), so acceptance is not supported. Option 2 postpones a pre-acceptance requirement to the performance stage; option 3 misclassifies an expertise gap as an integrity question, the integrity list containing no such matter; option 4 conflates two conditions, whereas inability to comply with ethical requirements is a distinct test that resource shortage does not automatically trigger.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): While deciding whether to accept an engagement, a firm examines the client's insistence on the lowest possible fee as a matter concerning the integrity of the client, not as a matter of the firm's capabilities and competency.
Reason (R): SQC 1 enumerates whether the client is aggressively concerned with maintaining the firm's fees as low as possible among the matters to be considered with regard to integrity of client, whereas the capabilities and competency list covers industry knowledge, regulatory or reporting experience, sufficiency of personnel, availability of experts and completion within the reporting deadline.

Which of the above is correct?
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is incorrect.
A is incorrect but R is correct.
questions.explanation: A states the classification correctly and R supplies the reason for it by pointing to the enumeration in the source, so R explains A rather than merely restating a compatible fact. The fee matter is the fourth of the seven integrity matters and appears nowhere in the capability list, which is why option 2 fails. Options 3 and 4 fail because neither statement is wrong. The analytical point worth retaining is that the concern is about the client's aggressive attitude towards the firm's fee - a signal about the client - and not about the firm's inability to work at that price, which would be a resource question.

questions.question:
Consider the seventh integrity matter, namely the reasons for the proposed appointment of the firm and the non-reappointment of the previous firm. Which of the following statements about it are INCORRECT?
Statement 1: It covers the reasons for the proposed appointment of the firm.
Statement 2: It covers the reasons for the non-reappointment of the previous firm.
Statement 3: It is fully satisfied once the client's management says that the change of auditors was routine, no separate consideration of the reasons for the firm's proposed appointment being needed.
Statement 4: It belongs to capabilities and competency, since a change of auditors affects the time available for the audit.
options: Statements 1 and 2 only
Statements 2, 3 and 4 only
Statements 1, 3 and 4 only
Statements 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Matter (vii) has two limbs, reasons for the proposed appointment of the firm and reasons for the non-reappointment of the previous firm, and statements 1 and 2 correctly describe them, so they are not the answers sought. Statement 3 is incorrect because it cancels one limb of the matter: both limbs have to be considered, and a routine explanation of the predecessor's exit does not answer why the firm is now proposed. Statement 4 is incorrect because this is an integrity matter; the capability list deals with industry knowledge, regulatory experience, sufficient personnel, experts and the reporting deadline, and does not treat a change of auditors as a timing question.

questions.question:
Each situation in Column I is a matter considered with regard to the integrity of the client under SQC 1. Match Column I with Column II.
Column I
(A) The finance head explains that cash purchases without invoices are "how the trade works here".
(B) The audit committee has resigned after pressing for a vigil mechanism, and management regards internal control as a formality.
(C) Two of the client's overseas counterparties have been named in a smuggling enquiry.
(D) A person proposed to the board is traced by the firm to another identity with no verifiable business history.
Column II
(1) Nature of the client's operations, including its business practices
(2) Attitude of the principal owners, key management and those charged with governance towards the interpretation of accounting standards and the internal control environment
(3) Indications that the client might be involved in money laundering or other criminal activities
(4) Identity and business reputation of the client's principal owners, key management and those charged with governance
questions.explanation: Situation A describes how the client transacts, i.e. the nature of its operations including its business practices, matter (ii). Situation B is about the attitude of those charged with governance towards the internal control environment, matter (iii); the tempting alternative, matter (i), is about who these persons are rather than what they think about standards and controls. Situation C is an indication of possible involvement in money laundering or other criminal activities, matter (vi), and situation D goes to identity and business reputation of principal owners, key management and those charged with governance, matter (i).

questions.question:
Statement 1: SQC 1 places the obligation on the firm to establish policies and procedures for acceptance and continuance of client relationships and specific engagements, rather than prescribing the outcome of any individual acceptance decision.
Statement 2: Those policies and procedures must give the firm reasonable assurance that relationships and engagements are undertaken or continued only where the stated conditions are met.
Statement 3: In this context reasonable assurance requires the firm to obtain an assurance from the client's those charged with governance that the client is honest.
Statement 4: The conditions - considered the integrity of the client, competence together with capabilities, time and resources, and the ability to comply with ethical requirements - must be met in relation to the relationship or engagement under consideration.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: Statements 1, 2 and 4 only
Statements 1, 3 and 4 only
Statements 2 and 3 only
Statements 1, 2, 3 and 4
questions.explanation: The element is framed as a requirement to establish policies and procedures producing reasonable assurance, so statements 1 and 2 are both faithful to the source, and statement 4 correctly lists the three conditions as they appear in the purpose clause. Statement 3 is wrong in two respects: the integrity of the client is something the firm itself considers through the seven enumerated matters, and the source does not convert that into a representation to be obtained from those charged with governance; nor does condition (a) demand proof of honesty. Statement 3 also misstates who bears the obligation, since reasonable assurance is what the firm's policies provide to the firm.

questions.question: Vega & Co. LLP, a firm of Chartered Accountants, was appointed statutory auditor of Nimbus Manufacturing Ltd for FY 2024-25 and the audit began in good faith after the normal client-acceptance procedures. Six weeks into the engagement the firm read a newspaper report confirming that the principal owner and Chairman of Nimbus had been convicted of money laundering two years earlier; this fact had not been disclosed and, had it been obtainable at the acceptance stage, would have caused the firm to decline the engagement. The engagement partner, Ms. Iyer, now considers what steps the firm should take, keeping in mind that the firm's quality-control manual sets out the matters to be addressed in connection with a possible withdrawal. Under SQC 1, which of the following best describes the firm's position upon learning of the conviction?
options: The firm is automatically and immediately obliged to resign both the audit engagement and the wider client relationship, without any further deliberation or analysis of the issues.
The firm can consider the possibility of withdrawing from the engagement as well as from the client relationship, addressing the specified issues before deciding.
Because the engagement was validly accepted at the start, the firm has no occasion to consider withdrawal and must complete the audit.
The firm may consider withdrawing only from the current engagement, the client relationship being outside the scope of this rule.
questions.explanation: SQC 1 provides that where a firm obtains information which, had it been obtainable earlier, would have caused it to decline the engagement, the firm can consider the possibility of withdrawing from the engagement AND the client relationship. The decisive fact is that the money-laundering conviction is precisely the kind of information that would have caused a decline at acceptance, so the trigger is met. The rule is framed as a possibility the firm may consider, not an automatic obligation, which rejects the first option that posits a forced immediate resignation. The scope expressly covers the client relationship as well, so the fourth option that limits withdrawal to the engagement alone is too narrow, and the third option is wrong because later-discovered information can validly reopen the acceptance judgment.

questions.question: Vega & Co. LLP, a firm of Chartered Accountants, was appointed statutory auditor of Nimbus Manufacturing Ltd for FY 2024-25 and the audit began in good faith after the normal client-acceptance procedures. Six weeks into the engagement the firm read a newspaper report confirming that the principal owner and Chairman of Nimbus had been convicted of money laundering two years earlier; this fact had not been disclosed and, had it been obtainable at the acceptance stage, would have caused the firm to decline the engagement. The engagement partner, Ms. Iyer, now considers what steps the firm should take, keeping in mind that the firm's quality-control manual sets out the matters to be addressed in connection with a possible withdrawal. Which of the following actions form part of the issues the firm's policies and procedures on withdrawal require it to address? 1. Discussing with Nimbus's management/those charged with governance the action the firm might take based on relevant facts and circumstances. 2. If the firm determines it is appropriate to withdraw, discussing with the appropriate level of management/those charged with governance the withdrawal and the reasons for it. 3. Informing every shareholder of Nimbus in writing of the reasons for the firm's possible departure. 4. Documenting significant issues, conclusions and the basis for those conclusions.
options: 1, 2 and 4 only
1, 3 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
All of 1, 2, 3 and 4
questions.explanation: The four issues listed in SQC 1 are discussing the action the firm might take with management/TCWG; where withdrawal is judged appropriate, discussing the withdrawal and its reasons with the appropriate level; considering whether a professional, regulatory or legal requirement exists to report to the regulatory authorities; and documenting significant issues, conclusions and the basis for conclusions. Statements 1, 2 and 4 each map onto those items and are therefore correct. Statement 3 is not part of the framework; SQC 1 addresses reporting to the regulatory authorities where required, not writing to every shareholder, so it is a distractor built on inflating a reporting duty to the wrong audience. Because only statements 1, 2 and 4 are supported, the option '1, 2 and 4 only' is the correct combination.

questions.question: Vega & Co. LLP, a firm of Chartered Accountants, was appointed statutory auditor of Nimbus Manufacturing Ltd for FY 2024-25 and the audit began in good faith after the normal client-acceptance procedures. Six weeks into the engagement the firm read a newspaper report confirming that the principal owner and Chairman of Nimbus had been convicted of money laundering two years earlier; this fact had not been disclosed and, had it been obtainable at the acceptance stage, would have caused the firm to decline the engagement. The engagement partner, Ms. Iyer, now considers what steps the firm should take, keeping in mind that the firm's quality-control manual sets out the matters to be addressed in connection with a possible withdrawal. Ms. Iyer asserts that once a firm decides to withdraw it must in all cases report the withdrawal to the regulatory authority. Under SQC 1, which response is most appropriate?
options: She is correct; there is an unconditional duty under SQC 1 to report every withdrawal to the regulator.
She is correct, but the duty to report arises only for listed entities such as Nimbus.
She is incorrect; the firm need only consider whether a professional, regulatory or legal requirement exists to report the withdrawal to the regulatory authorities.
She is incorrect; the reasons for withdrawal are discussed with the client alone, and the question of reporting a withdrawal to any external authority simply does not arise under this framework.
questions.explanation: SQC 1 frames the reporting element as a decision point: the firm must consider whether there is a professional, regulatory or legal requirement to report the withdrawal to the regulatory authorities. This is a conditional enquiry, not a blanket command, so the assertion of an unconditional duty in the first option overstates the rule and the second option invents a listed-company distinction the source does not draw. The fourth option under-reads the rule by denying that any reporting question arises at all, whereas the framework expressly requires the firm to consider the requirement. The decisive word is 'considering whether', which matches the third option.

questions.question: Vega & Co. LLP, a firm of Chartered Accountants, was appointed statutory auditor of Nimbus Manufacturing Ltd for FY 2024-25 and the audit began in good faith after the normal client-acceptance procedures. Six weeks into the engagement the firm read a newspaper report confirming that the principal owner and Chairman of Nimbus had been convicted of money laundering two years earlier; this fact had not been disclosed and, had it been obtainable at the acceptance stage, would have caused the firm to decline the engagement. The engagement partner, Ms. Iyer, now considers what steps the firm should take, keeping in mind that the firm's quality-control manual sets out the matters to be addressed in connection with a possible withdrawal. Regarding the discussion of the withdrawal and its reasons, which statement is correct under SQC 1?
options: Any discussion with the client about withdrawal is barred because it would breach confidentiality.
The reasons for withdrawal must be discussed with every employee of the client, irrespective of level, so that the whole organisation understands the firm's departure.
