Aspect (iii) covers the judgments made about materiality and significant risks, and the team's decision on the level of materiality and its reasoning is such a judgment, making it Matter 2. Option (a) reverses the two aspects; option (c) collapses them although the source lists them separately; option (d) misuses aspect (viii), which addresses the appropriateness of the report to be issued, not the underlying risk and materiality judgments. The distinction is between the risk assessment itself and the evaluation of the judgments behind it.

questions.question: Consider the following statements. Statement 1: Under aspect (i), the reviewer's function is to make a fresh, independent evaluation of the firm's compliance with independence requirements, which takes the place of any evaluation by the team. Statement 2: The significance considered under aspect (iv) extends to misstatements corrected by management as well as those left uncorrected. Statement 3: Completion of the engagement quality control review reduces the engagement partner's responsibility to the extent the reviewer concurs with the team's judgments. Statement 4: The reviewer considers whether appropriate consultation has taken place on difficult or contentious matters. Which of the above statements are incorrect?
options: Statements 2 and 4 only
Statements 1, 2 and 4 only
Statements 1 and 4 only
Statements 1 and 3 only
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect because aspect (i) directs the reviewer to the engagement team's evaluation of the firm's independence in relation to the specific engagement - the reviewer evaluates that evaluation rather than substituting a fresh one. Statement 3 is incorrect because SQC 1 expressly provides that the review does not reduce the responsibilities of the engagement partner, irrespective of the reviewer's concurrence. Statements 2 and 4 are correct: aspect (iv) covers corrected and uncorrected misstatements alike, and aspect (vii) requires the reviewer to consider whether appropriate consultation took place on difficult or contentious matters. The candidates must select the incorrect pair, which is 1 and 3 only.

questions.question: Palladium Retail Ltd. is a company whose equity shares are listed on a stock exchange. The audit of its financial statements for the year ended 31st March, 20X4 was conducted by M/s Vertika & Co., the engagement partner being CA Shubha Kale. CA Pradeep Mirashi, a partner in the firm's other office who is not part of the engagement team, was appointed as the engagement quality control reviewer. During the review, Pradeep observed that misstatements in inventory valuation aggregating to an amount close to materiality had been identified by the team but left uncorrected because management refused to record them, and he questioned the team's conclusion that only a summarized version of a related matter required to be reported needed to be communicated to the regulator and those charged with governance. Shubha considered the uncorrected misstatements to be acceptable on the strength of expected reversals in the next year, did not accept Pradeep's recommendations, and a difference of opinion arose among the engagement team, the engagement partner and the reviewer. The auditor's report was signed and issued on the same day without following any resolution process, and Pradeep did not sign any documentation of the review. Shubha later stated that since a reviewer could be appointed for a listed entity only if the firm chose, the firm had breached no requirement. Is Shubha's contention well-founded, and which option correctly reflects the position?
options: The contention is well-founded because SQC 1 leaves the review for listed entities to the firm's discretion; only the firm's own written quality control policies, and not the standard itself, could make such a review mandatory for a listed entity.

The contention is not well-founded: the review is mandatory for audits of the financial statements of listed entities, and once performed, its completion before issuance and the resolution of differences before issuance applied.
The contention is not well-founded because for a listed entity the reviewer must be a member of the engagement team, so the appointment itself was invalid.
The contention is well-founded because the firm had not adopted written policies on documentation of the review, and without such policies nothing could be documented or breached.
questions.explanation: For the audit of the financial statements of listed entities the engagement quality control review is mandatory, and it is optional only for any other engagement, so the partner's discretion argument fails. In addition, once a review is performed, it must be completed before the report is issued and any difference of opinion must be resolved before the report is issued, both of which were violated here. Option (a) wrongly treats the listed-entity review as optional; option (c) contradicts the definition, which requires the reviewer not to be part of the engagement team; option (d) confuses firm policy detail with the mandatory requirement itself.

questions.question: Palladium Retail Ltd. is a company whose equity shares are listed on a stock exchange. The audit of its financial statements for the year ended 31st March, 20X4 was conducted by M/s Vertika & Co., the engagement partner being CA Shubha Kale. CA Pradeep Mirashi, a partner in the firm's other office who is not part of the engagement team, was appointed as the engagement quality control reviewer. During the review, Pradeep observed that misstatements in inventory valuation aggregating to an amount close to materiality had been identified by the team but left uncorrected because management refused to record them, and he questioned the team's conclusion that only a summarized version of a related matter required to be reported needed to be communicated to the regulator and those charged with governance. Shubha considered the uncorrected misstatements to be acceptable on the strength of expected reversals in the next year, did not accept Pradeep's recommendations, and a difference of opinion arose among the engagement team, the engagement partner and the reviewer. The auditor's report was signed and issued on the same day without following any resolution process, and Pradeep did not sign any documentation of the review. Shubha later stated that since a reviewer could be appointed for a listed entity only if the firm chose, the firm had breached no requirement. Pradeep's two specific concerns map to which prescribed aspects of the engagement quality control review?
options: The inventory misstatements concern engages aspect (iv); the communication concern engages aspect (v).
The inventory misstatements concern engages aspect (iii); the communication concern engages aspect (viii).
Both concerns engage aspect (ii), because inventory valuation and regulatory reporting are significant risks.
The inventory misstatements concern engages aspect (vi); the communication concern engages aspect (i).
questions.explanation: Aspect (iv) requires consideration of the significance of corrected as well as uncorrected misstatements identified during the engagement, which squarely covers the uncorrected inventory valuation misstatements; aspect (v) covers matters to be communicated to management or those charged with governance and to regulatory bodies, which is the second concern. Option (b) mislabels them as materiality judgments and report appropriateness; option (c) confuses the identification of and response to significant risks with the evaluation of already-identified misstatements; option (d) maps them to working papers and independence, neither of which is in issue.

questions.question: Palladium Retail Ltd. is a company whose equity shares are listed on a stock exchange. The audit of its financial statements for the year ended 31st March, 20X4 was conducted by M/s Vertika & Co., the engagement partner being CA Shubha Kale. CA Pradeep Mirashi, a partner in the firm's other office who is not part of the engagement team, was appointed as the engagement quality control reviewer. During the review, Pradeep observed that misstatements in inventory valuation aggregating to an amount close to materiality had been identified by the team but left uncorrected because management refused to record them, and he questioned the team's conclusion that only a summarized version of a related matter required to be reported needed to be communicated to the regulator and those charged with governance. Shubha considered the uncorrected misstatements to be acceptable on the strength of expected reversals in the next year, did not accept Pradeep's recommendations, and a difference of opinion arose among the engagement team, the engagement partner and the reviewer. The auditor's report was signed and issued on the same day without following any resolution process, and Pradeep did not sign any documentation of the review. Shubha later stated that since a reviewer could be appointed for a listed entity only if the firm chose, the firm had breached no requirement. Based on the above case, which of the following actions should have been taken before the auditor's report was issued? Action 1: The difference of opinion should have been resolved under the established procedures, which may include consulting another practitioner or firm or a professional or regulatory body. Action 2: The engagement quality control review should have been completed before the report was issued. Action 3: Pradeep should have re-performed the valuation of the entire inventory to satisfy himself about the misstatements. Action 4: Pradeep should have documented that he was not aware of any unresolved matters, so as to close the review file.
options: Actions 1 and 2 only
Actions 1, 2 and 3 only
Actions 2 and 4 only
Actions 1, 2, 3 and 4
questions.explanation: Where there is a difference of opinion between the engagement team, the engagement partner and the reviewer, the report shall be issued only after the differences are resolved, and where the reviewer's recommendations are not accepted by the partner the matter is resolved by the established procedures, such as consulting another practitioner or firm or a professional or regulatory body; the review must also be completed before the report is issued. Action 3 misreads the review as a re-audit, whereas the reviewer evaluates the significant judgments and conclusions made by the team. Action 4 was impossible on these facts because Pradeep was aware of unresolved matters, and documentation must reflect the true position rather than close a file.

questions.question: Palladium Retail Ltd. is a company whose equity shares are listed on a stock exchange. The audit of its financial statements for the year ended 31st March, 20X4 was conducted by M/s Vertika & Co., the engagement partner being CA Shubha Kale. CA Pradeep Mirashi, a partner in the firm's other office who is not part of the engagement team, was appointed as the engagement quality control reviewer. During the review, Pradeep observed that misstatements in inventory valuation aggregating to an amount close to materiality had been identified by the team but left uncorrected because management refused to record them, and he questioned the team's conclusion that only a summarized version of a related matter required to be reported needed to be communicated to the regulator and those charged with governance. Shubha considered the uncorrected misstatements to be acceptable on the strength of expected reversals in the next year, did not accept Pradeep's recommendations, and a difference of opinion arose among the engagement team, the engagement partner and the reviewer. The auditor's report was signed and issued on the same day without following any resolution process, and Pradeep did not sign any documentation of the review. Shubha later stated that since a reviewer could be appointed for a listed entity only if the firm chose, the firm had breached no requirement. Which of the following statements about the documentation that the firm's policies should require the reviewer to make for the engagement reviewed is incorrect? Statement 1: Documentation that the procedures required by the firm's policies on quality control review have been performed. Statement 2: Documentation that the engagement quality control review has been completed before the report is issued. Statement 3: Documentation that the reviewer has independently recomputed the materiality applied by the engagement team. Statement 4: Documentation that the reviewer is not aware of any unresolved matters that would cause the reviewer to believe that the significant judgments and conclusions made by the engagement team were not appropriate.
options: Statements 1 and 2 only
Statements 2 and 4 only
Statements 1, 2 and 4 only
Statement 3 only
questions.explanation: SQC 1 prescribes exactly three documentation items for the engagement reviewed, corresponding to statements 1, 2 and 4: the required procedures performed, completion of the review before the report is issued, and the absence of unresolved matters casting doubt on the appropriateness of the team's significant judgments and conclusions. Nothing requires the reviewer to document an independent recomputation of materiality, and such a requirement would misstate the review as a re-performance exercise. Statements 1, 2 and 4 are each correct descriptions of the mandated documentation and therefore cannot be selected as incorrect.

questions.question: Palladium Retail Ltd. is a company whose equity shares are listed on a stock exchange. The audit of its financial statements for the year ended 31st March, 20X4 was conducted by M/s Vertika & Co., the engagement partner being CA Shubha Kale. CA Pradeep Mirashi, a partner in the firm's other office who is not part of the engagement team, was appointed as the engagement quality control reviewer. During the review, Pradeep observed that misstatements in inventory valuation aggregating to an amount close to materiality had been identified by the team but left uncorrected because management refused to record them, and he questioned the team's conclusion that only a summarized version of a related matter required to be reported needed to be communicated to the regulator and those charged with governance. Shubha considered the uncorrected misstatements to be acceptable on the strength of expected reversals in the next year, did not accept Pradeep's recommendations, and a difference of opinion arose among the engagement team, the engagement partner and the reviewer. The auditor's report was signed and issued on the same day without following any resolution process, and Pradeep did not sign any documentation of the review. Shubha later stated that since a reviewer could be appointed for a listed entity only if the firm chose, the firm had breached no requirement. Assertion (A): Pradeep could not have honestly documented that he was not aware of any unresolved matters. Reason (R): A difference of opinion between the engagement team, the engagement partner and the reviewer regarding the significance of the uncorrected misstatements and the required communications remained outstanding when the report was issued.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is incorrect.
A is incorrect but R is correct.
questions.explanation: The third documentation item requires the reviewer to record that he is not aware of any unresolved matters that would cause him to believe the significant judgments and conclusions made by the engagement team were not appropriate. The outstanding differences over the uncorrected inventory misstatements and the scope of the communications are precisely such unresolved matters, so R is correct and it explains why A follows. Pradeep's failure to sign any documentation cannot be cured by asserting a state of knowledge he did not possess, and the reviewer's documentation obligation presupposes the true position on the review date.

questions.question: Palladium Retail Ltd. is a company whose equity shares are listed on a stock exchange. The audit of its financial statements for the year ended 31st March, 20X4 was conducted by M/s Vertika & Co., the engagement partner being CA Shubha Kale. CA Pradeep Mirashi, a partner in the firm's other office who is not part of the engagement team, was appointed as the engagement quality control reviewer. During the review, Pradeep observed that misstatements in inventory valuation aggregating to an amount close to materiality had been identified by the team but left uncorrected because management refused to record them, and he questioned the team's conclusion that only a summarized version of a related matter required to be reported needed to be communicated to the regulator and those charged with governance. Shubha considered the uncorrected misstatements to be acceptable on the strength of expected reversals in the next year, did not accept Pradeep's recommendations, and a difference of opinion arose among the engagement team, the engagement partner and the reviewer. The auditor's report was signed and issued on the same day without following any resolution process, and Pradeep did not sign any documentation of the review. Shubha later stated that since a reviewer could be appointed for a listed entity only if the firm chose, the firm had breached no requirement. Which of the following statements about the review in the above case are correct? Statement 1: The review is a process for evaluating the significant judgments and conclusions made by the engagement team, not a re-audit of the engagement. Statement 2: The auditor's report could be issued only after the resolution of the differences of opinion. Statement 3: Since the engagement partner has overall responsibility for the audit, her conclusion prevails over the reviewer's once she documents her reasons. Statement 4: Where the reviewer's recommendations are not accepted by the engagement partner, the matter is to be resolved by the established procedures, such as by consulting another practitioner or firm or a professional or regulatory body.
options: Statements 1 and 3 only
Statements 2, 3 and 4 only
Statements 1, 2, 3 and 4
Statements 1, 2 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statement 1 restates the definition of the review, statement 2 restates the rule that the report shall be issued only after resolution of differences between the engagement team, the engagement partner and the reviewer, and statement 4 restates the established-procedures route including consultation of another practitioner or firm or a professional or regulatory body. Statement 3 is wrong: although the review does not reduce the engagement partner's responsibility, her overriding authority is not a substitute for resolution of the difference before issuance. Documenting her own reasons does not convert an unresolved difference into a resolved one.

questions.question: Nirman Constructions Ltd. is a listed entity whose financial statements were audited by M/s Ashwini Deshpande & Co. The engagement team included CA Faisal Qureshi, an experienced valuer in the firm, whom the engagement partner consulted repeatedly on the fair valuation of a road asset acquired in a complex exchange transaction and on the related disclosure judgments. Faisal prepared the technical valuation note that formed the basis of the team's conclusion and drafted the working paper dealing with the significant risk in the valuation. After the fieldwork concluded, the firm appointed Faisal as the engagement quality control reviewer for the audit, and he evaluated the team's judgments about materiality, the consultation carried out on the valuation and the appropriateness of the draft auditor's report, completing his review a few hours before the report was issued. In his documentation Faisal recorded that the procedures required by the firm's policies had been performed, that the review was completed before the report was issued and that he was not aware of any unresolved matters. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion about the review?
options: The review was valid because a reviewer need only have sufficient experience to evaluate the significant judgments, Faisal plainly had it, and his prior involvement with the engagement goes only to weight, not to eligibility.
The review was valid because consultation of a person by the engagement partner during the engagement is permissible and Faisal did nothing more.

The appointment was improper because a person who is part of the engagement team and who participated by preparing the valuation note cannot act as reviewer; participation must be avoided at all costs.
The appointment was improper only because a reviewer is not permitted to evaluate judgments about materiality.
questions.explanation: The reviewer must be a chartered accountant who is not part of the engagement team, and to maintain objectivity participation in the engagement is to be avoided at all costs. Faisal was a member of the team and his valuation note formed the basis of the very conclusion he later reviewed, so he would have been evaluating his own work. Option (b) misapplies the permissible-consultation rule: being consulted by the partner is allowed, but preparing engagement working papers is participation, not consultation. Option (d) is wrong because evaluation of the judgments made about materiality is a prescribed aspect of the review itself.

questions.question: Nirman Constructions Ltd. is a listed entity whose financial statements were audited by M/s Ashwini Deshpande & Co. The engagement team included CA Faisal Qureshi, an experienced valuer in the firm, whom the engagement partner consulted repeatedly on the fair valuation of a road asset acquired in a complex exchange transaction and on the related disclosure judgments. Faisal prepared the technical valuation note that formed the basis of the team's conclusion and drafted the working paper dealing with the significant risk in the valuation. After the fieldwork concluded, the firm appointed Faisal as the engagement quality control reviewer for the audit, and he evaluated the team's judgments about materiality, the consultation carried out on the valuation and the appropriateness of the draft auditor's report, completing his review a few hours before the report was issued. In his documentation Faisal recorded that the procedures required by the firm's policies had been performed, that the review was completed before the report was issued and that he was not aware of any unresolved matters. Ignoring the defect in the appointment, Faisal's three evaluation subjects - the materiality judgments, the consultation carried out on the valuation, and the appropriateness of the draft auditor's report - correspond respectively to which prescribed aspects of the review?
options: Aspects (ii), (vii) and (viii)
Aspects (iii), (vii) and (viii)
Aspects (iii), (vi) and (v)
Aspects (i), (iv) and (viii)
questions.explanation: The judgments made about materiality and significant risks are aspect (iii); whether appropriate consultation has taken place on difficult or contentious matters - the valuation being contentious - is aspect (vii); and the appropriateness of the report to be issued is aspect (viii). Option (a) substitutes aspect (ii), which addresses the identified significant risks and the responses to them, not the materiality judgments; option (c) mistakes the consultation subject for the working-papers aspect (vi) and the report subject for the communications aspect (v); option (d) invokes independence and misstatements, which are not the subjects described.

questions.question: Nirman Constructions Ltd. is a listed entity whose financial statements were audited by M/s Ashwini Deshpande & Co. The engagement team included CA Faisal Qureshi, an experienced valuer in the firm, whom the engagement partner consulted repeatedly on the fair valuation of a road asset acquired in a complex exchange transaction and on the related disclosure judgments. Faisal prepared the technical valuation note that formed the basis of the team's conclusion and drafted the working paper dealing with the significant risk in the valuation. After the fieldwork concluded, the firm appointed Faisal as the engagement quality control reviewer for the audit, and he evaluated the team's judgments about materiality, the consultation carried out on the valuation and the appropriateness of the draft auditor's report, completing his review a few hours before the report was issued. In his documentation Faisal recorded that the procedures required by the firm's policies had been performed, that the review was completed before the report was issued and that he was not aware of any unresolved matters. On the assumption that the appointment question is kept out of view, how do Faisal's three documentation entries stand under SQC 1?
options: They are deficient because he must further document that he independently recomputed the materiality levels applied by the team.
They are deficient because he must further document the outcome of the firm's monitoring inspections of the engagement.
Only the first entry is required; documenting completion before the report is issued is the engagement partner's task.
They are the complete set of matters the reviewer must document for the engagement reviewed.
questions.explanation: SQC 1 requires the reviewer to document three things for the engagement reviewed: that the procedures required by the firm's policies on quality control review have been performed, that the review was completed before the report is issued, and that the reviewer is not aware of any unresolved matters that would cause him to believe the team's significant judgments and conclusions were not appropriate. Faisal recorded all three, so nothing further is prescribed by the source; options (a) and (b) invent documentation requirements that the standard does not impose, and option (c) wrongly transfers the completion entry to the partner.

questions.question: Nirman Constructions Ltd. is a listed entity whose financial statements were audited by M/s Ashwini Deshpande & Co. The engagement team included CA Faisal Qureshi, an experienced valuer in the firm, whom the engagement partner consulted repeatedly on the fair valuation of a road asset acquired in a complex exchange transaction and on the related disclosure judgments. Faisal prepared the technical valuation note that formed the basis of the team's conclusion and drafted the working paper dealing with the significant risk in the valuation. After the fieldwork concluded, the firm appointed Faisal as the engagement quality control reviewer for the audit, and he evaluated the team's judgments about materiality, the consultation carried out on the valuation and the appropriateness of the draft auditor's report, completing his review a few hours before the report was issued. In his documentation Faisal recorded that the procedures required by the firm's policies had been performed, that the review was completed before the report was issued and that he was not aware of any unresolved matters. Suppose Faisal was never part of the engagement team, prepared no valuation note and drafted no working paper, and the only change is that the partner consulted him during the engagement on the valuation approach. Is he then eligible to act as the reviewer?
options: No, because any consultation during the engagement converts the reviewer into a member of the engagement team.
Yes, because the engagement partner may consult the reviewer during the engagement without compromising objectivity, and mere consultation is not participation in the engagement.
Yes, but only if his consultation advice is documented in the engagement working papers as a team judgment.

No, because a reviewer who has been consulted on a matter is disqualified from evaluating that matter in the review; his review would in substance be a review of his own advice to the engagement team.
questions.explanation: The source distinguishes participation in the engagement, which must be avoided at all costs to preserve the reviewer's objectivity, from consultation, which it expressly permits: the engagement partner may consult the reviewer during the engagement without compromising objectivity. With the participation facts removed, Faisal is a chartered accountant outside the engagement team with sufficient experience, so he satisfies the definition of reviewer. Options (a) and (d) erase the express permission to consult, and option (c) invents a documentation precondition found nowhere in the provisions.

questions.question: Nirman Constructions Ltd. is a listed entity whose financial statements were audited by M/s Ashwini Deshpande & Co. The engagement team included CA Faisal Qureshi, an experienced valuer in the firm, whom the engagement partner consulted repeatedly on the fair valuation of a road asset acquired in a complex exchange transaction and on the related disclosure judgments. Faisal prepared the technical valuation note that formed the basis of the team's conclusion and drafted the working paper dealing with the significant risk in the valuation. After the fieldwork concluded, the firm appointed Faisal as the engagement quality control reviewer for the audit, and he evaluated the team's judgments about materiality, the consultation carried out on the valuation and the appropriateness of the draft auditor's report, completing his review a few hours before the report was issued. In his documentation Faisal recorded that the procedures required by the firm's policies had been performed, that the review was completed before the report was issued and that he was not aware of any unresolved matters. Assertion (A): A review completed a few hours before issuance of the report is not objectionable on timing grounds alone. Reason (R): The requirement is that the engagement quality control review be completed before the report is issued; no minimum gap between completion and issuance is prescribed. Which of the following is correct?
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is incorrect.
A is incorrect because the reviewer's documentation must precede the completion of fieldwork.
A is incorrect because completion must precede issuance by a period fixed in the firm's engagement plan.
questions.explanation: The source requires documentation that the review was completed before the report is issued and says nothing about the length of the interval, so a completion a few hours before issuance satisfies the timing rule on its face and R correctly explains A. Any minimum lead time would be a firm policy choice, not a requirement of SQC 1, so options (d) and (e) import conditions the source does not state. Option (b) fails because the absence of a prescribed gap is the very reason the timing is unobjectionable, even though other defects in the appointment may remain.

questions.question: Meridian Finance Corporation is a private non-banking finance company whose equity shares are not listed on any stock exchange. Its audit for the year ended 31st March, 20X4 was undertaken by M/s Kamesh Rao & Associates. The engagement partner, CA Kamesh Rao, appointed CA Ananya Bhat, a member of the firm's Pune branch who is not part of the engagement team and who has sixteen years of experience in auditing non-banking finance companies, as the engagement quality control reviewer; her brother-in-law is the audit manager of the engagement team. Since Meridian is unlisted, the firm's policy treats the review as optional, but the partner chose to have it performed because of the high-risk loan portfolio. Ananya restricted her work to evaluating the significant judgments and conclusions made by the engagement team and did not re-perform audit procedures. During the engagement, the partner consulted her on the provisioning judgment for one stressed account and recorded his own conclusion after the discussion. The review was completed two days before the audit report was signed and issued. Mr. Rao later remarked to a peer reviewer that since Ananya had evaluated and concurred in the significant judgments, his own responsibility for the audit stood correspondingly reduced. Which of the following is the correct position on whether the engagement quality control review was required for the audit of Meridian's financial statements?
options: The review is mandatory for every audit of financial statements, so the firm's characterization of it as optional was itself a breach.
The review is optional for unlisted companies, and since it was performed voluntarily, the firm was free to complete it even after the report was issued.
The review becomes mandatory for an unlisted company whenever the engagement involves significant risks, as Meridian's high-risk portfolio does.

The review is mandatory only for the audit of the financial statements of listed entities and optional for any other engagement; for Meridian it was a voluntary decision of the firm rather than a requirement of SQC 1.
questions.explanation: SQC 1 requires the engagement quality control review for audits of the financial statements of listed entities and makes it optional for any other engagement, so for the unlisted Meridian the review was the firm's voluntary choice. Option (b) is the trap: performing the review voluntarily does not free the firm from the rule that the review be completed before the report is issued, a requirement that attaches to the review itself whenever performed. Options (a) and (c) extend the mandatory trigger beyond listed entities to all audits or to high-risk engagements, which the source does not provide.

Which of the following is the correct position regarding Ananya Bhat's eligibility to act as reviewer?
options: She is not eligible because the reviewer must be a partner of the firm.
She is not eligible because a member of her immediate family is part of the engagement team.

She is eligible because the reviewer may be any chartered accountant, other than a person who is part of the engagement team, with sufficient experience to evaluate the significant judgments and conclusions made by the team.
She is eligible only if she was wholly unconnected with the firm's operations in the audit of financial statements of non-banking finance companies.
questions.explanation: The definition requires only a chartered accountant who is not part of the engagement team and has sufficient experience; no partner status is needed, so option (a) fails and option (c) is satisfied by Ananya's sixteen years of relevant experience. The brother-in-law fact is a deliberate distraction: on these facts she is not part of the engagement team, and the quoted definition does not disqualify her for family relationships. Option (d) invents an exclusion from industry experience that the source does not state; indeed sufficient relevant experience is precisely what the definition demands.

It is permissible, because the engagement partner may consult the engagement quality control reviewer during the engagement without compromising the reviewer's objectivity.

Option (a) collapses the distinction; option (c) inverts the rule by making dependence on the advice the condition of propriety; option (d) states a sequencing restriction the source does not impose.

It is correct, because a voluntarily performed review reduces the partner's responsibility in the same way as a mandatory one once concurrence is recorded.

Which of the following statements about the review performed on Meridian are correct? Statement 1: The requirement that the review be completed before the report is issued did not apply because the review was voluntary. Statement 2: The review being a process for evaluating the significant judgments and conclusions made by the engagement team, Ananya was not required to re-perform audit procedures. Statement 3: Ananya should document that the procedures required by the firm's policies on quality control review have been performed and that the review was completed before the report was issued. Statement 4: Ananya should document that she is not aware of any unresolved matters that would cause her to believe that the significant judgments and conclusions made by the engagement team were not appropriate.
options: Statements 2, 3 and 4 only
Statements 1 and 3 only
Statements 1, 2 and 4 only
Statements 2 and 3 only
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect: the requirement that the review be completed before the report is issued, and the associated documentation requirements, attach to the review itself once the firm performs it, whether mandatory for a listed entity or voluntary for any other engagement. Statements 2, 3 and 4 correctly restate the nature of the review and two of the three matters the reviewer must document for the engagement reviewed - performance of the firm's required procedures, completion before issuance, and absence of unresolved matters casting doubt on the team's significant judgments and conclusions. questions.question: Match the situations with the correct consequence drawn from the engagement quality control review provisions. Column I: (A) After the reviewer's evaluation begins, the engagement partner and the reviewer disagree about the significance of an uncorrected misstatement. (B) The reviewer notices that the memorandum recording the team's materiality judgment is not among the working papers selected for review. (C) The reviewer completed the review three days before the report was issued, the firm's required procedures having been performed and documented. (D) During fieldwork the engagement partner seeks the reviewer's views on a contentious revenue recognition treatment. Column II: (1) This is permissible consultation and does not compromise the reviewer's objectivity. (2) The report shall be issued only after the difference is resolved. (3) The timing of the review is consistent with the requirement that it be completed before the report is issued. (4) The reviewer raises the aspect concerning whether the working papers selected for review reflect the work performed for significant judgments. Select the correct match.
questions.explanation: A difference between the partner and the reviewer must be resolved before the report is issued, so A pairs with 2; the missing materiality memorandum goes to the aspect on whether the working papers selected for review reflect the work performed for significant judgments, so B pairs with 4; completion three days before issuance satisfies the completion-before-issuance requirement, so C pairs with 3; and consulting the reviewer during the engagement is expressly permitted without compromising objectivity, so D pairs with 1. The other options confuse consultation with working-paper selection or misattribute the consultation consequence.

questions.question: Arrange the following events in the order in which they must stand at the completion of a compliant engagement quality control review of a listed company's audit, where the reviewer raised a concern that the engagement partner did not initially accept. Event 1: The reviewer evaluates the engagement team's significant judgments and conclusions. Event 2: The difference of opinion is resolved through the established procedures, such as consulting another practitioner or firm or a professional or regulatory body. Event 3: The reviewer documents that the review has been completed before the report is issued. Event 4: The auditor's report is issued.
questions.explanation: The evaluation of significant judgments and conclusions comes first; the review cannot be treated as complete, and the reviewer cannot document the absence of unresolved matters, while the difference persists, so resolution stands between the evaluation and documented completion; and issuance of the report comes last, because the review must be completed before the report is issued and the report may be issued only after the differences are resolved. Option (b) wrongly completes the review before resolution; option (d) wrongly issues the report before the completion documentation; option (c) resolves the difference before any evaluation, reversing cause and effect.

questions.question: During the audit of a listed entity, the engagement quality control reviewer asks for the memorandum in which the engagement team recorded how it arrived at its materiality judgment. The engagement manager objects that the reviewer's role is confined to a summary memorandum prepared for reviewers and cannot extend to the team's working papers. Which of the following is the most appropriate response?
options: The manager is right; the reviewer's access is confined to the summary memoranda which the team prepares for the purposes of the review and does not extend to the engagement working paper file.
The manager is right; the reviewer evaluates only the conclusions in the final report and not the papers supporting them.
The manager is wrong; the review includes considering whether the working papers selected for review reflect the work performed for significant judgments.
The manager is wrong, but the reviewer's demand should instead be treated as consultation on a contentious matter under aspect (vii).
questions.explanation: Among the prescribed aspects is whether the working papers selected for review reflect the work performed for the significant judgments, so a reviewer examining the paper trail behind a significant materiality judgment is acting squarely within the review. Option (a) invents a restriction to summary memoranda that the provisions do not state; option (b) misreads the review as an evaluation of the final report alone, whereas it evaluates the team's significant judgments and conclusions; option (d) misclassifies the inspection as consultation, which concerns difficult or contentious matters referred by the team.

questions.question: In documenting an engagement quality control review, a reviewer records a statement modeled on the third documentation requirement of SQC 1. Which formulation best captures what that requirement asks the reviewer to record?
options: That the reviewer personally agrees with each and every judgment exercised by the engagement team.
That no misstatement identified during the engagement remains uncorrected at the review date.
That the reviewer is not aware of any unresolved matters that would cause the reviewer to believe that the significant judgments and conclusions made by the engagement team were not appropriate.
That all differences of opinion with the engagement partner have been settled in the reviewer's favour.
questions.explanation: The third documentation item is worded as the absence of unresolved matters that would cause the reviewer to believe the team's significant judgments and conclusions were not appropriate; it is a negative comfort standard about unresolved matters, not a positive ratification of every judgment. Option (a) overstates the standard by requiring agreement with every judgment; option (b) confuses the documentation with the separate aspect on corrected and uncorrected misstatements, whose significance is evaluated rather than required to be nil; option (d) distorts the concept of unresolved matters, which must be resolved through established procedures before issuance rather than adjudicated in anyone's favour.

questions.question:
Case: Gandhi, Kale & Associates is a chartered accountants' firm with a documented system of quality control. For the statutory audit of Apex Metals Limited for the year ended 31 March 2024, significant audit procedures were completed on 30 June 2024, the auditor's report was dated 31 July 2024 and the annual general meeting was held on 20 September 2024. The final engagement file was assembled and closed on 20 September 2024. While reviewing the file, engagement partner Mr. Salunkhe noted that assembly fell 82 days after completion of fieldwork and recorded a concern that the 60-day deadline had been breached. In the same engagement an audit senior scanned about 400 pages of physical checklists and confirmations into the electronic engagement file; the scans did not capture entries recorded on the reverse side of two balance confirmations, the scanned images were neither indexed nor signed, and the archive format in use does not allow a scanned page to be printed. Separately, Zenith Textiles Limited, audited by the firm for the year 2019-20 with the auditor's report dated 30 June 2020, wrote in October 2024 demanding delivery of the original working papers for that audit on the ground that it had paid audit fees of Rs. 18 lakh; and Mr. Salunkhe, who resigned on 15 November 2024 to join another firm, offered to carry away the engagement files of the assignments he had signed. The firm's written retention policy provides for destruction of audit documentation five years after the date of the auditor's report.

With reference to Mr. Salunkhe's concern about the timing of assembly of the Apex Metals engagement file, which of the following is the MOST APPROPRIATE conclusion?
options: The concern is valid, because the 60-day period for completing the engagement file runs from completion of significant audit procedures on 30 June 2024, so assembly on 20 September 2024 fell 82 days later and outside it, the date of the auditor's report being relevant only to the retention of documentation.

The concern is not valid, because for an audit engagement the file must be completed within 60 days after the date of the auditor's report, that is by 29 September 2024, and assembly on 20 September 2024 was 51 days after that date and therefore within time.
The concern is not valid, because the clock for audit engagements starts from the date of the annual general meeting at which the financial statements are adopted.
The concern is valid in substance, because SQC 1 prescribes no fixed period for audit engagements and requires only assembly on a timely basis, and 82 days is not timely.
questions.explanation: SQC 1 requires the firm to establish policies and procedures to complete assembly of final engagement files on a timely basis after engagement reports have been finalized, and for audit engagements that general requirement is quantified as completion within 60 days after the date of the auditor's report. The decisive date is therefore 31 July 2024, making 29 September 2024 the last permissible day; assembly on 20 September 2024 was 51 days after the report date and so complied. The partner's 82-day computation uses the completion of fieldwork as the start date, which is the right rule applied to the wrong date. The date of the AGM is likewise irrelevant to assembly, and the fourth option wrongly discards the specific 60-day period prescribed for audit engagements in favour of the general timeliness wording, which governs only engagements for which no period is specified.

All of the above
questions.explanation: Where original paper documentation is electronically scanned for inclusion in engagement files, SQC 1 requires the firm's procedures to make the engagement teams generate scanned copies reflecting the full content of the original documentation, integrate them into the engagement files including indexing and signing, and enable the scanned copies to be retrieved and printed. Actions 1, 3 and 4 correspond exactly to those three requirements, and each is presently unmet in the case: the reverse-side entries are lost, nothing is indexed or signed, and the archive cannot print a page. Action 2 is wrong and would in fact defeat the requirement of safe custody of engagement documentation, which belongs to the firm; scanning is a means of building the file, not a means of parting with the underlying record. The two options that include Action 2 are therefore incorrect despite containing other correct steps.

Based on the above case, which of the following statements are correct?

WHAT CHANGES IF: assume that instead of 20 September 2024, the final engagement file for Apex Metals was assembled on 25 October 2024, every other fact remaining unchanged. Which of the following is the MOST APPROPRIATE conclusion?
