The first option imports the AGM as the reference date, which the requirement does not use. The second and third options confuse the two distinct documentation obligations: the 60-day period is the assembly deadline, while the seven-year period is the minimum retention period; keeping a file for seven years does not cure a file assembled after the deadline.

questions.question:
Case: Gandhi, Kale & Associates is a chartered accountants' firm with a documented system of quality control. For the statutory audit of Apex Metals Limited for the year ended 31 March 2024, significant audit procedures were completed on 30 June 2024, the auditor's report was dated 31 July 2024 and the annual general meeting was held on 20 September 2024. The final engagement file was assembled and closed on 20 September 2024. While reviewing the file, engagement partner Mr. Salunkhe noted that assembly fell 82 days after completion of fieldwork and recorded a concern that the 60-day deadline had been breached. In the same engagement an audit senior scanned about 400 pages of physical checklists and confirmations into the electronic engagement file; the scans did not capture entries recorded on the reverse side of two balance confirmations, the scanned images were neither indexed nor signed, and the archive format in use does not allow a scanned page to be printed. Separately, Zenith Textiles Limited, audited by the firm for the year 2019-20 with the auditor's report dated 30 June 2020, wrote in October 2024 demanding delivery of the original working papers for that audit on the ground that it had paid audit fees of Rs. 18 lakh; and Mr. Salunkhe, who resigned on 15 November 2024 to join another firm, offered to carry away the engagement files of the assignments he had signed. The firm's written retention policy provides for destruction of audit documentation five years after the date of the auditor's report.

Based on the above case, which of the following statements about the firm's arrangements for the safety and accessibility of engagement documentation are correct?
Statement 1: Storing the scanned images on a managed server is by itself sufficient to satisfy the requirements of accessibility and retrievability.
Statement 2: Omitting the entries on the reverse side of the confirmations defeats the requirement that scanned copies reflect the full content of the original documentation.
Statement 3: Leaving the scanned copies un-indexed and unsigned fails the requirement to integrate the scanned copies into the engagement files.
Statement 4: Using an archive format from which a scanned page cannot be printed is acceptable, because the image can still be read on screen.
options: 1 and 4 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: The safety and accessibility requirement asks for policies designed to maintain safe custody, integrity, accessibility and retrievability of engagement documentation, and where paper is scanned the firm's procedures must secure full-content copies, integration into the files including indexing and signing, and the ability to retrieve and print scanned copies. Statements 2 and 3 are correct because two of those specific conditions are unmet in the Apex Metals file. Statement 1 is incorrect because mere hosting of images does not establish accessibility and retrievability when the arrangement cannot deliver the scanned copy back in usable form; a server that cannot produce the page is not a compliant archive. Statement 4 is incorrect for the same reason, since the ability to print a scanned copy is expressly part of the requirement and is not satisfied by on-screen readability alone.

questions.question:
Case: Kulkarni & Deshpande is a firm of chartered accountants with eleven partners. Its internal quality-control memorandum records the following arrangements. (1) Responsibility for the monitoring process is entrusted to a person undergoing articleship who has completed two years of training, on the view that he is close to day-to-day work. (2) The memorandum states that monitoring stands completed once written policies and procedures have been framed, since the existence of written policies itself gives reasonable assurance. (3) A letter from a supplier of one of the firm's audit clients alleged that the firm's staff had accepted gifts prohibited by professional standards; the managing partner filed the letter without inquiry on the ground that it came from outside the firm, is unauthenticated, and no register of complaints exists. (4) Audit assistant Sneha suspects that a misstatement of Rs. 1.4 crore, identified during the audit of a major fee-paying client, was removed from the summary of misstatements; her only available route is to discuss it with the same engagement partner whose work she questions, and she fears losing her posting if she speaks. (5) In an earlier matter an investigation concluded that the firm's audit of a cooperative bank had not complied with professional standards; the firm closed the file with no further action because that client accounts for close to a fifth of its fees.

Based on the above case, which of the following statements are correct?
Statement 1: Arrangement (1) is inconsistent with the monitoring factor that requires responsibility for the monitoring process to be entrusted to a partner or other experienced person in the firm.
Statement 2: Arrangement (1) is acceptable, because a person close to day-to-day work is the best placed to monitor the quality control of engagements.
Statement 3: Arrangement (2) is inconsistent with monitoring, which must provide reasonable assurance that the policies and procedures relating to the system of quality control are operating effectively.
Statement 4: Monitoring is complete once the firm has decided whether its quality control system has been effectively implemented, no other factor being relevant.
options: 1 and 3 only
2 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
1, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Monitoring under SQC 1 is directed at providing reasonable assurance that the firm's policies and procedures relating to its system of quality control are operating effectively, so the mere existence of written policies stated in arrangement (2) does not discharge it and statement 3 is correct. Responsibility for the monitoring process is to be entrusted to a partner or other experienced person in the firm; a second-year article assistant is neither, so statement 1 is correct and statement 2, which substitutes proximity to daily work for the experience criterion, is not. Statement 4 is incorrect because deciding whether the system has been effectively implemented is only one of five factors, the others including dealing with complaints and allegations, taking action on identified deficiencies or non-compliance, and taking appropriate action against personnel who did not conform to the quality control policies.

questions.question:
Case: Kulkarni & Deshpande is a firm of chartered accountants with eleven partners. Its internal quality-control memorandum records the following arrangements. (1) Responsibility for the monitoring process is entrusted to a person undergoing articleship who has completed two years of training, on the view that he is close to day-to-day work. (2) The memorandum states that monitoring stands completed once written policies and procedures have been framed, since the existence of written policies itself gives reasonable assurance. (3) A letter from a supplier of one of the firm's audit clients alleged that the firm's staff had accepted gifts prohibited by professional standards; the managing partner filed the letter without inquiry on the ground that it came from outside the firm, is unauthenticated, and no register of complaints exists. (4) Audit assistant Sneha suspects that a misstatement of Rs. 1.4 crore, identified during the audit of a major fee-paying client, was removed from the summary of misstatements; her only available route is to discuss it with the same engagement partner whose work she questions, and she fears losing her posting if she speaks. (5) In an earlier matter an investigation concluded that the firm's audit of a cooperative bank had not complied with professional standards; the firm closed the file with no further action because that client accounts for close to a fifth of its fees.

With reference to arrangement (3), which of the following is the MOST APPROPRIATE analysis of the firm's obligations?
options: The firm need not investigate, because an allegation by a supplier of a client cannot relate to work performed by the firm.

The matter is a complaint or allegation that work performed by the firm fails to comply with professional standards and regulatory and legal requirements; complaints and allegations may originate from within or outside the firm and may be made by firm personnel, clients or other third parties, so the firm must investigate it in accordance with its established policies and procedures.

The matter falls only within the category of allegations of non-compliance with the firm's system of quality control, in that it concerns the conduct of the firm's staff rather than the sufficiency of the evidence obtained, so it is relevant to monitoring alone, the appropriate response being a review of whether the system has been effectively implemented and no investigation of the specific allegation being called for.
The firm's procedures are engaged only by complaints raised by its own personnel, since third parties have no standing to complain.
questions.explanation: Alleging that the firm's staff accepted gifts prohibited by professional standards is an allegation that work performed by the firm fails to comply with professional standards and regulatory and legal requirements, which is category (a) of the matters the firm's policies must address. The source expressly states that complaints and allegations may originate from within or outside the firm and may be made by firm personnel, clients or other third parties, so neither the supplier's outside position, nor the absence of authentication, nor the lack of a complaint register excuses the firm from investigating under established procedures. The third option misclassifies the subject matter as a system-of-quality-control allegation; such an allegation would instead concern non-compliance with the firm's own system, which this letter does not describe. The fourth option wrongly restricts the permissible sources of complaints.

questions.question:
Case: Kulkarni & Deshpande is a firm of chartered accountants with eleven partners. Its internal quality-control memorandum records the following arrangements. (1) Responsibility for the monitoring process is entrusted to a person undergoing articleship who has completed two years of training, on the view that he is close to day-to-day work. (2) The memorandum states that monitoring stands completed once written policies and procedures have been framed, since the existence of written policies itself gives reasonable assurance. (3) A letter from a supplier of one of the firm's audit clients alleged that the firm's staff had accepted gifts prohibited by professional standards; the managing partner filed the letter without inquiry on the ground that it came from outside the firm, is unauthenticated, and no register of complaints exists. (4) Audit assistant Sneha suspects that a misstatement of Rs. 1.4 crore, identified during the audit of a major fee-paying client, was removed from the summary of misstatements; her only available route is to discuss it with the same engagement partner whose work she questions, and she fears losing her posting if she speaks. (5) In an earlier matter an investigation concluded that the firm's audit of a cooperative bank had not complied with professional standards; the firm closed the file with no further action because that client accounts for close to a fifth of its fees.

Based on the above case, which of the following actions are consistent with SQC 1 in dealing with the situation described in arrangement (4)?
Action 1: Establish clearly defined channels through which firm personnel may raise a concern without fear.
Action 2: Require Sneha to obtain the concurrence of the engagement partner whose work she questions before she uses any channel.
Action 3: Investigate the allegation in accordance with established policies and procedures, with the investigation supervised by a partner with sufficient experience and authority.
Action 4: Defer any investigation until the client's fee terms for the next period have been settled.
options: 2 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Sneha's problem is precisely the one the requirement addresses: the firm must establish clearly defined channels for firm personnel to raise a concern without fear, and a concern that has no route other than the person whose work is questioned does not meet that description. Action 3 is also required, because complaints and allegations are to be investigated per established policies and procedures under the supervision of a partner with sufficient experience and authority. Action 2 defeats the 'without fear' element by interposing the subject of the allegation as a gatekeeper. Action 4 makes the firm's quality-control response contingent on fee considerations, which the requirement does not permit, so the two options containing either action are incorrect even though they also list Action 1 or 3.

questions.question:
Case: Kulkarni & Deshpande is a firm of chartered accountants with eleven partners. Its internal quality-control memorandum records the following arrangements. (1) Responsibility for the monitoring process is entrusted to a person undergoing articleship who has completed two years of training, on the view that he is close to day-to-day work. (2) The memorandum states that monitoring stands completed once written policies and procedures have been framed, since the existence of written policies itself gives reasonable assurance. (3) A letter from a supplier of one of the firm's audit clients alleged that the firm's staff had accepted gifts prohibited by professional standards; the managing partner filed the letter without inquiry on the ground that it came from outside the firm, is unauthenticated, and no register of complaints exists. (4) Audit assistant Sneha suspects that a misstatement of Rs. 1.4 crore, identified during the audit of a major fee-paying client, was removed from the summary of misstatements; her only available route is to discuss it with the same engagement partner whose work she questions, and she fears losing her posting if she speaks. (5) In an earlier matter an investigation concluded that the firm's audit of a cooperative bank had not complied with professional standards; the firm closed the file with no further action because that client accounts for close to a fifth of its fees.

Assertion (A): The course of action described in arrangement (5) is not compliant with SQC 1.
Reason (R): SQC 1 requires the firm to take action when deficiencies or non-compliance in its system of quality control are identified, to take appropriate action against personnel who did not conform to the quality control policies, and to take appropriate action where the results of investigation of a complaint or allegation indicate non-compliance.

Which of the following is the correct answer?
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is incorrect.
A is incorrect but R is correct.
questions.explanation: Arrangement (5) closes a matter in which investigation had already concluded that the firm's audit did not comply with professional standards, and that is the situation in which the firm is required to take appropriate action; A is therefore correct. R correctly states the relevant requirements, which operate independently of the commercial value of the client, and it supplies the very rule whose breach A asserts, so R is the correct explanation of A. The fee concentration of the client is the decisive irrelevancy: it is not a condition qualifying the duty to act. The reasoning in R is not merely a general statement about monitoring, so the second option is wrong, and R contains nothing incorrect, which disposes of the last two options.

questions.question:
Case: Kulkarni & Deshpande is a firm of chartered accountants with eleven partners. Its internal quality-control memorandum records the following arrangements. (1) Responsibility for the monitoring process is entrusted to a person undergoing articleship who has completed two years of training, on the view that he is close to day-to-day work. (2) The memorandum states that monitoring stands completed once written policies and procedures have been framed, since the existence of written policies itself gives reasonable assurance. (3) A letter from a supplier of one of the firm's audit clients alleged that the firm's staff had accepted gifts prohibited by professional standards; the managing partner filed the letter without inquiry on the ground that it came from outside the firm, is unauthenticated, and no register of complaints exists. (4) Audit assistant Sneha suspects that a misstatement of Rs. 1.4 crore, identified during the audit of a major fee-paying client, was removed from the summary of misstatements; her only available route is to discuss it with the same engagement partner whose work she questions, and she fears losing her posting if she speaks. (5) In an earlier matter an investigation concluded that the firm's audit of a cooperative bank had not complied with professional standards; the firm closed the file with no further action because that client accounts for close to a fifth of its fees.

WHAT CHANGES IF: assume that the allegation in arrangement (3) is made instead by a member of the firm's own audit staff rather than by a supplier outside the firm. Which of the following is the MOST APPROPRIATE conclusion?
options: The firm's duty arises only when the concern is raised by the client itself, so a supplier's letter created no obligation in the first place.

Because the source is outside the firm, the letter cannot engage the complaints and allegations requirement at all, and the matter must instead be taken up only through the monitoring factor relating to action against personnel who did not conform to the quality control policies, the firm's channels for personnel being irrelevant to it.
The obligation to investigate arises only if the complaint is made in writing and addressed to the managing partner.

Nothing changes as to the firm's duty to deal with the matter appropriately, since complaints and allegations may originate from within or outside the firm and may be made by firm personnel, clients or other third parties, and the investigation must be supervised by a partner with sufficient experience and authority.
questions.explanation: The source is explicit that complaints and allegations may originate from within or outside the firm and may be made by firm personnel, clients or other third parties, so moving the source from a supplier to a staff member does not enlarge or reduce the firm's duty; either way the firm must investigate in accordance with established policies and procedures and the investigation must be supervised by a partner with sufficient experience and authority. The first and second options both treat the outside origin as determinative, which the wording rejects. The third option invents a formal requirement of writing and of address to the managing partner, which the source does not impose. The change of fact that would matter is a change in subject matter, for example an allegation that a firm policy is routinely skipped rather than an allegation about the conduct of a specific engagement.

questions.question:
Case: Ranganathan Srinivasan & Co. completed an internal monitoring review covering every partner of the firm. The review reported that (i) in eight of twenty-two audit files the final engagement file had been assembled between 70 and 120 days after the date of the auditor's report; (ii) in three files the working papers relating to engagements of a former employee could not be located; (iii) two partners had accepted a client's own valuation of inventory without independent verification, although the firm's written policy requires independent verification of inventory valuation; and (iv) the firm had no record of any decision on whether its system of quality control had been effectively implemented. The managing partner proposes to treat these findings as confidential matters to be settled by reducing the fees of the affected clients, and to close the monitoring report without any further step on the ground that no client has complained.

Match the findings in Column I with the requirement or monitoring factor principally engaged in Column II.
Column I: (A) Finding (i) late assembly of audit engagement files. (B) Finding (ii) working papers that cannot be located. (C) Finding (iii) partners disregarding the firm's written inventory policy. (D) Finding (iv) no record of a decision on effective implementation.
Column II: (1) Completion of the final engagement file for an audit engagement within 60 days after the date of the auditor's report. (2) Policies and procedures designed to maintain safe custody, integrity, accessibility and retrievability of engagement documentation. (3) Taking appropriate action against personnel who did not conform to the quality control policies. (4) Deciding whether the quality control system of the firm has been effectively implemented.
questions.explanation: Finding (i) is a straightforward failure of the assembly requirement, which fixes 60 days after the date of the auditor's report for audit engagements, and 70 to 120 days falls outside it. Finding (ii) is a failure of the safety and accessibility requirement, since documentation that cannot be located has not been kept with safe custody, integrity, accessibility and retrievability. Finding (iii) concerns personnel, including partners, who did not conform to the firm's quality control policies, and so engages the factor requiring appropriate action against them. Finding (iv) is the monitoring factor of deciding whether the system of quality control has been effectively implemented, which the firm has simply never addressed. The other options each pair at least one documentation finding with a monitoring factor, confusing what the file requirements demand with what monitoring demands.

questions.question:
Case: Ranganathan Srinivasan & Co. completed an internal monitoring review covering every partner of the firm. The review reported that (i) in eight of twenty-two audit files the final engagement file had been assembled between 70 and 120 days after the date of the auditor's report; (ii) in three files the working papers relating to engagements of a former employee could not be located; (iii) two partners had accepted a client's own valuation of inventory without independent verification, although the firm's written policy requires independent verification of inventory valuation; and (iv) the firm had no record of any decision on whether its system of quality control had been effectively implemented. The managing partner proposes to treat these findings as confidential matters to be settled by reducing the fees of the affected clients, and to close the monitoring report without any further step on the ground that no client has complained.

Based on the above case, which of the following statements are correct?
Statement 1: Finding (iv) shows that the factor of deciding whether the firm's system of quality control has been effectively implemented has not been addressed.
Statement 2: Treating the findings as confidential matters settled by fee reductions is appropriate, because action is required only when a client complains.
Statement 3: Findings (i) and (ii) evidence non-compliance in the firm's system of quality control and call for action under the factor requiring action when deficiencies or non-compliance are identified.
Statement 4: The firm's monitoring responsibility was discharged by completing the review, since nothing in SQC 1 requires any step after a monitoring review.
options: 2 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
1, 3 and 4 only
1 and 3 only
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: monitoring must take into account deciding whether the quality control system has been effectively implemented, and taking action when deficiencies or non-compliance in the firm's system are identified, which is exactly what findings (i), (ii) and (iv) call for. Statement 2 is incorrect because the trigger for action is the identification of a deficiency or non-compliance, not a client's complaint; the fee reduction is a commercial gesture that leaves the quality-control defect unaddressed. Statement 4 confuses performing a monitoring activity with acting on its results. Finding (iii) additionally engages the separate factor of taking appropriate action against personnel who did not conform to the quality control policies, so any option that treats the review as the end of the matter is wrong.

questions.question:
Case: Ranganathan Srinivasan & Co. completed an internal monitoring review covering every partner of the firm. The review reported that (i) in eight of twenty-two audit files the final engagement file had been assembled between 70 and 120 days after the date of the auditor's report; (ii) in three files the working papers relating to engagements of a former employee could not be located; (iii) two partners had accepted a client's own valuation of inventory without independent verification, although the firm's written policy requires independent verification of inventory valuation; and (iv) the firm had no record of any decision on whether its system of quality control had been effectively implemented. The managing partner proposes to treat these findings as confidential matters to be settled by reducing the fees of the affected clients, and to close the monitoring report without any further step on the ground that no client has complained.

With reference to finding (iii), which of the following is the MOST APPROPRIATE conclusion?
options: No action is required, because a partner's professional judgment on a client's valuation cannot be tested against a written firm policy.

The firm should take appropriate action against the personnel, including these partners, who did not conform to its quality control policies, in addition to acting on the deficiency so identified in its system.

The appropriate remedy is limited to transferring these partners to engagements that do not involve inventory, since the written policy speaks only to inventory valuation and non-conformity cannot be predicated of a rule which a partner is expected to apply with professional judgment.
Action is called for only if the affected client's financial statements are subsequently restated.
questions.explanation: One of the factors to be taken into account in monitoring quality control of engagements is taking appropriate action against personnel who did not conform to the quality control policies; a written firm policy requiring independent verification of inventory valuation is such a policy, and departing from it is non-conformity whatever the seniority of the person concerned. The first option wrongly treats partners as outside the firm's own control framework, which would make the system of quality control unenforceable against the very people who operate it. The third option is a resource adjustment, not action for non-conformity, and the fourth imports a consequential trigger, a restatement, that the requirement does not use. The deficiency in the design or operation of the policy is separately caught by the factor requiring action when deficiencies or non-compliance are identified.

questions.question:
Case: Ranganathan Srinivasan & Co. completed an internal monitoring review covering every partner of the firm. The review reported that (i) in eight of twenty-two audit files the final engagement file had been assembled between 70 and 120 days after the date of the auditor's report; (ii) in three files the working papers relating to engagements of a former employee could not be located; (iii) two partners had accepted a client's own valuation of inventory without independent verification, although the firm's written policy requires independent verification of inventory valuation; and (iv) the firm had no record of any decision on whether its system of quality control had been effectively implemented. The managing partner proposes to treat these findings as confidential matters to be settled by reducing the fees of the affected clients, and to close the monitoring report without any further step on the ground that no client has complained.

Which ONE of the following statements about the proposal to close the monitoring report without further step is INCORRECT?
options: Closing the report without action is inconsistent with the requirement to take action when deficiencies or non-compliance in the firm's system of quality control are identified.
The firm must also consider taking appropriate action against the personnel who did not conform to the quality control policies.
Monitoring policies and procedures must provide reasonable assurance that the firm's policies and procedures relating to its system of quality control are operating effectively.
Closing the report is permissible because the factors to be taken into account in monitoring are alternatives, so satisfying any one of them is sufficient.
questions.explanation: The question asks for the incorrect statement, and the fourth is incorrect: the five matters listed for monitoring are factors to be taken into account together, not alternatives of which one may be chosen, and the firm that has acted on none of them cannot rely on having performed one. The first statement is correct and directly answers the managing partner's proposal, since deficiencies and non-compliance have been identified in findings (i) to (iv). The second and third statements are also correct formulations of the same requirement. A candidate reasoning that entrusting monitoring to a partner, or conducting a review, is by itself enough has misread the cumulative character of these factors.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the factors to be taken into account in monitoring the quality control of engagements under SQC 1?
options: Entrusting responsibility for the monitoring process to a partner or other experienced person in the firm.
Deciding whether the quality control system of the firm has been effectively implemented.
Deciding whether it is appropriate to continue a particular client relationship.
Taking action when deficiencies or non-compliance in the firm's system of quality control are identified.
questions.explanation: The factors listed for monitoring are entrusting responsibility for the monitoring process to a partner or other experienced person in the firm, deciding whether the quality control system has been effectively implemented, dealing with complaints and allegations against the firm or its employees of non-compliance with professional standards or regulatory requirements, taking action when deficiencies or non-compliance in the system are identified, and taking appropriate action against personnel who did not conform to the quality control policies. Deciding whether to continue a client relationship is a client acceptance and continuance matter, not one of the listed monitoring factors, and is the odd item out. The third option is a credible distractor because continuance decisions do form part of the firm's overall system of quality control; what monitoring addresses is the effectiveness of that system as a whole rather than the individual continuance judgment.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the assembly and retention requirements for engagement documentation under SQC 1?
Statement 1: Assembly fixes the latest point by which the final engagement file must be completed, whereas retention fixes the minimum period for which engagement documentation must be kept.
Statement 2: For audit engagements, both the 60-day assembly period and the seven-year retention period run from the date of completion of the audit fieldwork.
Statement 3: For audit engagements, both the 60-day assembly period and the minimum seven-year retention period are measured from the date of the auditor's report.
Statement 4: A file assembled within 60 days of the date of the auditor's report need not be retained for any further period.
options: 1 and 3 only
2 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Assembly requires completion of the final engagement file on a timely basis after engagement reports have been finalized, quantified for audits as 60 days after the date of the auditor's report, while retention requires documentation to be kept for a sufficient period, quantified for audits as a minimum of seven years from the date of the auditor's report. Statements 1 and 3 capture that distinction and the common reference date. Statement 2 substitutes completion of fieldwork for the report date, which is the most frequent error in applying these periods. Statement 4 mistakes assembly for the end of the documentation obligation; the two periods serve different purposes, one closing the file and the other preserving it, and compliance with the first says nothing about the second.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): In respect of an audit engagement, it is the date of the auditor's report, and not the date of completion of fieldwork or the date of the annual general meeting, that governs both the deadline for completing the final engagement file and the commencement of the minimum retention period.
Reason (R): SQC 1 requires the firm to establish policies and procedures to complete assembly of final engagement files on a timely basis after engagement reports have been finalized, fixing 60 days after the date of the auditor's report in the case of audit engagements, and to retain engagement documentation for a minimum of seven years from the date of the auditor's report in the case of audit engagements.

Which of the following is the correct answer?
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is incorrect.
A is incorrect but R is correct.
questions.explanation: Both statements are accurate reproductions of the requirement, so the answer lies between the first two options. R does not, however, explain A: R is a restatement of the same two rules in their own terms, whereas A is a claim about which date controls, and a restatement of a rule cannot by itself show why that rule rather than fieldwork completion or the AGM date applies. The reasoning that actually explains A is that the general assembly requirement is expressed by reference to engagement reports being finalized, which fixes the report date as the trigger, and the retention period is expressly drawn from the date of the auditor's report. Candidates are tempted by the first option because R is longer and more detailed, but length of the reason is not logical support for the assertion.

questions.question:
A firm's procedure for including electronically scanned copies of original paper documentation in its engagement files contains three steps stated out of order.
Step 1: Enable the scanned copies to be retrieved and printed.
Step 2: Generate scanned copies that reflect the full content of the original documentation.
Step 3: Integrate the scanned copies into the engagement files, including indexing and signing.
Which of the following is the correct order in which these steps fall in the workflow the firm's procedures must secure?
questions.explanation: Scanning is meaningful only if the engagement team first generates copies that reflect the full content of the original documentation, which is the condition that protects the integrity of what is captured while the paper original is still in hand. Only then can those copies be integrated into the engagement files, the integration expressly including indexing and signing, since a copy that is not indexed and signed has not really entered the file. Retrieval and printing is the last step because it is the capability the completed file must continue to deliver throughout the retention period. Reversing the order, as in the second option, would allow material to be indexed and signed before it is known to be complete, and the fourth option treats printing capability as a precondition of capture, which it is not.

questions.question:
Match the situations in Column I with the category of complaint or allegation principally engaged in Column II, having regard to the matters the firm's policies and procedures must deal with appropriately.
Column I: (A) A client's finance head writes that the firm's statutory audit of the company failed to comply with the applicable accounting standards. (B) An employee reports that the firm's mandatory second-level review step is being skipped in two branch offices. (C) A competitor alleges that the firm's file review procedure is not being followed anywhere in the firm. (D) A supplier alleges that the firm's staff working at a client's premises accepted gifts prohibited by professional standards.
Column II: (1) Complaint or allegation that work performed by the firm fails to comply with professional standards and regulatory and legal requirements. (2) Allegation of non-compliance with the firm's system of quality control.
questions.explanation: The two categories are distinguished by their subject matter, not by who raises them. Situations A and D attack particular work performed by the firm or the conduct of the staff performing it, alleging failure to comply with accounting standards or with professional standards, and so fall in category (1). Situations B and C attack the firm's control framework itself, namely whether prescribed review and file review procedures are being followed across offices, and so fall in category (2). Note that B and C come from an employee and a competitor respectively, which shows that a category (2) allegation may originate from within or outside the firm; the source is not the basis of classification.

questions.question: A firm receives an allegation from a client that the audit work performed on its debtors was deficient and did not comply with professional standards. The firm's human resources head suggests that the investigation be supervised by whichever member of staff is most familiar with the file, in order to complete the matter within a fortnight. Which of the following is the MOST APPROPRIATE course regarding supervision of the investigation?
options: An experienced consultant engaged on contract for the purpose, the consultant not being a partner of the firm.
A partner of the firm with sufficient experience and the authority required to supervise the investigation.
The engagement partner who performed the work that is the subject of the allegation, being the person most familiar with the file.
The firm's administrative head, since allegations of this kind are handled internally.
questions.explanation: The firm investigates such complaints and allegations in accordance with its established policies and procedures, and the investigation is to be supervised by a partner with sufficient experience and authority. The requirement is therefore conjunctive: the supervisor must be a partner, must have sufficient experience, and must have authority, so an outside consultant, an administrative head and a familiar but junior staff member each fail on at least one limb. Speed is not a criterion the standard adopts, so the fortnight suggested by the human resources head is a distraction from the question of who is qualified to supervise. The engagement partner is the weakest option, because the very work he performed is what is alleged to have been deficient.

questions.question:
A firm's ethics cell examines an anonymous letter alleging that the firm overlooked a related party transaction in a consolidated audit. Statements 1 to 4 concern the firm's obligations once complaints and allegations are received.
Statement 1: If the results of the investigation indicate non-compliance, the firm takes appropriate action.
Statement 2: Where the investigation does not indicate non-compliance, the obligation to take appropriate action under the complaints and allegations requirement is not triggered on that allegation.
Statement 3: The firm's obligation to act on the matter arises only if a regulatory body commences proceedings against the firm.
Statement 4: Because the letter is anonymous, the firm's policies and procedures need not be applied to it at all.
options: 1 and 2 only
3 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are two sides of the same conditional: the requirement to take appropriate action operates where the results of the investigation indicate non-compliance, and an investigation that so indicates ends the matter only in the sense that action, not further inquiry, becomes necessary. Statement 3 wrongly transfers the trigger from the firm's own investigation to external proceedings. Statement 4 is the tempting error: complaints and allegations may originate from within or outside the firm and may be made by firm personnel, clients or other third parties, and nothing conditions the duty on the complainant identifying himself, so anonymity affects the weight of the evidence rather than whether the firm's established procedures are applied.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about engagement documentation and its ownership are correct?
Statement 1: Engagement documentation is the property of the firm, so an individual partner does not own the files of the engagements he signed.
Statement 2: A client that has paid the full audit fee acquires an entitlement to the working papers which overrides the firm's ownership.
Statement 3: Because ownership rests with the firm, the firm's policies on safe custody, integrity, accessibility and retrievability govern where and how the files are held.
Statement 4: The minimum seven-year retention obligation for audit documentation applies only to documentation held by the engagement partner personally.
options: 2 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: The requirement that engagement documentation is the property of the firm is stated without qualification, and its natural consequence is that neither the signing partner nor the fee-paying client acquires ownership, so statements 1 and 3 are correct and statement 2 is incorrect. Statement 3 also links ownership to the safety and accessibility element: it is the firm, as owner, that must design policies maintaining safe custody, integrity, accessibility and retrievability. Statement 4 is incorrect because retention is a firm-level obligation arising from the firm's system of quality control; it is not measured by which individual happens to hold the papers, and a rule expressed that way would be defeated simply by a partner keeping files at home.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): SQC 1 requires the firm to establish clearly defined channels through which its personnel may raise a concern without fear.
Reason (R): Complaints and allegations may originate from within or outside the firm and may be made by firm personnel, clients or other third parties, so personnel must have an assured route for raising concerns relating to the firm's work or its system of quality control.

Which of the following is the correct answer?
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is incorrect.
A is incorrect but R is correct.
questions.explanation: Both statements are faithful to the source, so the answer depends on the logical connection. R establishes only that firm personnel are among the possible makers of complaints and allegations; it does not supply the 'without fear' element, which is a distinct requirement addressing the manner in which internal concerns can be raised rather than the mere fact that they may be raised. A channel that exists on paper but exposes the person raising the concern to consequences would satisfy R and still fail A, which shows that R is incomplete as an explanation. Candidates who choose the first option have treated a background fact as though it were the rationale for the protection.

questions.question: A firm's audit documentation for the year ended 31 March 2016, on which the auditor's report was dated 1 May 2016, was destroyed on 20 June 2023. The firm's quality control partner now asks whether anything would change if the same file had instead been destroyed on 20 April 2023, the assembly of that file having been completed on 25 June 2016. Which of the following is the MOST APPROPRIATE conclusion?
options: Both destructions breach SQC 1, because audit engagement documentation must be retained permanently once an audit report has been issued, the firm's obligations as owner of the documentation being of indefinite duration.

Destruction on 20 June 2023 followed the expiry of the minimum seven years from 1 May 2016 and so does not breach that minimum, whereas destruction on 20 April 2023 was before 1 May 2023 and does breach it.
Neither breaches SQC 1, because the seven-year period runs from the date on which assembly of the final engagement file was completed.
The destruction on 20 April 2023 is permissible, because the file had already been assembled within 60 days of the date of the auditor's report.
questions.explanation: For audit engagements retention is prescribed as a minimum of seven years from the date of the auditor's report, so a report dated 1 May 2016 fixes 1 May 2023 as the earliest date at which the minimum is satisfied. Destruction on 20 June 2023 falls after that date and does not breach the minimum, while destruction on 20 April 2023 is eleven days short of it and does. The third option wrongly relocates the start of retention to completion of assembly, confusing the 60-day assembly deadline with the preservation period, and the fourth compounds the error by treating timely assembly as though it could discharge retention. The first option overstates the requirement, which prescribes a minimum period rather than permanent retention.

questions.question: Which ONE of the following statements regarding the firm's monitoring policies and procedures under SQC 1 is INCORRECT?
options: Monitoring is directed at providing the firm with reasonable assurance that its policies and procedures relating to its system of quality control are operating effectively, being concerned with effectiveness in operation and not merely with the framing of the policies.
Monitoring must take into account dealing with complaints and allegations against the firm or its employees of non-compliance with professional standards or regulatory requirements.

The monitoring of quality control of engagements stands completed once responsibility for the monitoring process has been entrusted to a partner, since entrustment is the only one of the listed factors capable of objective verification.
Taking appropriate action against personnel who did not conform to the quality control policies is one of the factors to be taken into account in monitoring the quality control of engagements.
questions.explanation: Entrusting responsibility for the monitoring process to a partner or other experienced person in the firm is one of five factors to be taken into account in monitoring the quality control of engagements, and it is not a sufficient condition for monitoring. The remaining factors, deciding whether the system has been effectively implemented, dealing with complaints and allegations, acting on identified deficiencies or non-compliance, and acting against non-conforming personnel, all require substantive response, so the second and fourth options are correct statements. The first option correctly states the object of the requirement, namely reasonable assurance that the policies and procedures relating to the system of quality control are operating effectively. The incorrect proposition rests on the additional claim that only entrustment is objectively verifiable, which the source neither says nor implies.

questions.question: A firm completes the final engagement file for a statutory audit eight weeks after the date of the auditor's report. For a non-audit assignment on which a report was also issued that month, the firm's policy prescribes no fixed period and the file was assembled 90 days after the report was finalized. Which of the following is the MOST APPROPRIATE evaluation of the firm's assembly practice?
options: The audit file meets the specific 60-day requirement for audit engagements; for the non-audit assignment no fixed period is prescribed, and the test is whether assembly was completed on a timely basis after the engagement report was finalized, so no breach of a stated number of days can be asserted against it.

Both files breach the requirement, because the 60-day period prescribed for audit engagements is a general rule for the assembly of final engagement files and applies to every assignment on which the firm issues a report, whether or not it is described as an audit engagement.

Neither file can be measured against any requirement, because completion of assembly is left to the professional discretion of the engagement team and the source fixes a period only for retention of documentation, so a complaint about the age of a file is a matter of practice rather than of quality control.

The audit file breaches the requirement, because the 60-day period runs from the date on which the engagement was accepted rather than from the date of the auditor's report, and eight weeks measured from that earlier date is far too late.
questions.explanation: The general requirement is completion of assembly of final engagement files on a timely basis after the engagement reports have been finalized, and the specific quantification of 60 days is expressed in terms confined to audit engagements. Eight weeks is 56 days after the date of the auditor's report, so the audit file satisfies the specific requirement. The second option applies the audit-specific period too broadly to every assignment on which a report is issued, which the source does not do. The fourth mislocates the start of the 60-day period at acceptance of the engagement, a date the requirement does not use. The third option is too narrow, because the general timeliness requirement still binds the firm in respect of the non-audit assignment, even though no particular day-count can be quoted against it.

questions.question:
A firm proposes a single mechanism for handling quality matters: a suggestion box placed at the reception and opened by the front-desk clerk, with the outcome of any investigation treated as confidential to the compliance partner, and with the firm taking no step against any person whose conduct is found to be non-conforming. Statements 1 to 4 evaluate that proposal.
Statement 1: A suggestion box opened by a front-desk clerk does not meet the requirement for clearly defined channels through which firm personnel may raise a concern without fear.
Statement 2: Investigations of complaints and allegations must be supervised by a partner with sufficient experience and authority, which the proposal does not provide for.
Statement 3: The firm may leave non-conforming conduct untouched, because action against non-conforming personnel is required only at the instance of an aggrieved client.
Statement 4: Complaints and allegations must be dealt with appropriately under established policies and procedures, and action is required where the results of the investigation indicate non-compliance.
options: 1, 2 and 4 only
1 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
All of the above
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 each identify a defect in the proposal against the requirements: firm personnel must have clearly defined channels to raise a concern without fear, the firm investigates complaints and allegations in accordance with established policies and procedures with the investigation supervised by a partner with sufficient experience and authority, and appropriate action follows where the results indicate non-compliance. Statement 3 is incorrect, since taking appropriate action against personnel who did not conform to the quality control policies is a factor the firm must take into account in monitoring the quality control of engagements, and it does not wait upon a client's initiative. Treating the outcome as confidential to one partner does not by itself breach anything stated in the source, which is why the point is not made the basis of any incorrect statement.

questions.question: A new partner is allotted her first statutory audit and prepares a checklist of the matters for which the engagement partner is responsible under SA 220. The checklist reads: (i) leadership responsibilities for quality within the firm; (ii) ethical requirements; (iii) acceptance and continuance of client relationships and audit engagements; (iv) assignment of audit engagement team; (v) engagement performance; (vi) monitoring; (vii) documentation. Which observation about this checklist is correct?
options: The checklist is complete, because SA 220 mirrors every element of the firm's system of quality control.
Item (vi) does not belong in the SA 220 list, because monitoring is confined to the firm's system.
Item (iv) does not belong in the SA 220 list, because assigning people to engagements is a matter for the firm alone.
Item (i) is wrongly worded for SA 220 and item (vii) is not one of the matters SA 220 lists for the engagement partner.
Items (iii) and (v) are firm-level matters rather than engagement partner matters.
questions.explanation: SA 220 speaks of leadership responsibilities for quality on audits, that is, on the particular engagement, and not of leadership within the firm, which is the wording of the corresponding SQC 1 element; item (i) is therefore a firm-level element placed in an engagement-level list. Documentation is addressed in the firm's system of quality control within the engagement performance element, and it is not separately named among the six matters for which SA 220 describes the engagement partner's responsibilities, so item (vii) is also out of place. The remaining four items are correctly stated. Item (iv) is precisely the SA 220 substitute for the firm's human resources element, so the suggestion that assigning people is the firm's alone is wrong, and monitoring is expressly named in the SA 220 list.

questions.category: SQC 1 - Review Mechanisms - Peer Review Board
questions.question: A member objects to a peer review visit to his practice unit, saying: "Peer review is an inspection of my audit files to see whether I have committed professional misconduct, and the Peer Review Board is constituted by the Central Government, so its findings are a statutory sanction against me." Identify the errors in this objection. (1) Peer review means examination and review of systems and procedures, not a misconduct inquiry into individual files. (2) The object being determined is whether those systems and procedures have been put in place by the practice unit for ensuring quality of assurance services as per technical, professional and ethical standards. (3) The Peer Review Board is constituted by the ICAI Council. (4) The objective of the Peer Review Board is to ensure that, in carrying out assurance assignments, technical, professional and ethical standards are complied with by members of ICAI. Which statements are correct?
options: 1 and 3 only
2 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
1, 3 and 4 only
All of the above
questions.explanation: All four statements are correct and together they answer the objection. Peer review is defined as the examination and review of systems and procedures to determine whether the same have been put in place by the practice unit for ensuring the quality of assurance services as per technical, professional and ethical standards, so its unit of examination is the practice unit's system and not the individual file or the member's conduct. The Peer Review Board is constituted by the ICAI Council, which defeats the claim of Central Government constitution - that distinction matters, because the board set up by the Central Government is the Quality Review Board, whose members are nominated by the Central Government and the ICAI Council. Statement 4 states the board's objective accurately, so the member is also wrong in treating peer review as a sanctioning exercise.

questions.category: SQC 1 - Review Mechanisms - QRB and NFRA
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the quality review and oversight mechanisms is NOT correct?
options: The Quality Review Board is set up by the Central Government and consists of members nominated by the Central Government and the ICAI Council.
One of the functions of the Quality Review Board is to make recommendations to the Council for the quality of services provided by members of ICAI.
The National Financial Reporting Authority has been constituted in terms of Section 132(1) of the Companies Act, 2013, and has power to enforce compliance with standards.
The Quality Review Board may review the quality of services of members in respect of entities specified under NFRA, unless NFRA itself undertakes that review.
The Peer Review Board is constituted by the ICAI Council.
questions.explanation: The jurisdiction boundary is the opposite of what option 4 states: the Quality Review Board can review the quality of services provided by members of ICAI other than entities specified under NFRA, and those referred to the Quality Review Board by NFRA. Entities specified under NFRA are therefore outside the board's ordinary remit, and the board acquires a matter relating to such an entity only where NFRA refers it, so the wording 'save where NFRA itself undertakes that review' inverts the condition. Every other statement reproduces the source correctly: the board is set up by the Central Government with members nominated by the Central Government and the ICAI Council, recommending to the Council on quality is one of its three functions, NFRA flows from Section 132(1) of the Companies Act, 2013, and the Peer Review Board is constituted by the ICAI Council.

questions.question: M/s Sunrise Agro Limited appointed CA Karan as engagement partner for the audit of its financial statements for FY 2025-26. In the introduction to the audit file he wrote: "This SA deals with my responsibilities regarding quality control procedures for the audit of financial statements. Because I must implement those procedures at the particular audit engagement level, my objective is to obtain absolute assurance that the audit complies with professional standards and with regulatory and legal requirements, and for that purpose I will apply the firm's policies and procedures to this engagement." He further recorded that his team comprised two article clerks and that the client's internal audit function had reported a cash shortage of Rs. 4 lakh in March 2026 which had been investigated and written off as an isolated lapse. Which part of the statement in his file note is incorrect?
options: The identification of the subject matter of SA 220 as the auditor's responsibilities regarding quality control procedures for an audit of financial statements.
The level at which the quality control procedures are to be implemented, namely the particular audit engagement.
The nature and degree of assurance stated, namely absolute instead of reasonable, and the objective stated by reference to that assurance.
The requirement that the audit comply with professional standards and with regulatory and legal requirements.
The reliance on the firm's policies and procedures in discharging engagement level responsibilities.
questions.explanation: The engagement partner has to implement quality control procedures at the particular audit engagement level that provide him with reasonable assurance that the audit complies with professional standards and regulatory and legal requirements. Reasonable assurance is the operative standard and it is inherently less than absolute assurance, so the stated objective is overstated and is the single incorrect element in the passage. The subject matter of the standard, the engagement level at which the partner acts, and the dual benchmark of professional standards together with regulatory and legal requirements are all faithfully reproduced. Option 5 is a distraction rather than an error: SA 220 is modelled on the lines of SQC 1 and the partner's own leadership message stresses compliance with the firm's quality control policies and procedures, so that reliance is consistent with the source even though the passage itself does not say so. The size of the team and the written-off cash shortage are facts included to test whether they are treated as decisive, and neither has any bearing on the standard of assurance which the engagement partner must aim at.

questions.question: Vidyut Yanthram Limited (VYL), a listed entity, appointed M/s Anchor & Co. as statutory auditors for FY 2025-26. Partway through, the engagement quality control reviewer raised a concern on the appropriateness of the impairment assumptions used for a loss-making wind-energy division; on the same day a financial newspaper published an article alleging misreporting, and the company's share price moved sharply. Under an order of the National Financial Reporting Authority, an investigation into the conduct of the auditors of VYL was commenced. During the year the board of VYL was reconstituted, two whole-time directors resigned, and the finance controller who had prepared the impairment model was replaced. The reviewer and the engagement partner eventually differed on one significant matter but resolved it by consulting a technical panel of the firm before the file was closed. On 30 June 2026 the engagement partner signed and dated the auditor's report, having personally telephoned the reviewer at 7.40 a.m. that morning and received the oral confirmation 'I stand by my earlier note, you may proceed'; the reviewer's written completion note was dated 2 July 2026. The reviewer had been appointed at the planning stage, and the engagement partner had discussed each of the significant matters arising during the audit with the reviewer in the course of the work. (The above facts apply to all five questions of this VYL case family.) Which statement correctly describes the position under SA 220 as to the auditor's report?
options: The report was validly dated, because the engagement partner ascertained the reviewer's final position before signing.
The report should not have been dated until the engagement quality control review was completed, and on 30 June 2026 that review was not yet complete.
The dating is immaterial, because the partner had discussed every significant matter with the reviewer and had determined that a reviewer had been appointed.
The dating is irregular only because the reviewer and the partner differed on one significant matter, which must be resolved after the report is dated.
The irregularity arises because the investigation into the auditors of VYL had not been closed when the report was signed.
questions.explanation: For an engagement quality control review the engagement partner shall determine that the reviewer has been appointed, discuss significant matters arising during the audit engagement with that reviewer, and not date the auditor's report until the engagement quality control review is completed. The third duty is objective and timing-based: an oral statement by the reviewer that he stands by his earlier note does not complete the review, and the reviewer's own completion note is dated 2 July 2026, two days after the report was dated. The facts that the reviewer was appointed early and that the significant matters were discussed in the course of the work discharge two of the three duties but cannot substitute for the third, so option 3 fails. Option 4 adds a requirement the source does not state and inverts the order of events, and option 5 imports a consequence of the investigation that the source does not attach to dating.

questions.question: Vidyut Yanthram Limited (VYL), a listed entity, appointed M/s Anchor & Co. as statutory auditors for FY 2025-26. Partway through, the engagement quality control reviewer raised a concern on the appropriateness of the impairment assumptions used for a loss-making wind-energy division; on the same day a financial newspaper published an article alleging misreporting, and the company's share price moved sharply. Under an order of the National Financial Reporting Authority, an investigation into the conduct of the auditors of VYL was commenced. During the year the board of VYL was reconstituted, two whole-time directors resigned, and the finance controller who had prepared the impairment model was replaced. On 30 June 2026 the engagement partner signed and dated the auditor's report, having personally telephoned the reviewer at 7.40 a.m. that morning and received the oral confirmation 'I stand by my earlier note, you may proceed'; the reviewer's written completion note was dated 2 July 2026. The reviewer had been appointed at the planning stage, and the engagement partner had discussed each of the significant matters arising during the audit with the reviewer in the course of the work. (The above facts apply to all five questions of this VYL case family.) A junior on the VYL team said in a counselling session that he had found an unreconciled difference in a divisional schedule but had not raised it, fearing the effect on the audit fee already recovered and on his assessment. No message from the engagement partner about raising concerns had ever been given to the team. Which conclusion is most appropriate?
options: The partner complied with SA 220, because no firm policy forbade the raising of such differences.
The emphasis which his actions and messages had to give on raising concerns without fear of reprisals was absent.
The matter lies entirely with the firm's human resources policies, since fear of reprisals is a personnel question.
The omission is cured by the partner having discussed significant matters with the engagement quality control reviewer.
The silence of the partner matters only where the team member who hesitated to speak is himself a partner and not an associate.
questions.explanation: In taking responsibility for the overall quality on each audit engagement, the engagement partner's actions and appropriate messages to the engagement team must emphasise, among other things, the engagement team's ability to raise concerns without fear of reprisals. On these facts no such message was ever conveyed and a team member suppressed a finding out of fear for his assessment and for fee consequences, which is precisely the situation the emphasis is meant to prevent. The duty is placed on the engagement partner at the engagement level and is not discharged by the silence of firm policy, so option 1 reverses the position; nor does it migrate to the firm's personnel function, and it is not cured by the separate duty to discuss significant matters with the reviewer. The source attaches the duty to messages to the engagement team without any grade qualification, so option 5 is invented.

questions.question: Vidyut Yanthram Limited (VYL), a listed entity, appointed M/s Anchor & Co. as statutory auditors for FY 2025-26. Partway through, the engagement quality control reviewer raised a concern on the appropriateness of the impairment assumptions used for a loss-making wind-energy division; on the same day a financial newspaper published an article alleging misreporting, and the company's share price moved sharply. Under an order of the National Financial Reporting Authority, an investigation into the conduct of the auditors of VYL was commenced.
