The reviewer had been appointed at the planning stage, and the engagement partner had discussed each of the significant matters arising during the audit with the reviewer in the course of the work. (The above facts apply to all five questions of this VYL case family.) The partners of M/s Anchor & Co. wrote to the Quality Review Board seeking directions on the audit of VYL and asking the Board to review the quality of the services provided by them as auditors of VYL. Which response of the Board is consistent with the source?
options: The Board will review the quality of services provided by the members in respect of VYL, because a listed company audit is a core assurance service.
The Board cannot review the quality of services of members in respect of entities specified under NFRA, such as VYL, and may do so only where NFRA refers the matter.
The Board may review the quality of services of the members in respect of VYL, because NFRA has already commenced an investigation into those auditors.
The Board cannot take any step in relation to VYL, because review of the systems and procedures of a practice unit is reserved exclusively to the Peer Review Board.
The Board may act only through recommendations to the ICAI Council, and cannot itself review the quality of services provided by members.
questions.explanation: The Quality Review Board can review the quality of services provided by members of ICAI other than entities specified under NFRA and those referred to the Board by NFRA. VYL is a listed entity whose auditors are subject to the powers of NFRA over auditors of certain companies such as listed, insurance and banking companies, so VYL falls in the excluded class and the Board's remit extends to it only if NFRA refers the matter. Option 3 offers a distinction without a basis: the source states no rule that an investigation commenced by NFRA hands review to the Board, and the only gateway is a referral by NFRA. Option 4 confuses mechanisms, since examination of the systems and procedures of a practice unit is the description of peer review and is not a bar on the statutory functions of the Board. Option 5 understates the functions, because reviewing the quality of services provided by members is itself one of the three functions alongside recommending to the Council and guiding members to improve quality.

questions.question: Vidyut Yanthram Limited (VYL), a listed entity, appointed M/s Anchor & Co. as statutory auditors for FY 2025-26. Partway through, the engagement quality control reviewer raised a concern on the appropriateness of the impairment assumptions used for a loss-making wind-energy division; on the same day a financial newspaper published an article alleging misreporting, and the company's share price moved sharply. Under an order of the National Financial Reporting Authority, an investigation into the conduct of the auditors of VYL was commenced. During the year the board of VYL was reconstituted, two whole-time directors resigned, and the finance controller who had prepared the impairment model was replaced. The reviewer and the engagement partner eventually differed on one significant matter but resolved it by consulting a technical panel of the firm before the file was closed. On 30 June 2026 the engagement partner signed and dated the auditor's report, having personally telephoned the reviewer at 7.40 a.m. that morning and received the oral confirmation 'I stand by my earlier note, you may proceed'; the reviewer's written completion note was dated 2 July 2026. The reviewer had been appointed at the planning stage, and the engagement partner had discussed each of the significant matters arising during the audit with the reviewer in the course of the work. (The above facts apply to all five questions of this VYL case family.) Consider these statements about the VYL engagement. (1) The engagement partner discharged the duty to determine that an engagement quality control reviewer had been appointed. (2) The engagement partner discharged the duty to discuss significant matters arising during the audit engagement with that reviewer. (3) The engagement partner failed in the duty not to date the auditor's report until the engagement quality control review was completed. (4) The difference of view between the partner and the reviewer is itself a breach of the requirement that leadership messages emphasise the issuing of an appropriate auditor's report. Which statements are correct?
options: 1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2 and 4 only
3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: The reviewer was appointed at the planning stage and the partner ascertained that appointment, so statement 1 is correct; the partner discussed each significant matter arising during the audit with the reviewer, so statement 2 is likewise correct. The failure is confined to the third duty, since the report was dated on 30 June 2026 while the reviewer's completion note bears a later date of 2 July 2026, which makes statement 3 correct as a description of the omission and means any option excluding statement 3 is wrong; statements 1 and 3 are correct and statements 2 and 4 are not, so every combination option which admits statement 2 or statement 4 is wrong. Statement 4 is unsupported: the source lists the issuing of an appropriate auditor's report among the matters the partner's actions and messages are to emphasise, and it says nothing that converts a difference of view between partner and reviewer into a breach of that requirement. The decisive facts are therefore the timing of the dating and the absence of any rule about differences of view.

questions.question: Vidyut Yanthram Limited (VYL), a listed entity, appointed M/s Anchor & Co. as statutory auditors for FY 2025-26. Partway through, the engagement quality control reviewer raised a concern on the appropriateness of the impairment assumptions used for a loss-making wind-energy division; on the same day a financial newspaper published an article alleging misreporting, and the company's share price moved sharply. Under an order of the National Financial Reporting Authority, an investigation into the conduct of the auditors of VYL was commenced. During the year the board of VYL was reconstituted, two whole-time directors resigned, and the finance controller who had prepared the impairment model was replaced. The reviewer and the engagement partner eventually differed on one significant matter but resolved it by consulting a technical panel of the firm before the file was closed. On 30 June 2026 the engagement partner signed and dated the auditor's report, having personally telephoned the reviewer at 7.40 a.m. that morning and received the oral confirmation 'I stand by my earlier note, you may proceed'; the reviewer's written completion note was dated 2 July 2026. The reviewer had been appointed at the planning stage, and the engagement partner had discussed each of the significant matters arising during the audit with the reviewer in the course of the work. (The above facts apply to all five questions of this VYL case family.) Assume instead that the reviewer had recorded in writing on 27 June 2026 that the engagement quality control review was complete, with no outstanding matter, and that the partner dated the report on 30 June 2026. Everything else in the case remains unchanged, including the investigation ordered by NFRA and the resignation of two whole-time directors during the year. What is the effect of this change on the engagement partner's duties regarding the review?
options: The three duties are satisfied, the review having been completed before the report was dated, and neither external event bears on them.
The duty not to date the report until the review is completed is satisfied, but the partner must now obtain the clearance of NFRA before dating.
The duties remain unsatisfied, because the partner had personally telephoned the reviewer instead of obtaining a written completion note from the reviewer.
The change is irrelevant, because the partner's duty regarding dating is discharged once the significant matters have been discussed with the reviewer.
The duties are satisfied only if the partner also gives the leadership messages to the engagement team that SA 220 requires.
questions.explanation: The engagement partner's three duties in relation to an engagement quality control review are to determine that the reviewer has been appointed, to discuss significant matters arising during the audit with the reviewer, and not to date the auditor's report until that review is completed. With a written record dated 27 June 2026 that the review was complete and nothing outstanding, the dating on 30 June 2026 follows completion, so all three duties are met on the modified facts. Neither the investigation ordered by NFRA into the auditors of a listed company nor a change in the composition of the client's board is made a condition of those duties by the source, so the second option, which superadds a clearance requirement of NFRA, has no basis in the source. The third option misstates the duty as prescribing the form in which completion must be evidenced, and option 4 repeats the error of treating discussion as a substitute for completion. Option 5 merges the leadership responsibilities into the engagement performance duty, which the source keeps separate.

questions.question: Kaveri Cold Chain Limited engaged Mr. Anand, a partner of a branch office of Crescent & Co., as engagement partner for its audit of the financial statements for FY 2025-26. In a post-balance-sheet review meeting, a new associate raised the point that a member of the audit team held an immaterial investment in the client and that the firm's independence database contained an unresolved alert. Mr. Anand had never seen that database entry, which had been recorded before he was allotted to the engagement, and the associate had reported the point two days earlier. He said in reply: "Independence is something the firm's system confirms annually, so I have nothing to do except place reliance on that confirmation, and this investment is immaterial in amount." The associate's other points on inventory and revenue cut-off were taken up and resolved to his satisfaction the same week. The client's borrowings from a related party were also restructured during the year, a fact that had been reported to Mr. Anand by the manager before planning. Consider the following steps: (1) obtain relevant information from the firm to identify circumstances that create threats to independence; (2) evaluate information on identified breaches to determine whether they create a threat to independence for the audit engagement; (3) take appropriate action to eliminate such threats or reduce them to an acceptable level by applying safeguards. Which correctly states the timing at which SA 220 requires the engagement partner to perform them?
options: Only before accepting the engagement, since threats arising afterwards are for the firm to handle.
At the time of planning only, because the engagement team is fixed by then.
Throughout the engagement, as and when the relevant information comes to his notice.
Only upon a written report from an engagement team member, since informal notice is insufficient.
Only where the matter is material to the financial statements.
questions.explanation: To ensure compliance with the independence requirements that apply to the audit, the engagement partner shall obtain relevant information from the firm to identify circumstances that create threats to independence, evaluate information on identified breaches to determine whether they create a threat for the audit engagement, and take appropriate action to eliminate such threats or reduce them to an acceptable level by applying safeguards. The source frames these as continuing duties of the partner on the engagement and not as a single act at acceptance or at planning, which is decisive here: the alert and the investment came to notice in a post-balance-sheet review meeting and had to be evaluated and acted upon then, so the duty operates throughout the engagement as information comes to notice. The fourth option fails because the source does not require a written report from a team member, and the fifth wrongly treats an immaterial investment as outside the independence enquiry, and the immateriality of the holding does not answer the partner's stated reason for doing nothing.

questions.question: A training note for article clerks states: "Independence on an audit is secured by the firm and nobody else. The firm's system of quality control under SQC 1 sets the policies and procedures directed at providing reasonable assurance that the firm and its personnel, and where required by applicable ethical pronouncements other individuals in a position to influence the engagement, comply with relevant ethical requirements; it includes policies to identify and respond to threats to independence, to rotate personnel where applicable for listed entities, and to require written confirmation of compliance with independence. Under SA 220 the engagement partner need do nothing further, because the firm has already discharged the obligation." Evaluate this note. (1) The firm-level independence policies described are those of the firm's system of quality control under SQC 1. (2) SA 220 casts on the engagement partner a distinct three-step duty in relation to independence for the audit. (3) Because SA 220 is modelled on the lines of SQC 1, the firm-level policies displace the partner-level duty where the two cover the same subject. (4) One element of the partner's duty is to obtain relevant information from the firm to identify circumstances that create threats to independence. Which statements are correct?
options: 1 and 3 only
2 and 4 only
1, 2 and 4 only
1, 3 and 4 only
All of the above
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct and statement 3 is not. SA 220 describes the engagement partner's responsibility for ethical requirements as a separate and additional responsibility, discharged by obtaining relevant information from the firm to identify circumstances creating threats to independence, evaluating information on identified breaches, and taking appropriate action to eliminate threats or reduce them to an acceptable level by applying safeguards. The fact that SA 220 is modelled on the lines of SQC 1 explains the shape of the framework and does not make the firm-level system a substitute for the partner's own duty, so the note's conclusion does not follow. Statement 4 is also the answer to the practical question in the note: the partner is expressly required to seek information from the firm, which presupposes that firm-level work is a source of inputs for the partner rather than a discharge of his responsibility.

questions.question: Two audit files were examined. In File A the engagement partner issued a written message to the team stating that the firm's quality control policies and procedures were to be complied with and that quality was essential in performing audit engagements. In File B the engagement partner issued no message at all, and the audit was completed without any recorded concern. Assertion (A): File B discloses a failure by the engagement partner in his responsibility for overall quality on that audit engagement. Reason (R): SA 220 requires the engagement partner to rely on the firm's system of quality control, and in File B the firm had no system. Which of the following is correct?
options: Both A and R are correct and R explains A.
Both A and R are correct but R does not explain A.
A is correct but R is incorrect.
A is incorrect but R is correct.
Neither A nor R is correct.
questions.explanation: The assertion is correct: in taking responsibility for the overall quality on each audit engagement, it is the engagement partner's actions and appropriate messages to the engagement team that are to emphasise the importance to audit quality of performing work which complies with professional standards and legal requirements, of complying with the firm's quality control policies and procedures, of issuing an appropriate auditor's report, of the team's ability to raise concerns without fear of reprisals, and of the fact that quality is essential in performing audit engagements. Silence on both files, as in File B, leaves that responsibility un-discharged whatever the outcome of the audit. The reason is incorrect on two counts, because SA 220 does not put the partner on reliance on the firm's system in place of his own actions and messages, and nothing in the facts states that the firm had no system. An incorrect reason cannot support the assertion in any event.

questions.question: A partner of a mid-size practice is designated engagement partner for a statutory audit. Before the audit begins he asks his article assistant to list the matters for which SA 220 imposes additional responsibilities on the engagement partner in relation to an audit engagement and to state what the source requires for each. Which list and description is correct?
options: All six matters for which SA 220 describes the responsibilities of the engagement partner are elaborated in that table, including acceptance and continuance, the assignment of the team and monitoring.
Three matters are elaborated, namely leadership responsibilities for quality on audits, ethical requirements and engagement performance; the other three are named but not elaborated.
Two matters are elaborated, namely leadership responsibilities and engagement performance, while ethical requirements are left entirely to the firm's system.
Four matters are elaborated, monitoring being the third additional one, because the source states the factors the engagement partner must consider in monitoring.
Three matters are elaborated, namely ethical requirements, acceptance and continuance, and engagement performance, leadership being a firm-level element only.
questions.explanation: SA 220's table of additional responsibilities of the engagement partner in relation to an audit engagement elaborates three matters only: leadership responsibilities for quality on audits, ethical requirements, and engagement performance with its three duties regarding an engagement quality control review. The six matters for which SA 220 describes the partner's responsibilities also include acceptance and continuance of client relationships and audit engagements, assignment of the audit engagement team, and monitoring, but the source gives no content for those three. The second option is the correct description of the extent of the source. The remaining options are wrong for identifiable reasons: the first treats all six matters as elaborated, the third reduces the elaborated set to two and leaves ethical requirements to the firm alone, the fourth adds monitoring to the elaborated set, and the fifth mis-assigns leadership responsibilities to the firm level alone.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the engagement partner's duties where an engagement quality control review is required is NOT correct?
options: The engagement partner shall determine that an engagement quality control reviewer has been appointed.
The engagement partner shall discuss with the engagement quality control reviewer the significant matters arising during the course of that audit engagement.
The engagement partner shall not date the auditor's report until the engagement quality control review is completed.
The engagement partner may date the report and obtain the reviewer's completion afterwards, provided the reviewer agrees in writing.
The engagement partner's duties regarding the review form part of his responsibility for engagement performance.
questions.explanation: The prohibition on dating the auditor's report until the engagement quality control review is completed is absolute in the source and is not subject to a contrary written agreement between the partner and the reviewer. Option 4 therefore states the position incorrectly, since the reviewer's consent cannot convert a report dated before completion into a compliant one. Options 1 to 3 restate the three duties exactly, and option 5 correctly places them under engagement performance, one of the six matters for which SA 220 describes the partner's responsibilities and one of the three that the table of additional responsibilities elaborates. A common error to resist is treating the second duty, discussion of significant matters, as capable of satisfying the third; discussion and completion are separate requirements.

questions.question: A regional council circulated a note on the allocation of quality control work. It reads: "(i) The firm establishes the system of quality control and the associated elements; (ii) the engagement partner implements quality control procedures at the particular audit engagement level; (iii) leadership responsibility for quality on audits is owned by the engagement partner, whereas leadership responsibility for quality within the firm is a matter for the firm; (iv) the engagement partner is responsible for the firm's monitoring of its system of quality control, because SA 220 lists monitoring among his matters." Which statement misstates the position?
options: (ii)
(iii)
(iv)
Both (i) and (iv)
questions.explanation: Statement (iv) misstates the position. Monitoring is indeed named among the six matters for which SA 220 describes the responsibilities of the engagement partner, and leadership responsibilities for quality on audits is one of those matters, so statements (i) to (iii) are consistent with the source and with the firm-level and engagement-level division of labour. But listing a heading among the partner's matters does not transfer to the partner the firm's monitoring of its system of quality control, and the source supplies no content whatever as to what the partner's monitoring responsibility involves. The error is a familiar one, namely reasoning from the name of a matter to its substance. Equally, the source does not make the partner the owner of firm-wide leadership, which statement (iii) keeps correctly apart.

questions.question: Match the emphasis required in the engagement partner's actions and appropriate messages to the engagement team with the situation in which it is most directly engaged. Column I: (A) Performing work that complies with professional standards and legal requirements. (B) Complying with the firm's quality control policies and procedures. (C) Issuing an appropriate auditor's report. (D) The engagement team's ability to raise concerns without fear of reprisals. Column II: (1) A team member identifies an unresolved inventory difference during a post-balance-sheet review meeting and hesitates to report it. (2) A draft report is circulated for internal clearance before signature. (3) A team member proposes to skip a required procedure because 'the client is small'. (4) A team member suggests departing from the firm's audit manual for the sake of speed. Which of the following matches are correct?
questions.explanation: Skipping a required procedure because the client is small goes directly to performing work that complies with professional standards and legal requirements, so A matches 3. Departing from the firm's audit manual for speed engages compliance with the firm's quality control policies and procedures, so B matches 4. Circulating a draft report for internal clearance before signature engages the emphasis on issuing an appropriate auditor's report, so C matches 2. A team member's hesitation to report an unresolved difference because of fear for his position engages the emphasis on the team's ability to raise concerns without fear of reprisals, so D matches 1. Note that the emphasis on issuing an appropriate report and the separate duty not to date the auditor's report until the engagement quality control review is completed are different requirements, one a leadership message and the other an engagement performance duty.

questions.question: A textile manufacturer appointed Sagar & Associates as statutory auditor. During the audit the engagement partner told the team at the opening meeting only that the firm's fees had to be recovered within sixty days of the report and that the file was to be closed by 25 June 2026; he made no reference to audit quality. In May 2026 the engagement quality control reviewer, appointed at the planning stage, raised a concern about a related party transaction. In a general body meeting in April 2026 a shareholder objected to the appointment of the auditor, and the auditors were asked to furnish information to the Central Government. On 24 June 2026 the partner signed the report, and the reviewer's written completion note was dated 1 July 2026. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion about the engagement partner's leadership responsibility for quality on this audit?
options: He discharged it, because he determined that a reviewer had been appointed and discussed the concern with the reviewer.
He did not discharge it, because his actions and messages stressed fee recovery and file-closing instead of the matters those messages must emphasise.
He discharged it, because leadership responsibility for quality within the firm rests with the firm and not with him.
He did not discharge it, because he discussed the concern with the reviewer only after it was raised.
He discharged it, because the shareholder objection at the annual meeting and the information called for by the Central Government are unrelated to the quality of his audit.
questions.explanation: The engagement partner takes responsibility for the overall quality on each audit engagement through his actions and appropriate messages to the engagement team, and those messages are required to emphasise five specific things: performing work that complies with professional standards and legal requirements, complying with the firm's quality control policies and procedures, issuing an appropriate auditor's report, the team's ability to raise concerns without fear of reprisals, and the fact that quality is essential in performing audit engagements. On these facts the only messages given were about fee recovery and closing the file, so that responsibility was not discharged, which makes the second option the appropriate conclusion. The first and fourth options describe duties belonging to engagement performance and to the relationship with the reviewer rather than the leadership messages, and cannot cure the silence here. The third option confuses leadership on audits with leadership within the firm, and the fifth offers irrelevant facts which the case includes precisely because they are not decisive.

questions.question: A textile manufacturer appointed Sagar & Associates as statutory auditor. During the audit the engagement partner told the team at the opening meeting only that the firm's fees had to be recovered within sixty days of the report and that the file was to be closed by 25 June 2026; he made no reference to audit quality. In May 2026 the engagement quality control reviewer, appointed at the planning stage, raised a concern about a related party transaction. In a general body meeting in April 2026 a shareholder objected to the appointment of the auditor, and the auditors were asked to furnish information to the Central Government. On 24 June 2026 the partner signed the report, and the reviewer's written completion note was dated 1 July 2026. Consider these statements. (1) The reviewer having been appointed at the planning stage satisfies the partner's duty to determine that a reviewer has been appointed. (2) The concern about the related party transaction was a significant matter arising during the audit engagement which the partner was required to discuss with the reviewer. (3) The report of 24 June 2026 was dated before the engagement quality control review was completed. (4) The requirement to furnish information to the Central Government is a quality control procedure which the engagement partner had to implement at the engagement level. Which statements are correct?
options: 1 and 3 only
2 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
1, 3 and 4 only
All of the above
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The appointment at the planning stage answers the duty to determine that an engagement quality control reviewer has been appointed; a reviewer's concern about a related party transaction is a significant matter arising during the audit and falls within the duty to discuss significant matters with the reviewer; and the report dated 24 June 2026 preceded the reviewer's written completion note of 1 July 2026, so the duty not to date the auditor's report until the review is completed was broken. Statement 4 is wrong, because a requirement to furnish information to the Central Government is not a quality control procedure at the particular audit engagement level which the partner implements; the partner's engagement level procedures are those directed to reasonable assurance that the audit complies with professional standards and with regulatory and legal requirements. The objection raised at the general meeting and the sixty-day fee instruction are equally beside the point.

questions.question: A chartered accountant who is not a partner of any audit practice was appointed engagement quality control reviewer for the audit of a listed company by a firm of which he was not a partner. He said: "SA 220 is modelled on the lines of SQC 1 and it describes responsibilities of the engagement partner for six matters. Since none of those six matters is 'engagement quality control review' as such, and since the reviewer is not the engagement partner, SA 220 says nothing whatever about what happens on an engagement where a review is carried out." Which evaluation of this statement is correct?
options: The statement is correct, because a matter not separately named in the list of six is outside SA 220.
The statement is incorrect, because engagement performance is one of the six matters and SA 220 prescribes the partner's duties regarding the review.
The statement is correct, because the regime of engagement quality control review belongs to the firm's system of quality control under SQC 1 and not to SA 220 at all.
The statement is incorrect, because the reviewer becomes an engagement partner for the purpose of SA 220 once appointed.
The statement is correct in part, because SA 220 addresses only dating and discussion, which apply only to unlisted entities.
questions.explanation: The reviewer's premise about the list of six matters is right but his conclusion is wrong. Engagement performance is one of the six matters for which SA 220 describes the responsibilities of the engagement partner, and in the table of additional responsibilities the source elaborates that matter by prescribing three duties relating to an engagement quality control review, namely determining that a reviewer has been appointed, discussing significant matters arising during the audit engagement with the reviewer, and not dating the auditor's report until the review is completed. A subject therefore falls within SA 220 through the matter under which it is dealt with, and not only through a separately headed entry. Option 3 overstates the position, because the content of the review regime is a matter for the firm's system of quality control while the partner's duties regarding it are in SA 220. Nothing makes the reviewer an engagement partner and no listed or unlisted qualification appears in the source.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Where the firm's independence monitoring records a breach by a person connected with an audit engagement after the audit has begun, the engagement partner cannot treat the matter as closed on the ground that the firm has already been notified. Reason (R): SA 220 requires the engagement partner to evaluate information on identified breaches to determine whether they create a threat to independence for the audit engagement and to take appropriate action to eliminate such threats or reduce them to an acceptable level by applying safeguards. Which of the following is correct?
options: Both A and R are correct and R explains A.
Both A and R are correct but R does not explain A.
A is correct but R is incorrect.
A is incorrect but R is correct.
Neither A nor R is correct.
questions.explanation: The reason states two of the three steps which SA 220 requires of the engagement partner to ensure compliance with the independence requirements that apply to the audit, the third being to obtain relevant information from the firm to identify circumstances that create threats to independence. Because those steps are the partner's own, notification of the firm does not close the matter: he must evaluate the information on the identified breach to determine whether it creates a threat to independence for this engagement and then act on any threat by eliminating it or reducing it to an acceptable level through safeguards. The assertion follows directly from that duty and the reason is the explanation of it, so the logical connection is genuine and not merely two correct statements about the same subject. The timing is immaterial, since the source does not confine these steps to the date of appointment.

questions.question: Two propositions were put to a partners' meeting. Proposition 1: "On the Nidhi Appliances audit we obtained a written completion note from the reviewer dated 19 July 2026 and dated our report the next day, and we had discussed all significant matters with the reviewer; our conduct on dating complied with SA 220." Proposition 2: "On the Anand Motors audit the reviewer's completion note is dated 5 September 2026 and our report is dated 4 September 2026; we may cure this by obtaining the reviewer's confirmation that he has no change to his earlier note." Which evaluation is correct?
options: Both propositions are sound, because in each case a reviewer had been appointed, the significant matters had been discussed and some record of the reviewer's final view was available.
Proposition 1 is sound; Proposition 2 is not, because the review must be completed before the report is dated and a later confirmation of a stale view does not complete it.
Proposition 1 is unsound, because discussion with the reviewer must follow the completion note.
Proposition 2 is sound, because the reviewer's confirmation establishes that the review was in substance complete.
Both propositions are unsound, because the reviewer must sign the auditor's report as well as the completion note.
questions.explanation: Proposition 1 is sound: the engagement quality control review was complete on 19 July 2026 and the auditor's report was dated the following day, so the prohibition on dating before completion was observed, and the discussion of significant matters with the reviewer had also taken place. Proposition 2 fails, because the report was dated on 4 September 2026 while the review was completed only on 5 September 2026, and a subsequent confirmation that the reviewer sees no reason to alter his note does not retrospectively complete a review that was outstanding when the date was written. The decisive fact is the order of the two dates. Option 5 invents a requirement that the reviewer sign the auditor's report, and option 3 inverts a sequence that SA 220 does not impose.

questions.question: The quality control head of a firm prepared a comparison of the firm's system of quality control under SQC 1 with the engagement partner's responsibilities under SA 220. Consider these statements. (1) Both frameworks begin their enumerations with leadership responsibilities for quality, but the firm's element concerns leadership within the firm while SA 220's concerns leadership on audits. (2) Both frameworks include ethical requirements, acceptance and continuance of client relationships, engagement performance and monitoring. (3) SA 220 places the firm's element of human resources in the hands of the engagement partner under the name of assignment of the audit engagement team. (4) SA 220's enumeration of the engagement partner's matters includes documentation, so the partner is answerable for engagement file documentation as a named matter. Which statements are correct?
options: 1 and 4 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3 only
1, 3 and 4 only
All of the above
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 correctly draw the mirror between the two frameworks. Leadership comes first in each, with the firm's element expressed as leadership responsibilities for quality within the firm and SA 220's as leadership responsibilities for quality on audits; ethical requirements, acceptance and continuance of client relationships, engagement performance and monitoring appear in both, with SA 220 qualifying acceptance and continuance by reference to audit engagements; and the firm-level human resources element corresponds at engagement level to the assignment of the audit engagement team. Statement 4 is wrong, because documentation is not separately named among the six matters for which SA 220 describes the engagement partner's responsibilities, so the enumeration cannot be read to make the partner answerable for it as a named matter. The exclusion of statement 4 also disposes of options 1, 4 and 5.

questions.category: SQC 1 - Review Mechanisms - QRB and NFRA
questions.question: Four matters were brought before the Quality Review Board. Matter 1: quality of services provided by a member auditing an insurance company. Matter 2: quality of services provided by a member auditing an unlisted public company which is not specified under NFRA. Matter 3: quality of services provided by a member auditing a listed company, where NFRA has referred that matter to the Board. Matter 4: quality of services provided by a member auditing a banking company, where NFRA has commenced an investigation into that auditor but has made no referral to the Board. In which matters may the Board review the quality of services?
options: 1 and 2 only
All of them
2, 3 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
questions.explanation: The Quality Review Board can review the quality of services provided by members of ICAI other than entities specified under NFRA and those referred to the Board by NFRA. Matter 2 falls in the first limb, since the audited entity is not one specified under NFRA, and Matter 3 falls in the second limb because NFRA has referred it, notwithstanding that a listed company is otherwise outside the Board's remit. Matter 1 concerning an insurance company and Matter 4 concerning a banking company are outside the Board's competence, because insurance and banking companies are among the companies whose auditors fall within the powers of NFRA and no referral has been made. An investigation commenced by NFRA is not the same thing as a reference to the Board, which is the decisive point for Matter 4.

questions.category: SQC 1 - Review Mechanisms - QRB and NFRA
questions.question: A student wrote in an answer script: "Three review mechanisms operate over the work of members. The Peer Review Board, constituted by the ICAI Council, examines the systems and procedures put in place by a practice unit to ensure the quality of assurance services as per technical, professional and ethical standards, and its objective is to ensure that in carrying out assurance assignments those standards are complied with by members of ICAI. The Quality Review Board, set up by the Central Government and consisting of members nominated by the Central Government and the ICAI Council, makes recommendations to the Council on quality, reviews the quality of services provided by members and guides members to improve quality. NFRA, constituted under Section 132(1) of the Companies Act, 2013, enforces compliance with standards and oversees the quality of service or undertakes investigation of auditors of certain companies such as listed, insurance and banking companies. It follows that where a member audits a listed company, the Quality Review Board and NFRA both review the quality of that member's services, and NFRA's review is excluded." Which parts of this answer are incorrect?
options: The description of the Peer Review Board and of what peer review examines in the practice unit of a member of ICAI.
The description of the three functions performed by the Quality Review Board.
The final statements, which assume that both the Board and NFRA review the quality of a listed company audit.
The statement that NFRA has been constituted in terms of Section 132(1) of the Companies Act, 2013.
The statement that peer review examines the systems and procedures put in place by a practice unit.
questions.explanation: The three descriptive paragraphs are accurate, including the constitution, composition and three functions of the Quality Review Board and the statutory basis and stated powers of NFRA. The error is in the conclusion drawn from them. Entities specified under NFRA are outside the jurisdiction of the Quality Review Board, whose remit covers services provided by members other than such entities together with matters referred to it by NFRA, so a listed company audit is not a matter in which the Board reviews quality while NFRA's review is excluded; on the contrary it is NFRA whose powers reach the auditors of listed companies and the Board whose remit does not. Options 4 and 5 single out statements that the source expressly supports, and option 1 and 2 likewise, so none of them identifies the error.

questions.question: Ms. Iyer was designated engagement partner for the audit of Raaga Textiles Limited. She determined that an engagement quality control reviewer had been appointed and discussed the significant matters arising with that reviewer. Before accepting the role she obtained from the firm information identifying a circumstance creating a threat to independence, namely that her brother held a substantial holding in the client, and she eliminated that threat by requiring the shares to be disposed of before she took up the work. She also took charge of monitoring the firm's system of quality control. She gave no message to the engagement team about the importance of quality, the firm's view being that its written manual already covered the point. Which of the following responsibilities was not discharged by her in accordance with SA 220?
options: Her duties regarding an engagement quality control review under engagement performance.
Her three-step duty in relation to independence for the audit.
Leadership responsibility for quality on the audit through actions and appropriate messages to the engagement team.
Her responsibility in relation to acceptance and continuance of client relationships and of audit engagements as listed by SA 220.
Her responsibility relating to the assignment of the audit engagement team.
questions.explanation: The engagement partner's leadership responsibility for quality on audits is discharged through his actions and appropriate messages to the engagement team emphasising the importance to audit quality of complying with professional standards and legal requirements, complying with the firm's quality control policies and procedures, issuing an appropriate auditor's report, the team's ability to raise concerns without fear of reprisals, and the fact that quality is essential. No message at all was given here, and the existence of the firm's written manual does not supply the partner's own actions and messages, so this responsibility was not discharged. The three duties regarding the engagement quality control review were performed, and the independence duty was performed in its three steps of obtaining information from the firm, evaluating the position and taking appropriate action to eliminate the threat. The facts say nothing to show that acceptance and continuance or the assignment of the team was neglected, and in any event the source gives no content for those matters.

questions.question: In the audit of Meridian Cables Limited the engagement partner held a kickoff meeting at which he emphasised performing work that complies with professional standards and legal requirements, complying with the firm's quality control policies and procedures, and the fact that quality is essential in performing audit engagements. He said nothing about the auditor's report and nothing about raising concerns. Subsequently a team member discovered an uncorrected misstatement affecting a related party disclosure and, recalling that a colleague had once been criticised for raising a trivial point, said nothing; the report was issued without that disclosure being dealt with and was signed and dated by the partner. Which conclusion is most appropriate?
options: The partner's messages were sufficient, because the fact that quality is essential covers everything else.
The emphasis on raising concerns without fear of reprisals is what these facts engage, and the messages were also incomplete for want of the emphasis on issuing an appropriate report.
The failure is one of engagement performance rather than of leadership, because a report should not be dated until the engagement quality control review has been completed by that reviewer.
The failure is that of the firm's system of quality control alone, since the reporting of uncorrected misstatements is a firm-wide matter.
There is no failure, because SA 220 lists leadership responsibilities for quality within the firm rather than on audits.
questions.explanation: SA 220 requires the engagement partner's actions and appropriate messages to the engagement team to emphasise five things, of which only three were given here. The emphasis on the engagement team's ability to raise concerns without fear of reprisals is the one that bears directly on the suppressed misstatement, since the team member's reluctance traces to an earlier criticism, and the emphasis on issuing an appropriate auditor's report was also omitted, the more so as the report issued failed to deal with a related party disclosure. Option 3 is wrong because there is nothing in the facts showing that an engagement quality control review was pending when the report was dated, so the engagement performance duty is not the identified failure. Option 5 misreads SA 220, which speaks of leadership responsibilities for quality on audits at the engagement level while leadership within the firm is the corresponding SQC 1 element.

questions.question: Mr. Desai was the engagement partner on three audits and reported as follows on his leadership responsibility for quality on audits. Audit X: he gave all five emphases to the team and dated the report after the engagement quality control review was completed. Audit Y: he gave the emphasis that quality is essential and that work must comply with professional standards and legal requirements, and no more. Audit Z: he gave the emphasis that the team must comply with the firm's quality control policies and procedures, that an appropriate auditor's report must be issued, and that concerns may be raised without fear of reprisals. In which audit was the requirement of SA 220 most completely fulfilled?
options: Audit X only
Audit Y only
Audit Z only
Audits X and Z
Audits Y and Z
questions.explanation: The engagement partner's actions and appropriate messages to the engagement team are required to emphasise five matters: performing work that complies with professional standards and legal requirements, complying with the firm's quality control policies and procedures, issuing an appropriate auditor's report, the engagement team's ability to raise concerns without fear of reprisals, and the fact that quality is essential in performing audit engagements. Audit X is the only one in which all five were conveyed, and the dating there also followed completion of the engagement quality control review. Audit Y conveyed two and Audit Z three, so neither is complete; a partial set of messages fulfils the requirement only in part, which is why the tempting answer of grouping X with Z is wrong. The number of emphases given is the decisive fact.

questions.question: M/s Deepa & Associates was approached for the statutory audit of Triton Structures Limited for FY 2025-26. The firm's client acceptance and continuance file for Triton was still open when the work began, because management had pressed for a fee which the firm's own computation of the work involved did not support. Deepa wrote in her note: 'Acceptance and continuance of client relationships is a matter for the firm under its system of quality control. SA 220 lists six matters for the engagement partner, and its table of additional responsibilities elaborates only leadership responsibilities for quality on audits, ethical requirements and engagement performance. It follows that acceptance and continuance imposes nothing on me as engagement partner.' Separately the managing director asked that Deepa's name not be communicated to those charged with governance, and Deepa treated that request as the principal professional question arising on the engagement. Which conclusion is correct?
options: Her reasoning is correct, because only the three matters elaborated in the table of additional responsibilities place any responsibility on the engagement partner.
Her conclusion fails, because SA 220 describes the engagement partner's responsibilities for acceptance and continuance of client relationships and audit engagements.
Her reasoning fails, because acceptance and continuance on a particular engagement is dealt with by the engagement quality control reviewer once that reviewer has been appointed.
The request about her name is the principal question arising, because SA 220 requires the engagement partner to communicate her identity to those charged with governance.
The unresolved fee discussion is decisive, because SA 220 requires the engagement partner to have fee pressure settled before the audit plan is approved.
questions.explanation: SA 220 is modelled on the lines of SQC 1 and describes the responsibilities of the engagement partner for six matters, the third of which is acceptance and continuance of client relationships and audit engagements; the matter therefore stands among the partner's responsibilities irrespective of whether the table of additional responsibilities elaborates it. The silence of that table is the trap in Deepa's reasoning: the table elaborates leadership responsibilities, ethical requirements and engagement performance, and silence as to the remaining three matters does not convert them into matters in which the engagement partner has no responsibility. The request that her name be withheld from those charged with governance and the unresolved fee pressure are relevant-looking facts which the source does not make decisive, since nothing in it requires the partner to disclose her identity to those charged with governance or to settle fees before the audit plan is approved. Transferring acceptance to the reviewer is also wrong, because the reviewer's stated role in the source concerns the engagement quality control review.

questions.question: CA Ganesan's firm was appointed to carry out a limited review of the interim financial information of Vayu Bearings Limited and, for the same company, the statutory audit of its annual financial statements. In a file note he wrote: 'SA 220 is modelled on the lines of SQC 1, and the firm's system of quality control governs all assurance work of the firm. It follows that the six matters for which SA 220 describes the responsibilities of the engagement partner, including assignment of the audit engagement team and acceptance and continuance of client relationships and audit engagements, apply in the same terms to the review engagement as they do to the audit, so that my leadership messages on the audit need not be given on the review, and my implementation of quality control procedures at the particular audit engagement level is fully covered by the firm's system.' Which evaluation of this note is correct?
options: The note is correct, because a limited review of interim financial information is an audit of financial statements for the purposes of quality control.
The note is correct, because a standard modelled on the lines of another standard carries over that other standard's area of application.
The note is correct as to the six matters but incorrect as to the leadership messages, which are a matter for the firm alone.
The note is incorrect, because SA 220 deals with the auditor's responsibilities regarding quality control procedures for an audit of financial statements.
The note is incorrect, because implementing quality control procedures at engagement level is the function of the firm's monitoring element and not of the engagement partner even on an audit.
questions.explanation: SA 220 deals with the responsibilities of the auditor regarding quality control procedures for an audit of financial statements, and it requires the engagement partner to implement those procedures at the particular audit engagement level with an enumeration expressed in the language of audit engagements, as acceptance and continuance of client relationships and audit engagements, and assignment of the audit engagement team, both show. The statement that SA 220 is modelled on the lines of SQC 1 accounts for the shape of the engagement level framework and does not extend the standard's own subject matter to a review engagement, nor allow the firm's wider coverage of assurance work to be read across into the partner's engagement level duties. The first option is therefore plainly wrong, a review is not an audit of financial statements; the second makes the modelling statement do work it cannot do; the third leaves leadership messages on an audit with the firm alone, which contradicts the partner's own leadership responsibility; and the fifth transfers engagement level implementation to monitoring.

questions.question: On the audit of Harbour Logistics Limited the engagement quality control review was recorded as complete on 9 September 2026, the auditor's report was signed and dated 12 September 2026 and the signed report was released to the company on 15 September 2026. The engagement partner had determined that a reviewer had been appointed for the engagement and had discussed every significant matter arising during the audit with that reviewer. At a partners' meeting he said: 'SA 220 requires my leadership messages to the team to emphasise the importance of issuing an appropriate auditor's report. That is the only requirement which SA 220 places on me about the report, so the timing of the reviewer's work as compared with the date of my report is a question for the firm's system and not for me.' Which conclusion is correct?
options: His statement is incorrect, because SA 220 separately requires him under engagement performance not to date the report until the review is completed, and that duty was observed.
His statement is correct, because the leadership emphasis on issuing an appropriate auditor's report is the whole of what SA 220 requires of him about that report in any circumstances.
His statement is incorrect, because the report should have been dated on 9 September 2026, the date on which the review was completed.
His statement is correct in part, because the duty as to dating arises only where the reviewer and the engagement partner have differed on a significant matter.
His statement is incorrect, because an auditor's report may be released only after it has also been signed by the engagement quality control reviewer.
questions.explanation: SA 220 deals with the auditor's report at two separate points and for different purposes. Under leadership responsibilities for quality on audits, the partner's actions and appropriate messages to the engagement team are to emphasise the importance to audit quality of issuing an appropriate auditor's report, which concerns the appropriateness of what is issued; under engagement performance, the partner is required not to date the auditor's report until the engagement quality control review is completed, which is an independent requirement about the date. The partner's statement collapses the two into one and is therefore incorrect, and on the facts the dating duty was observed, the report being dated 12 September 2026 after the review was recorded complete on 9 September 2026, so nothing required the date to be advanced to 9 September. The source makes the dating duty unconditional, so a difference of view with the reviewer is not a trigger for it, and it nowhere requires the reviewer to sign the auditor's report.
